findings.session_b_note:
The co-occurrence table (Section 5 of the data package) provides definitive quantitative data. The top co-occurrences against R023's OWNER active verses (351 verses):

| Registry | Word | Shared verses |
|---|---|---|
| R103 | love | 196 |
| R111 | mercy | 76 |
| R117 | peace | 37 |
| R059 | faith | 37 |
| R044 | despair | 28 |
| R173 | will | 25 |
| R187 | strength | 24 |
| R197 | authority | 23 |
| R156 | surrender | 21 |
| R121 | praise | 20 |
| R099 | kindness | 20 |
| R043 | desire | 19 |
| R112 | mind | 18 |
| R182 | Soul | 17 |
| R034 | covenant | 17 |
| R073 | guilt | 17 |
| R051 | distress | 16 |
| R057 | evil | 16 |
| R140 | seeking | 15 |
| R004 | anger | 15 |

**The most significant co-occurrence by a substantial margin is love (R103 — 196 shared verses).** This is more than twice the count of the next highest (mercy, 76). The love co-occurrence is so dominant that it constitutes more than half of all active OWNER verses (196/351 = 55.8%). This is not incidental clustering — it signals a deep structural connection between compassion and love that the programme must address in Session D (SD-001, SD-005).

**The mercy co-occurrence (76 shared verses) is the second highest** — consistent with the direct shared vocabulary (XREF terms G1653, G1656, G3628) and the shared anchor verses (Rom 9:15, Jas 5:11, Num 6:25). The compassion-mercy structural boundary is the most urgent distinction question in the programme (SD-009).

**Unexpected high signals:**
- Peace (R117 — 37 verses): higher than might be expected given the apparent conceptual distance. SD-025 raises this connection: the co-occurrence (37 verses) suggests a structural relationship between divine compassion and human peace/surrender that warrants investigation.
- Faith (R059 — 37 verses): SD-022 identifies this: chesed and faith appear together extensively in the Psalter. The structural question is whether faith operates as the receptive capacity by which divine compassion is appropriated.
- Despair (R044 — 28 verses): compassion and despair co-occurring at 28 verses points toward the structural relationship between distress/need and compassion's operation — compassion is most active where despair is most present.
- Will (R173 — 25 verses) and Surrender (R156 — 21 verses): SD-025 flags this cluster; the co-occurrence suggests a covenantal-response pattern: divine compassion calls forth human will-engagement and surrender.
- Anger (R004 — 15 verses): Isa 54:8 anchor verse frames the temporal contrast between anger and chesed/racham. The co-occurrence reflects the structural boundary between compassion and judgment in the divine inner life.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-067-006: T6 as a whole reveals that goodness is structurally one of the most connected characteristics in the programme — both in co-occurrence breadth (top-25 co-occurrence list spanning the full dimensional …
findings.finding_value: T6 as a whole reveals that goodness is structurally one of the most connected characteristics in the programme — both in co-occurrence breadth (top-25 co-occurrence list spanning the full dimensional spectrum), shared anchor density (7 shared anchors including the two highest-density synthesis nodes in the programme: Mic 6:8 and Gal 5:22), and root-level vocabulary sharing across three root families (TOV, AGATHO, CHRESTO) distributed across multiple registries. The structural picture confirms what T1 indicated definitionally: goodness is not a specialist characteristic but one that permeates and connects the whole inner-being landscape. The most significant T6 finding is the dual constitutive relationship (Q&A-152): goodness is simultaneously a constituent of the Spirit-fruit whole (Gal 5:22) and itself constituted by a tri-fold structure (Mic 6:8). This means goodness has both a containing relationship (it is part of something larger — Spirit-formed character) and an internal structure (it contains three orientations — justice, kindness, humility). The boundary distinctions (T6.5) remain the weakest component — all three nearest-neighbour boundaries (love, kindness, generosity) require Session D cross-registry synthesis. The R187 (strength) co-occurrence anomaly at 32 shared verses remains an open question for Session D (SP-067-027).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-021: T3 confirmed that goodness is fundamentally integrating — it engages and aligns every faculty (Q&A-095). T6 confirmed that goodness is centrally connected across the programme's characteristic landsca…
findings.finding_value: T3 confirmed that goodness is fundamentally integrating — it engages and aligns every faculty (Q&A-095). T6 confirmed that goodness is centrally connected across the programme's characteristic landscape — broad co-occurrence, shared anchors at the highest-density synthesis nodes, root-vocabulary sharing across three families. These two findings are structurally related: a characteristic that is internally integrating (T3) is also externally connecting (T6). The Mic 6:8 anchor (T6.6 — shared with 6 registries) integrates justice, kindness, love, humility, compassion, and will in a single verse — this is the structural expression of goodness's integrating faculty-engagement. Gal 5:22 (shared with 5 registries) integrates Spirit-fruit characteristics in a cluster — the same integrating logic. The characteristic that most fully integrates the inner faculties (T3) is also the characteristic most structurally connected to adjacent characteristics (T6). Integration within produces connection without.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-026: T5 confirmed that goodness plays a dual developmental role — formation product and formation agent (Q&A-136). T6 confirmed that the characteristics most closely connected to goodness in co-occurrence …
findings.finding_value: T5 confirmed that goodness plays a dual developmental role — formation product and formation agent (Q&A-136). T6 confirmed that the characteristics most closely connected to goodness in co-occurrence and shared anchors are the same characteristics named in the transformation arcs. The Gal 5:22 shared anchors (love, joy, patience, peace, faith) are the characteristics that co-occur in the context of Spirit-produced formation (the fruit list). The Mic 6:8 shared anchors (justice, kindness, love, humility) are the characteristics that are co-constituted with goodness in the definition of the formed human moral life. The cross-registry connections (T6) are the structural record of what characteristics goodness produces in others when it acts as a formation agent (T5). R103 (love) as the highest co-occurrence connection (T6.1 — 28 shared verses) is also the characteristic most naturally produced by encounter with goodness in the positive transformation arc — goodness → trust and love as natural co-products. T5's formation-agent role has T6's cross-registry connections as its structural trace in the programme.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-006: Love's structural position in the programme is that of the central node in the inner-being vocabulary's relational architecture. Co-occurrence data: 196 with compassion, 105 with strength, 68 with pea…
findings.finding_value: Love's structural position in the programme is that of the central node in the inner-being vocabulary's relational architecture. Co-occurrence data: 196 with compassion, 105 with strength, 68 with peace, 62 with faith — confirming love's connections to the full range of C17 characteristics and extending to C20 (strength/authority). Shared anchor data: 48 verses shared across multiple registries, with Exo 34:6 (5 registries) and Gal 5:22 (5 registries) as the highest-density shared anchors — confirming love as the vocabulary cluster around which the programme's most significant cross-registry verses gather. Sequential position: love stands downstream of divine action (received) and upstream of the ethical-moral life (generative of commandment-keeping, Spirit-fruits, community identity). Causal productivity: love generates joy, rest, grief, obedience, praise — the programme's most causally productive characteristic. Vocabulary sharing: term sharing ratio 0.701, the highest in C17 — love shares vocabulary with compassion, mercy, kindness, goodness, desire, and peace. The primary gap: distinctions from adjacent characteristics (compassion, mercy, kindness) remain partially drawn; Session D is the resolution context.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-005: Love's definition as the programme's most semantically comprehensive inner-being characteristic is confirmed and deepened by the structural relationship analysis. The term sharing ratio (0.701 — highe…
findings.finding_value: Love's definition as the programme's most semantically comprehensive inner-being characteristic is confirmed and deepened by the structural relationship analysis. The term sharing ratio (0.701 — highest in C17) and the co-occurrence breadth (196 with compassion through to 29 with mercy) reflect the definition's conclusion: love is not a bounded standalone characteristic but the semantic centre of a cluster. The sequential finding (love as mediating-and-generative node — Q&A-105) maps onto the definition's tripartite structure: love is downstream (condition-received from God), central (disposition that organises), and upstream (act that generates all subsequent ethical life). The definition's vocabulary arc (from divine being to love of darkness — Q&A-131) is confirmed by the structural relationship data: the vocabulary extends into every adjacent registry (through XREF sharing, co-occurrence, and shared anchors), touching every corner of the programme. The structural analysis thus confirms the definitional claim: love is not merely a characteristic among others but the organising principle of the inner-being vocabulary.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-010: Love's comprehensive constitutional location (all five levels) is structurally consistent with its position as the programme's central co-occurrence node. A characteristic that operates at every const…
findings.finding_value: Love's comprehensive constitutional location (all five levels) is structurally consistent with its position as the programme's central co-occurrence node. A characteristic that operates at every constitutional level will co-occur with the broadest range of other characteristics — because any verse that names soul, heart, mind, spirit, or body is potentially within love's evidential terrain. The co-occurrence breadth (top 25 covering registries from C17 through C20 and beyond) reflects the constitutional breadth: strength and authority (C20) co-occur with love because the same verses that address God's inner character include both love and power vocabulary — the divine portrait (Exo 34:6) is constitutionally comprehensive. The vocabulary sharing ratio (0.701 — highest in C17) similarly reflects the constitutional comprehensiveness: love shares vocabulary with compassion (at the somatic/racham level), with goodness (at the heart/tov level), with desire (at the ahav/phileō root level), with peace (at the soul-rest level). Constitutional breadth and vocabulary breadth are the same phenomenon viewed from different angles.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-014: The faculty engagement breadth in T3 is consistent with love's structural position as the programme's central sequential node in T6. A characteristic that engages all eleven faculties will necessarily…
findings.finding_value: The faculty engagement breadth in T3 is consistent with love's structural position as the programme's central sequential node in T6. A characteristic that engages all eleven faculties will necessarily stand at the intersection of the programme's full inner-being vocabulary — because any characteristic that engages one faculty will co-occur with love insofar as love also engages that faculty. The memory-faculty engagement explains part of the co-occurrence with despair (R044 — 55 shared verses): lament appeals to the memory of God's love (Lam 3:22) as its ground. The identity-faculty engagement explains the co-occurrence with calling (R019 — 51 shared): identity-as-beloved and identity-as-called are grammatically co-ordinate (Rom 1:7). The moral-sensitivity engagement explains co-occurrence with guilt (R073 — 32 shared): moral sensitivity calibrated by love recognises guilt as the state that precedes the forgiveness that generates love (Luk 7:47). Faculty engagement and structural relationships thus form a coherent explanatory system: the faculty profile generates the co-occurrence pattern.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-017: The three relational axes in T4 generate the structural relationship pattern in T6. The GOD→HUMAN axis explains love's highest co-occurrences with the programme's theological vocabulary: calling (R019…
findings.finding_value: The three relational axes in T4 generate the structural relationship pattern in T6. The GOD→HUMAN axis explains love's highest co-occurrences with the programme's theological vocabulary: calling (R019 — 51 shared, identity-as-beloved and identity-as-called), faith (R059 — 62 shared, the inner condition for receiving divine love), and compassion (R023 — 196 shared, the compassionate-responsive mode of divine love). The HUMAN→HUMAN axis explains the co-occurrence with peace (R117 — 68 shared, peacemaking as love's horizontal expression) and community-related vocabulary. The sequential structure (divine love prior → human love responsive → ethical life) explains love's mediating position (Q&A-105): it stands between the GOD→HUMAN axis and the HUMAN→HUMAN axis as the transmission point. Love received from God becomes love given to neighbour — the sequential position is the relational interface described structurally. The 48 shared anchor verses are the evidential sites where these relational intersections are most visible: Exo 34:6 (GOD→HUMAN axis at maximum density), Gal 5:22 (HUMAN→HUMAN axis generated by Spirit), Joh 13:34 (HUMAN→HUMAN axis constituted by GOD→HUMAN love as model).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-019: The formation process and the structural relationships are mutually reinforcing systems. The formation pathway (divine love received → Spirit infusion → soul purification → community expression) maps …
findings.finding_value: The formation process and the structural relationships are mutually reinforcing systems. The formation pathway (divine love received → Spirit infusion → soul purification → community expression) maps onto the sequential structural position: love's formation follows the same sequence as love's structural position in the programme — first received (downstream of divine action), then formed (mediating), then expressed (generative of ethical life). The growth-capacity of love (1Th 3:12 — Q&A-092) explains the programme's most puzzling co-occurrence finding: strength and authority (C20, 105 and 69 shared verses respectively). Love growing under the Lord's enabling encounters contexts of power — covenantal love among the people of God is exercised within structures of authority, governance, and strength. The love-power co-occurrence reflects the formation context: love formed within communities is formed within structures of authority. The eschatological trajectory (toward perfect love and direct knowledge) describes the structural relationships' completion: when love reaches its eschatological form, the partial sequential relationships (love received → love given → ethical life) are resolved into the direct love-knowledge of the new covenant (Jer 31:34).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-021: The structural relationship data and the evidential foundation are the most mutually confirming pair in the synthesis matrix. The co-occurrence breadth (T6.1) is directly explained by the vocabulary b…
findings.finding_value: The structural relationship data and the evidential foundation are the most mutually confirming pair in the synthesis matrix. The co-occurrence breadth (T6.1) is directly explained by the vocabulary breadth (T7.1.10 — the widest semantic arc in the programme): a vocabulary that spans from divine being to love of darkness will co-occur with every other inner-being characteristic because it occupies every register of the inner-being vocabulary. The shared anchor density (48 verses — T6.6) is explained by the primary anchor's function (Lam 3:22 — T7.2.5/T7.2.6): the programme anchors the most significant cross-registry verses at love because love is the definitional centre from which adjacent characteristics derive their meaning. The vocabulary sharing ratio (0.701 — T6.4) is explained by the root-level connections (T7.1.2): the racham root connects love, compassion, and mercy; the ahav root connects love and desire; the tov root connects love and goodness. The structural relationship data is, at its core, the observable programme-level effect of the lexical architecture that the evidential foundation analysis reveals. Structural breadth and lexical breadth are the same reality at different levels of analysis.

findings.finding_value: Reading T6 as a whole reveals mercy as structurally integrative — its cross-registry position is not peripheral but central. The T6 synthesis: (a) co-occurrence positions mercy as a hub between the guilt-facing pole (R073 guilt at 75) and the grace-giving pole (R023 compassion at 76) and the power cluster (R187, R196, R197, R198); (b) mercy appears consistently in the middle of inner-being sequences as the bridge from negative condition to positive outcome (Q&A-149); (c) mercy is produced by love and compassion and produces forgiveness, joy, shame, identity, comfort; (d) mercy has constituent status within wisdom (Jam 3:17) and has constituent elements within itself (atonement as mechanism, compassion as motivation, holiness as relational frame); (e) the vocabulary root architecture is theologically coherent (Q&A-157), each root family tracing the full arc of the mercy-event; (f) 16 shared anchor verses confirm mercy's appearance at the intersection of multiple analytical domains (Q&A-165); (g) boundaries with compassion and lovingkindness are partially drawn but require Session D. The T6 synthesis: mercy functions as the structural integrator of the inner-being relational economy — it is the characteristic through which negative conditions are bridged to positive states across the widest range of cross-registry connections in C17.

findings.finding_value: T6 as a whole positions contrition within the inner-being landscape as a convergence characteristic with multiple structural connections. The co-occurrence pattern places contrition at the nexus of heart (R183), fear (R061), pride (R123), sorrow (R151), and fellowship (R062) — all meeting in contrition's primary anchor verses. The causal structure is rich: contrition is causally produced by divine-human encounter; it causally produces divine nearness; it is constitutive of genuine repentance (R135). The vocabulary is sufficiently distinctive (dkh/ktt/nkh root families) that contrition maintains lexical identity even amid these structural connections. The shared anchor analysis confirms Isa 57:15 as the convergence verse — simultaneously registering in divine identity, human moral failure, and creaturely posture registers. T6 synthesis: contrition is a structurally central characteristic that connects multiple inner-being registers (dependence, fear, pride, heart, sorrow, fellowship) while maintaining a distinctive vocabulary and position as the penitential sub-form of creaturely dependence before God.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-062-006: T6 positions fellowship as a structurally central hub characteristic — it connects desire (R43 — strongest co-occurrence signal), unity (R167 — corporate outcome), spirit (R184 — mediating agent), com…
findings.finding_value: T6 positions fellowship as a structurally central hub characteristic — it connects desire (R43 — strongest co-occurrence signal), unity (R167 — corporate outcome), spirit (R184 — mediating agent), comfort (R192 — affective product of shared suffering), contrition and sorrow (R30, R151 — shared anchor Isa 53:5), yielding (R180 — shared anchor 2Pe 1:4), covenant (R34 — shared anchor Mal 2:14). Fellowship is structurally upstream of unity (fellowship is the participatory inner reality; unity is its corporate structural expression) and downstream of desire (desire directs fellowship). The vocabulary analysis (T6.4) reveals the root-level connection between wound and companionship (both from chavar) as the deepest structural finding: fellowship and suffering-wounding share the same etymological root, revealing that the deepest fellowship is structurally connected to the deepest wounding.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-012: T1's five-mode structure explains T6's co-occurrence pattern. The desire-R43 co-occurrence (6 shared verses — strongest signal) reflects T1's finding that desire is the internal motivating state direc…

The unity-R167 co-occurrence reflects T1's finding that fellowship is the participatory inner reality of which unity is the corporate outcome — they co-occur because fellowship produces unity. The structural connections in T6 are the cross-registry expression of T1's definitional relationships.

T2's somatic location (H2250 wound — body) explains the cross-registry connections to R30 contrition and R151 sorrow at Isa 53:5 — all three characteristics meet at the somatic-constitutional level in that verse.

findings.finding_value: T3's moral evaluation and conscience faculty engagements explain the co-occurrence pattern with desire (R43) in T6. Desire (R43) directs fellowship; conscience assesses the moral quality of the fellowship object; moral evaluation confirms or challenges the direction. The three characteristics (desire, fellowship, conscience) operate in sequence: desire directs → conscience evaluates → fellowship forms. The T6 co-occurrence signal between R43 and R062 is the shared-verse evidence of this sequential relationship that T3's faculty analysis illuminates.

The God-to-human direction (T4.1 — divine initiative) corresponds to the R180 yielding connection (T6 — shared anchor 2Pe 1:4): the divine initiative at 2Pe 1:4 requires an inner human yielding (escape from corruption) as its receiving condition. The human-to-human giving direction (T4.3 — companionship, covenant, comfort-sharing) corresponds to the R34 covenant, R192 comfort, and R43 desire connections in T6. The relational directions (T4) and the structural cross-registry connections (T6) are the inner-being and cross-registry expressions of the same relational movements.

findings.finding_value: T5's formation mechanisms (participatory transfer and wound-as-cleansing) explain why fellowship is structurally connected in T6 to both desire (R43 — participatory-transfer mechanism begins with desire-directed alignment) and to contrition/sorrow (R30, R151 — wound-as-cleansing mechanism meets contrition and sorrow at Isa 53:5). T5's two formation mechanisms generate two distinct clusters of T6 structural connections: the habitual-alignment cluster (R43 desire, R167 unity, R34 covenant) and the suffering-cleansing cluster (R30 contrition, R151 sorrow, R192 comfort). Formation mechanism determines structural cluster.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-064-006: T6 reveals forgiveness as a structural hub in the C17 and broader programme network. The guilt-073 connection (51 shared verses — dominant) positions forgiveness as the definitional counterpart and re…
findings.finding_value: T6 reveals forgiveness as a structural hub in the C17 and broader programme network. The guilt-073 connection (51 shared verses — dominant) positions forgiveness as the definitional counterpart and remedy to guilt. The mercy-111 connection (15 shared) positions mercy as the generating disposition for forgiving. The love-103 connection (8 shared) confirms the downstream love-production as a recurring structural signal. Jer 31:34 as the highest-convergence anchor (shared with guilt, love, thought) is analytically significant for Session D. The lexical analysis (T6.4) reveals salach's lexical isolation — no root-sharing — which structurally preserves the divine-exclusive domain of forgiveness at its deepest Hebrew root. The distinctions analysis positions: guilt as the condition forgiveness addresses (kind distinction), mercy as the disposition that generates forgiving (layer distinction), reconciliation as the restored state that forgiveness makes possible (sequence distinction). T6 synthesis: forgiveness is a structural hub whose connections are definitionally structured — every major co-occurrence corresponds to a logical role in the forgiveness transaction (guilt = prior condition; mercy = divine disposition; repentance = access-posture; love = downstream product; faith = receiving instrument; reconciliation = restored outcome).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-012: T1's definitional structure explains T6's co-occurrence pattern with precision. Guilt-073 (51 shared verses) is the definitional counterpart (T1 — forgiveness releases guilt; they are structurally ins…
findings.finding_value: T1's definitional structure explains T6's co-occurrence pattern with precision. Guilt-073 (51 shared verses) is the definitional counterpart (T1 — forgiveness releases guilt; they are structurally inseparable). Mercy-111 (15 shared) is the generating disposition (T1 — God's mercy is what produces the forgiving act). Repentance-135 (12 shared) is the access-posture (T1 — human side receiving condition). Love-103 (8 shared) is the named downstream state (T1 — Luk 7:47). Faith-059 (9 shared) is the receiving instrument (T1). Every major co-occurrence registry corresponds to a logical role in T1's definitional structure. T6's co-occurrence data is therefore a reading of the complete forgiveness transaction from the outside — each co-registry names one element of the transaction that T1 defines from the inside.

Constitutional location and co-occurrence signals are mutually confirming: every major constitutional locus of forgiveness corresponds to a co-occurrence registry that operates in the same constitutional space.

findings.finding_value: T3's memory faculty finding (Jer 31:34 — divine "remember no more") explains the R160 thought/knowledge co-occurrence at that verse: the divine cognitive act of non-remembering and the human cognitive outcome of knowing God meet in the same verse because they are structurally connected — the guilt-barrier's removal (forgiveness) enables the cognitive-relational access (knowing God). T3's affect-faculty finding (love produced — Luk 7:47) explains the R103 love co-occurrence (8 shared verses) — love is the affective downstream product of forgiveness. T3's conscience faculty finding confirms the R073 guilt structural partnership — guilt is what conscience identifies as the prior condition that forgiveness addresses. Faculty engagements (T3) and structural co-occurrences (T6) are mutually explanatory.

findings.finding_value: T4's relational directions correspond to T6's structural connections. The God-to-human direction (T4.1) corresponds to the mercy-111 connection (mercy as the divine disposition generating the act, operating in the same direction). The human-to-God direction (T4.2) corresponds to the repentance-135 and faith-059 connections (the access-postures that operate in the seeking direction). The horizontal giving-direction (T4.3) corresponds to the love-103 connection (love as the upstream motivator of horizontal forgiveness — Eph 4:32) and the reconciliation-130 connection (Mat 5:24 — reconciliation as the restored state that horizontal forgiveness produces). T4's relational architecture and T6's co-occurrence network are different analytical lenses on the same structural reality.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-026: T5's formation sequence (forgiveness received → love → capacity to extend) explains why T6 finds love-103 as a co-occurrence signal (8 shared verses) — love is the formation product most visibly evide…
findings.finding_value: T5's formation sequence (forgiveness received → love → capacity to extend) explains why T6 finds love-103 as a co-occurrence signal (8 shared verses) — love is the formation product most visibly evidenced in the co-occurrence data. T5's two mechanisms (declaratory and atoning) explain the guilt-073 co-occurrence dominance (51 shared verses) — guilt is the condition both mechanisms address, and so it co-occurs across the entire forgiveness corpus. T5's sanctification-formation dimension (T5.5 — Eph 4:32) explains the reconciliation-130 shared anchor (Mat 5:24): the commanded forgiveness in the formation context is structurally connected to the restored relational state (reconciliation) as the goal of the horizontal act. T5's formation mechanisms generate T6's structural connections.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-028: T6's structural connections and T7's vocabulary analysis confirm and explain each other. The salach root's lexical isolation (T6.4 — no root-sharing with other programme registries; T7.1.1 — no XREF t…
findings.finding_value: T6's structural connections and T7's vocabulary analysis confirm and explain each other. The salach root's lexical isolation (T6.4 — no root-sharing with other programme registries; T7.1.1 — no XREF terms) reveals that forgiveness maintains a lexically distinct divine-exclusive domain — the strongest co-occurrence registry (guilt-073 at 51 shared verses) operates in the same semantic territory but at the verse level, not at the root-sharing level. This means the structural partnership between forgiveness and guilt is relational-definitional, not lexical-etymological. The Jer 31:34 multi-registry convergence (T6.6 — shared with guilt, love, thought) is also T7's most analytically rich verse (T7.2.5 — the primary anchor trio includes Jer 31:34): the verse that carries the most structural connections is the verse that is exegetically richest, confirmed from both directions.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-006: T6 reveals compassion as the structural centre of the C17 cluster rather than a peripheral member. The love co-occurrence (196/351 = 55.8% of all OWNER verses) is uniquely dominant — compassion and lo…
findings.finding_value: T6 reveals compassion as the structural centre of the C17 cluster rather than a peripheral member. The love co-occurrence (196/351 = 55.8% of all OWNER verses) is uniquely dominant — compassion and love co-occur in more than half of all active verses, raising the programme-level question whether they are truly separable at the data level. Three structural observations from the co-occurrence landscape: (1) compassion sits at C17's centre of gravity (love, mercy, kindness as top three co-occurrences — all within-cluster); (2) compassion generates a human-response cluster (peace, faith, will, surrender, seeking co-occurring at significant levels — the pattern of divine compassion generating human inner-being responses); (3) compassion is constitutively responsive to human distress (despair, guilt, distress, evil all present in the co-occurrence table — compassion operates most characteristically in the presence of need). The CHASAD root crossing compassion (C17) and shame (C06) is the programme's most structurally unexpected finding — a root family that bridges two clusters. Exod 34:6 as the programme's most multiply-anchored verse (6 registries) must be treated as a cluster-level synthesis anchor. The compassion/mercy boundary (SD-009) is the most critical unresolved distinction. T6.7 (dimensional sharing) is programme-stage limited — formally deferred.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-012: T1's primary dimension (Relational Disposition) and T6's co-occurrence landscape are mutually confirming. The love co-occurrence dominance (196 verses) is the co-occurrence expression of T1's relation…
findings.finding_value: T1's primary dimension (Relational Disposition) and T6's co-occurrence landscape are mutually confirming. The love co-occurrence dominance (196 verses) is the co-occurrence expression of T1's relational-disposition classification: love and compassion co-occur at this extraordinary rate because they share the relational-disposition register. T1's finding that compassion is constitutively outward-facing explains why the co-occurrence landscape shows the C17 cluster (love, mercy, kindness) as the primary co-occurrence family. T6's unresolved compassion/mercy distinction (SD-009) is the most critical consequence of T1's definitional incompleteness — the boundary between compassion and mercy as adjacent Relational Disposition characteristics is the definitional question T1 cannot answer without T6 data.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-017: T2's somatic-constitutional location explains several T6 structural connections. The shared anchor at Isa 53:5 (with R030 contrition) confirms that the somatic wound vocabulary intersects both compass…
findings.finding_value: T2's somatic-constitutional location explains several T6 structural connections. The shared anchor at Isa 53:5 (with R030 contrition) confirms that the somatic wound vocabulary intersects both compassion and contrition at the constitutional-somatic level — both characteristics have somatic-body language as part of their evidential ground. The CHASAD root's crossing of compassion and shame clusters (T6.4 — most unexpected structural finding) is partly explainable from T2: if CHASAD names a covenantal-soul disposition, it can operate in both the positive register (chesed — steadfast love/compassion) and the negative register (bōsheth — shame as the opposite soul-condition of exposed vulnerability). T2's constitutional portrait (soul-body interface) is the constitutional ground for the root-level cluster-crossing that T6 identifies.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-021: T3's finding that compassion is the motivational ground of conscientiousness explains the co-occurrence pattern in T6. Conscience (T3.9) and moral evaluation (T3.8) are the faculties that register the…
findings.finding_value: T3's finding that compassion is the motivational ground of conscientiousness explains the co-occurrence pattern in T6. Conscience (T3.9) and moral evaluation (T3.8) are the faculties that register the pitiable need as a moral claim; compassion is the affective-motivational response that converts that moral knowledge into action. The co-occurrence of will (R173 — 25 verses) and surrender (R156 — 21 verses) in T6 is the co-occurrence expression of T3's volitional faculty finding: compassion engages and redirects the will toward the suffering other. The sequential relationship confirmed in T6 (compassion → mercy — constitutionally causal) is the relational expression of T3's finding that compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action: the mercy-act is the action that compassion's motivation produces.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-024: T4's scope-by-need finding (compassion crosses covenantal boundaries) and T6's co-occurrence landscape (the human-response cluster — peace, faith, will, surrender — co-occurring with compassion) revea…
findings.finding_value: T4's scope-by-need finding (compassion crosses covenantal boundaries) and T6's co-occurrence landscape (the human-response cluster — peace, faith, will, surrender — co-occurring with compassion) reveal a structural pattern: divine compassion reaching across boundaries generates a characteristic cluster of human inner-being responses regardless of the covenantal position of the recipient. The Nineveh response (repentance and turning) and the pattern of peace/faith/will/surrender co-occurring with compassion both confirm this: compassion-received generates a recognisable inner-being response cluster that is structurally consistent across relational positions. T6's mapping of the human-response cluster is the co-occurrence evidence for T4's structural finding about scope and response.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-026: T5's three mechanisms of change explain the structural pattern visible in T6's co-occurrence landscape. The encounter/sudden mechanism (splanchnizō producing immediate transformation) corresponds to t…
findings.finding_value: T5's three mechanisms of change explain the structural pattern visible in T6's co-occurrence landscape. The encounter/sudden mechanism (splanchnizō producing immediate transformation) corresponds to the high co-occurrence with despair (28 verses) and distress (16 verses) — these are the conditions that trigger the sudden compassion-event. The covenantal-sustaining mechanism corresponds to the high co-occurrence with love (196 verses), mercy (76 verses), and covenant (17 verses) — these are the characteristics that share the sustaining, gradual register with chesed. The participatory-ontological mechanism corresponds to the sequential relationship (compassion → mercy confirmed as constitutionally causal in T6.2) — the deepest formation mechanism produces the person who naturally extends mercy as the externalised form of the compassion-character formed within. Formation mechanisms (T5) explain co-occurrence patterns (T6).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-028: T6's structural connections and T7's vocabulary analysis are mutually confirming at the most analytically significant points. The CHASAD root crossing two clusters (T6.4 — most unexpected structural f…
findings.finding_value: T6's structural connections and T7's vocabulary analysis are mutually confirming at the most analytically significant points. The CHASAD root crossing two clusters (T6.4 — most unexpected structural finding) is confirmed and extended by T7's vocabulary analysis: the CHASAD root includes shame as the negative semantic pole embedded within the root itself (T7.1 P5), not as an external antonym. This means the cluster-crossing T6 identifies is not an external structural anomaly but an internal semantic feature: the compassion vocabulary contains its own opposite at the root level. Exod 34:6 as the programme's most multiply-anchored verse (T6.6 — 6 registries) is also T7's most evidentially rich single text — the verse that carries the most structural connections is the same verse that is most analytically central to the vocabulary analysis. The love co-occurrence dominance (T6.1 — 196/351 verses) is confirmed by T7's vocabulary arc: the vocabulary's fullest range (womb to almsgiving) overlaps extensively with the love vocabulary's range, which is why they co-occur across more than half of all active verses.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-006: T6 produces the most structurally significant finding in the review set for any single tier: grace is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic. It is the originating point of a causal chai…
findings.finding_value: T6 produces the most structurally significant finding in the review set for any single tier: grace is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic. It is the originating point of a causal chain, not its product. This categorically distinguishes grace from every other characteristic reviewed — all others can be produced by at least one other characteristic; grace cannot. This structural uniqueness is confirmed by T2.9's origin analysis (grace originates with God — it does not originate in the human constitutional system) and is analytically consistent across T6.2 (seeking is the posture before grace arrives, not its producer), T6.3 (S-rating on "is grace produced by another characteristic"), and T6.4 (the vocabulary's structural completeness without a generative human-side term). The co-occurrence pattern reveals grace at the intersection of divine initiative and creaturely need: seeking (R140 — 40 verses, dominant) as the creature's pre-grace posture; moral failure cluster (evil, guilt, sin, transgression) as the creaturely context; power cluster (strength, might) confirming the 2Cor 12:9 connection. The love co-occurrence (R103 — 14 verses) is the primary within-cluster signal raising the grace-love boundary question (SD013). All major boundary distinctions (grace-love, grace-mercy, grace-justice, grace-chesed) remain open at T6.5 — the most unresolved boundary cluster in the review set. T6.7 (dimensional sharing) is programme-stage limited.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-012: T1's dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) and T6's co-occurrence pattern are mutually confirming. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is the co-occurrence ex…
findings.finding_value: T1's dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) and T6's co-occurrence pattern are mutually confirming. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is the co-occurrence expression of T1's finding that grace requires the receptor's inner posture of appeal: seeking is the relational posture before grace arrives, and the vocabulary encodes this (tachanum — built into the same root as chen). T6's structural uniqueness finding (grace is not produced by any other characteristic) is T1's definitional consequence: because grace is constitutively the uncaused inclination of the greater toward the lesser, it cannot be produced by anything in the lesser's constitutional system. T1's definition predicts T6's structural uniqueness.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-021: T3's faculty findings explain several patterns in T6's co-occurrence landscape. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is partly explained by T3.6's agency-constituting finding: seekin…
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty findings explain several patterns in T6's co-occurrence landscape. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is partly explained by T3.6's agency-constituting finding: seeking requires the constituted agency that grace provides for its own reception (SD026 — grace giving the capacity for supplication). The power cluster co-occurrences (strength R187 — 15 verses, might R198 — 10 verses) confirm T3.7's agency-constituting finding at the cross-registry level: grace producing agency is registered as co-occurring with power/strength across the corpus. T3.8's moral clarity finding explains the guilt co-occurrence (R073 — 10 verses): the moral clarity grace produces is most visible at the point of moral failure, and the co-occurrence reflects this — grace and guilt appear together because grace produces the moral clarity that accurately names the guilt it addresses.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-024: T4's relational architecture and T6's co-occurrence network express the same structural reality from relational and cross-registry perspectives. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (T6 — R140, 40 vers…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational architecture and T6's co-occurrence network express the same structural reality from relational and cross-registry perspectives. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (T6 — R140, 40 verses) is the co-occurrence expression of T4.2 (the human-to-God supplication direction): seeking is the relational posture, and R140 is the registry that names it. The sequential relationship confirmed in T6.2 (grace precedes and enables faith, repentance, supplication, mourning — SD003, SD006, SD026, SD038) is the causal expression of T4's architectural finding: grace is the enabling condition for every positive human-to-God relational posture. The boundary questions in T6.5 (grace-love, grace-mercy, grace-chesed) correspond to T4.5's scope analysis: the characteristics that share grace's scope (particularly love and mercy) are the same characteristics whose relational scope overlaps with grace's at T4.5.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-026: T5's five formation mechanisms explain the structural pattern visible in T6's co-occurrence and sequential landscape. The encounter mechanism (sudden grace-event) corresponds to the sequences confirme…
findings.finding_value: T5's five formation mechanisms explain the structural pattern visible in T6's co-occurrence and sequential landscape. The encounter mechanism (sudden grace-event) corresponds to the sequences confirmed in T6.2 (grace precedes and causes the immediate responses of mourning, fear, supplication — SD038, SD026). The word mechanism (Act 20:32) corresponds to the faith co-occurrence (R059 — 10 verses): the proclaimed word that carries grace produces faith as its response. The inference mechanism (Rom 8:32 — assurance derived by reasoning) corresponds to the hope and peace co-occurrences (R117 — 10 verses): reasoned assurance from grace produces the inner peace and hope co-occurring registries name. The mediated-transformation mechanism (tenderheartedness → forgiving) produces the love co-occurrence (R103 — 14 verses) as tenderheartedness is the inner precondition of the forgiving that love and grace share. T5's mechanisms generate T6's structural connections.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-099-006: T6 reveals that kindness sits at the structural centre of a dense network of related characteristics rather than on the edge. Its most consistent co-occurrences (faithfulness, justice, compassion, for…
findings.finding_value: T6 reveals that kindness sits at the structural centre of a dense network of related characteristics rather than on the edge. Its most consistent co-occurrences (faithfulness, justice, compassion, forgiveness, humility, patience) are not merely adjacent virtues but appear to be partially constituent of kindness itself — the Mic 6:8 triad (justice/kindness/humility) and the Eph 4:32 cluster (kindness/tenderheartedness/forgiveness) function as composite wholes where each element reinforces and partly defines the others. The causal network is explicit and directional: divine kindness → praise + repentance in the recipient → reproduced human kindness toward others → sustained covenant relationships. This causal chain means kindness is not only a characteristic that one possesses but one that is structurally self-propagating through its own operation. The semantic-root finding is analytically significant: the CHESED root family spans the noun (chesed — kindness), the verb (chasad — be kind), the person (chasid — the kind one), the negative (shame/reproach for its failure), and a proper name (Chesed) — a root family that covers definition, action, identity, consequence, and proper-noun instantiation within a single family. T6's most significant intra-tier finding: Mic 6:8 anchors eight registries simultaneously, which confirms that kindness is not a standalone quality but a node in a structural web of C17 cluster characteristics — its full meaning requires these other registries to be seen.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-012: T1's finding that kindness is composite — constituted by faithfulness, justice, compassion, forgiveness — is confirmed and extended by T6's co-occurrence data. The T6 finding that kindness consistentl…
findings.finding_value: T1's finding that kindness is composite — constituted by faithfulness, justice, compassion, forgiveness — is confirmed and extended by T6's co-occurrence data. The T6 finding that kindness consistently co-occurs with faithfulness (Reg 60), justice (Reg 98), love (Reg 103), and compassion (Reg 23) is not merely a co-occurrence pattern but reflects the T1 structural composition: these co-occurring characteristics are partially internal to kindness itself, not merely adjacent to it. This has a significant implication: kindness cannot be fully studied within a single registry — it requires the cluster analysis that Session D will provide. The T6 causal network (divine kindness → praise + repentance → reproduced human kindness) is the T1 relational mechanism made explicit at the T6 structural level. The T1 boundary finding (kindness is not love, not compassion, not grace — Q&A-021) is where T6's distinction analysis (Q&A-082) begins and cannot resolve without Session D cross-registry work. The two tiers together reveal the tension: kindness is internally composite in ways that make its boundary with adjacent characteristics difficult to draw precisely.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-017: T2's heart-location finding and T6's structural relationship findings together reveal something about kindness that neither tier alone states: the heart is not only the constitutional site of kindness…
findings.finding_value: T2's heart-location finding and T6's structural relationship findings together reveal something about kindness that neither tier alone states: the heart is not only the constitutional site of kindness but the site where kindness's constituent adjacent characteristics (faithfulness, justice, compassion, forgiveness) are also inscribed. Pro 3:3 — "write them on the tablet of your heart" — names the heart as the inscription site for chesed and emet (faithfulness/truth) together, suggesting that the T6 co-occurrence pattern (kindness + faithfulness as the most persistent pair) has a constitutional basis: they are co-inscribed. This means T6's network of adjacent characteristics is not merely relational or contextual co-occurrence but a constitutional clustering: they share the same constitutional site. The T2 constitutional movement outward (heart → acts) and T6's causal network (kindness → reproduced kindness → sustained covenant relationships) trace the same movement from two angles — T2 names the direction, T6 names the mechanism of propagation.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-021: T3's finding that kindness engages volition, agency, and conscientiousness as an integrated whole maps onto T6's causal network in a specific way: it is precisely these three faculties operating toget…
findings.finding_value: T3's finding that kindness engages volition, agency, and conscientiousness as an integrated whole maps onto T6's causal network in a specific way: it is precisely these three faculties operating together that make the T6 causal chain function. The T6 finding that received human kindness causes its reproduction (2Sa 10:2 — "as his father dealt loyally with me, so I will deal loyally") requires all three: the cognition (knowing what was done), the moral evaluation (recognising the obligation), and the agency (acting on it). The T6 co-occurrence finding that kindness clusters with faithfulness, patience, and humility maps onto T3's multi-faculty profile: faithfulness requires conscientiousness; patience requires impulse-control at the volitional level; humility requires conscience and moral evaluation. The T3 finding that imagination and creativity are absent connects with T6's finding that kindness is a central node in a relational-moral web — it is constitutively oriented toward the actual other, not toward the imagined or created.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-024: T4's relational circuit and T6's structural network overlap most clearly at the causal level. The T6 causal network (divine kindness → praise + repentance → reproduced human kindness → sustained coven…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational circuit and T6's structural network overlap most clearly at the causal level. The T6 causal network (divine kindness → praise + repentance → reproduced human kindness → sustained covenant relationships) is a structural description of the T4 circuit in causal terms: T4 identifies the directions; T6 names the causal mechanism connecting them. The T6 finding that Mic 6:8 anchors eight registries is a cluster-level reflection of T4's circuit: Mic 6:8's triadic requirement (do justice / love kindness / walk humbly) is addressed to the covenant community's relational practice — it describes the T4 relational interface requirements in condensed form. The T6 finding that kindness is self-propagating through the causal chain (received kindness → reproduced kindness) is the structural guarantee that the T4 circuit is not a closed loop requiring constant external input but a self-sustaining relational ecosystem once kindness is received and given. The T4 finding that the spiritual beings interface is absent (Q&A-070) is consistent with T6's causal analysis: the causal chain operates within the human-divine-communal relational web, not across spiritual-ontological boundaries.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-026: T5's formation mechanisms and T6's structural relationships interact at the level of what each characteristic in the co-occurrence cluster contributes to kindness formation. The T6 finding that kindne…
findings.finding_value: T5's formation mechanisms and T6's structural relationships interact at the level of what each characteristic in the co-occurrence cluster contributes to kindness formation. The T6 finding that kindness consistently co-occurs with faithfulness, patience, humility, and compassion maps onto T5's chasid formation arc: each of these co-occurring characteristics is also part of the formation process — faithfulness is what makes the chasid reliable over time (formation dimension); patience is what makes kindness sustainable under provocation (T5 suffering connection); humility is what prevents the chasid's identity from becoming pride (T5 formation outcome that avoids the structural opposite). The T5 formation mechanisms (Spirit-formation, inscription, encounter) all produce not just kindness in isolation but kindness in its relational cluster — the Spirit produces the full fruit (Gal 5:22: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness) not one element at a time. T5's eschatological trajectory (Eph 2:7 — immeasurable future display of kindness in Christ) is the T6 causal chain extended to its ultimate end: the causal propagation of kindness through the covenant community reaches its telos in the eschatological display of divine kindness in Christ.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-028: T6's structural relationship findings and T7's lexical and literary findings are mutually confirming at the level of the semantic root. The T6 finding that the CHESED root family covers noun (chesed),…
findings.finding_value: T6's structural relationship findings and T7's lexical and literary findings are mutually confirming at the level of the semantic root. The T6 finding that the CHESED root family covers noun (chesed), verb (chasad), person (chasid), shame-negative (H2617B), and proper noun (Chesed) is a T7 lexical observation that has structural significance: a root family that spans all these categories is not merely a lexical curiosity but evidence that kindness (as the CHESED root names it) is a comprehensive inner-being reality — it has a noun form (what it is), a verb form (what it does), a person form (who embodies it), a consequence form (what happens when it fails), and a proper-noun instantiation (when it names a person). The T6 co-occurrence finding that kindness clusters with faithfulness, justice, and compassion maps directly onto the T7 semantic range finding that chesed itself encompasses goodness/kindness/faithfulness — the co-occurrence cluster is partly a reflection of the internal semantic complexity of chesed: different registries are studying different dimensions of what is, in the original Hebrew, a single concept. T7's primary anchor verse (Lam 3:22) is T6's most significant causal statement: the inexhaustibility of chesed (T7) is the precondition for the causal chain's stability (T6) — if chesed could run out, the chain would break.

findings.finding_value: T6 establishes peace as a hub characteristic with three primary structural bonds: (1) Trust (R163) — causal precondition: trust → peace (Isa 26:3, Psa 4:8); (2) Covenant (R34) — constitutional ground: the SHA.L root shared at root level; the peace-covenant is grounded in the same completeness-root; (3) Reconciliation (R130) — constitutive mechanism: reconciliation constitutes relational peace (Col 1:20, Eph 2:14). The causal system is reinforcing: trust → peace → strength → more trust. The hub position is confirmed by 25 co-occurring registries (≥3 verses) and 59 shared anchor relationships across 43 registries — the widest cross-registry engagement in C17.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-060-006: T6 as a whole reveals that R060 (faithfulness/na.tan) occupies a connecting-hub structural position in the inner-being landscape. Its five-dimensional breadth (MC, RD, Cognition, Transformation, DHC) …
findings.finding_value: T6 as a whole reveals that R060 (faithfulness/na.tan) occupies a connecting-hub structural position in the inner-being landscape. Its five-dimensional breadth (MC, RD, Cognition, Transformation, DHC) means it shares dimensional territory with virtually every adjacent characteristic. Its co-occurrence breadth (14 registries ≥6 shared verses) and shared-anchor density (12 shared anchors across 9 registries) confirms the hub position empirically. The sequential relationships (giving→worship, suffering→giving, faithlessness→giving-over) show it operating as both a causal initiator and a causal consequence in relation to other characteristics. The aman root architecture reveals that R060, R059, and R044 are conceptually entangled at the root level — the programme's separation is analytical, not lexical. The distinction from nearest neighbours (hesed/R099, love/R103) is of kind — dispositional vs. actional — confirming that R060 holds a distinct structural position as the actional realisation of what the dispositional characteristics name. What T6 reveals as a whole: this characteristic is not isolated in the inner-being landscape; it is a connector through which multiple adjacent characteristics are expressed, related, and developed.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-010: The constitutional pervasiveness of the characteristic (T2 — it reaches every constitutional level through distinct modes) and the hub position it occupies in the structural landscape (T6 — connecting…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional pervasiveness of the characteristic (T2 — it reaches every constitutional level through distinct modes) and the hub position it occupies in the structural landscape (T6 — connecting multiple adjacent characteristics across all five dimensions) are causally related. The characteristic can occupy the hub position precisely because it is constitutionally pervasive: it is not anchored to a single constitutional level that would limit its relational scope. A purely spirit-level characteristic would only relate structurally to other spirit-level characteristics; a purely somatic characteristic would only relate somatically. This characteristic, moving across all levels, can relate structurally to characteristics at every level. What this pair reveals: constitutional breadth enables structural breadth. The connecting-hub position is a structural consequence of the constitutional polymorphism of giving as an inner-being act.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-014: The full-person faculty integration (T3 — all major faculties engaged) and the producing/produced-by structural position (T6) reveal that the characteristic's hub position is sustained by its faculty-…
findings.finding_value: The full-person faculty integration (T3 — all major faculties engaged) and the producing/produced-by structural position (T6) reveal that the characteristic's hub position is sustained by its faculty-integration property. It produces worship (R121, R176) because worship is the proper faculty response to received giving (T3 — perception of divine giving → affect of gratitude → volition of blessing → relational act of worship). It is produced by love (R103) and trust (R059) because love and trust are the inner-being sources from which the giving proceeds (T3 — affect motivates, volition commits, agency enacts). The causal sequences (T6.2) are faculty sequences in disguise: each sequential step is a faculty transition (suffering perceived → compassion moved → giving enacted). What this pair reveals: the structural network of this characteristic in the inner-being landscape is held together by faculty transitions. The characteristic is a hub because it is where multiple faculty-driven causal sequences converge and produce giving as their common expression.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-017: The relational interfaces (T4 — God-to-human primary, human-to-God responsive, covenantal scope) and the structural landscape (T6 — hub position, causal sequences, shared anchors) reveal that R060's h…
findings.finding_value: The relational interfaces (T4 — God-to-human primary, human-to-God responsive, covenantal scope) and the structural landscape (T6 — hub position, causal sequences, shared anchors) reveal that R060's hub position is constituted by its position at the centre of the divine-human relational network. The sequential patterns (T6.2 — giving→worship, suffering→giving, faithlessness→giving-over) are relational sequences: each involves God and the human in the roles described by T4. The shared anchors (T6.6) are high-density precisely because they are relational nodes — Hos 11:8 anchors five registries because it holds the divine inner-being and the human relational situation simultaneously. What this pair reveals: the structural hub position of R060 in the inner-being landscape is a direct consequence of its occupation of the divine-human relational centre. It is a hub because it is where the primary divine-human dynamic (God gives, human receives and responds) is most directly expressed and most extensively connected.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-021: The structural landscape analysis (T6 — hub position, aman root architecture entangling R059/R044/R060, distinction of kind from nearest neighbours) and the vocabulary/methodological analysis (T7 — fu…
findings.finding_value: The structural landscape analysis (T6 — hub position, aman root architecture entangling R059/R044/R060, distinction of kind from nearest neighbours) and the vocabulary/methodological analysis (T7 — full vocabulary arc, grammatically actional, primary anchor Hos 11:8) produce the final convergent finding. The aman root architecture (T6.4.2, Q&A-157) and the vocabulary arc (T7.1.10, Q&A-179) are describing the same reality: the programme's separation of registries by word is an analytical convenience that cuts across a root-level unity. The vocabulary arc — enacted pole (na.tan/verb) + constituted pole (emunah/hesed/pistis/nouns) — names the same reality that the root architecture identifies: the aman root generates both the dispositional terms and the contextual terms, while na.tan provides the enacted verbal expression. The grammatically actional character of na.tan (T7.1.2, Q&A-171) is the structural reason for its distinction-of-kind from the nominal faithfulness vocabulary (T6.5.3, Q&A-162). What this pair reveals as the final synthesis: the vocabulary evidence and the structural landscape evidence independently converge on the same conclusion — this characteristic is the enacted form of what the faithfulness vocabulary names dispositionally, and this distinction is fundamental to understanding both the characteristic itself and its position in the inner-being landscape.

From the span data: **Love (a.ha.vah / H0160)** — the most frequent co-occurring characteristic across M06-A, appearing in 2Sa 13:15, Pro 10:12, Pro 15:17, Psa 109:5, Ecc 9:6, Amo 5:15, Psa 45:7, Psa 119:113, and multiple other verses. **Jealousy/Envy (qin.ah / H7068)** — appears in Ecc 9:6 ("their love and their hate and their envy") and Eze 35:11 ("anger and envy...because of your hatred"). **Iniquity/Sin (a.von, chet)** — in Exo 20:5 (visiting iniquity on those who hate), Lev 19:17 (lest you incur sin because of hatred), Hos 9:7 (great iniquity and great hatred). **Shame (bo.shet)** — in Job 8:22 (those who hate you will be clothed with shame), Psa 44:7, Psa 86:17 — shame consistently falls on the hater when God reverses the situation.

findings.finding_value: The characteristics most consistently co-occurring with M01-A reverential fear across the verse evidence are: (1) **wisdom** — Pro 1:7; 9:10; Psa 111:10; Job 28:28 (fear and wisdom paired as foundation and fruit across the Proverbs and wisdom Psalms corpora — extremely frequent co-occurrence); (2) **obedience / faithful conduct** — Deu 6:2; 8:6; 10:12; 2Ch 19:9; Col 3:22 (fear paired with walking in God's ways, keeping commandments, and faithful service — throughout the Deuteronomic corpus and NT); (3) **trust / confidence** — Pro 14:26; Psa 112:7-8; 1Sa 12:24 (fear of the Lord paired with trust in God and settled confidence, not anxiety); (4) **humility** — Pro 15:33; 22:4 (fear paired with humility as the dispositional ground of honour and blessing); (5) **love of God** — Deu 10:12-13 (fear, love, and service presented together as the whole covenantal orientation required).

M01-B acute fear co-occurs most frequently with: (1) **flight / protective action** — Gen 32:7; 1Ki 1:50; Jer 26:21 (fear driving immediate volitional action); (2) **trembling** (M01-E terms) — 1Sa 28:5 (fear and heart-trembling paired); Heb 12:21 (fear and trembling at Sinai — M01-B and E co-occurring in the same verse); (3) **faith / trust** as its structural opposite — Mar 4:40; Luk 8:50; Mar 5:36 (fear and faith paired as inner opposites).

M01-D dismay co-occurs with: (1) **shame** — Isa 37:27; Jer 48:20; Jer 50:36 (dismay and shame paired as co-consequences of judgment); (2) **trembling** (M01-E) — Jer 30:5 (trembling and dismay in the same panic-cry); (3) **bodily collapse** — Dan 5:6 (color change, limb-failure as the somatic co-occurrence of dismay).

M01-F anticipatory dread co-occurs with: (1) **grief / sorrow** — 2Cor 7:5 (fear within alongside external conflicts — fear and anguish co-present); (2) **faith as opposite** — 1Jo 4:18 (fear and perfect love as structural opposites — the absence of one implies the presence of the other).

The most prominent co-occurrence patterns across M01 are: wisdom with fear-of-God (M01-A, extremely frequent); faith/trust as M01-B's opposite; trembling as M01-B's and D's somatic companion; shame as M01-D's judicial companion. The most structurally significant co-occurrence is M01-A with wisdom — so consistent and so central that the two characteristics are almost definitionally linked (Pro 1:7 makes this definitional: fear of the Lord IS the beginning of wisdom).

The most frequent co-occurrences evidenced: (1) **Grief/Mourning (M03)**: Mar 3:5 (M02-A-VCG-04) shows anger paired with grief; Eze 3:14 (M02-B-VCG-03) shows rage as "bitterness and burning intensity" — bitterness has grief-register. (2) **Divine judgment/wrath as paired terms**: Jer 21:5 (M02-B-VCG-06) explicitly lists "anger, fury, and great wrath" as three co-occurring intensifying states within one emotional complex — the three terms of the cluster name are internally co-occurring. (3) **Jealousy and rage**: Pro 6:34 (M02-B-VCG-03) — jealousy produces rage; Eze 5:13 (M02-B-VCG-06) — God's fury driven by jealousy; Zec 8:2 (M02-B-VCG-06) — rage and jealousy paired. Jealousy (M02-E) and rage (M02-B) consistently co-occur. (4) **Pride/Arrogance (M08)**: Saul's anger (1Sa 18:8 / M02-B-VCG-02) — "the inner state is inseparable from jealousy and wounded honor." Uzziah's enraged defiance (2Ch 26:19 / M02-B-VCG-02) precedes divine judgment — pride and anger are paired in these cases.

(2) **Divine judgment/wrath as paired terms**: Jer 21:5 (M02-B-VCG-06) explicitly lists "anger, fury, and great wrath" as three co-occurring intensifying states within one emotional complex — the three terms of the cluster name are internally co-occurring. (3) **Jealousy and rage**: Pro 6:34 (M02-B-VCG-03) — jealousy produces rage; Eze 5:13 (M02-B-VCG-06) — God's fury driven by jealousy; Zec 8:2 (M02-B-VCG-06) — rage and jealousy paired. Jealousy (M02-E) and rage (M02-B) consistently co-occur. (4) **Pride/Arrogance (M08)**: Saul's anger (1Sa 18:8 / M02-B-VCG-02) — "the inner state is inseparable from jealousy and wounded honor." Uzziah's enraged defiance (2Ch 26:19 / M02-B-VCG-02) precedes divine judgment — pride and anger are paired in these cases.

Strife co-occurs with envy (Gal 5:20: strife alongside enmity and jealousy; Phili 1:15: rivalry paired with envy), with pride (Pro 13:10: strife rooted in insolence), and with the flesh's works generally. Strife rarely appears alone; it is typically part of a vice-cluster.

Six co-occurring characteristics appear with high frequency in M03's verse evidence.

(1) Fear (M01): distress paired with terror (Zep 1:15 — M03-D-VCG-04 ⇄ M03-D-VCG-01); anguish paired with dread (Luk 21:25 — M03-D-VCG-05). Co-occurrence is frequent in prophetic distress oracles.

(2) Repentance (M11): penitential weeping (M03-A-VCG-02), godly grief producing repentance (M03-C-VCG-02), covenantal distress turning the will (M03-D-VCG-03), communal mourning expressing inward turning (M03-B-VCG-04 — Jam 4:9; Joe 2:12). Co-occurrence is structurally built into several VCGs.

(3) Joy (M04): the structural opposite named as the characteristic that grief displaces and that displaces grief — weeping giving way to joy (Psa 30:5 — M03-A-VCG-04), mourning reversed into dancing (Psa 30:11 — M03-B-VCG-03), sorrow replaced by everlasting joy (Isa 35:10 — M03-C-VCG-01), sorrowful yet always rejoicing (2Cor 6:10 — M03-C-VCG-01).

(4) Strength/Weakness (M23/M24): grief producing bodily depletion (sighing wasting bones — M03-E-VCG-03; grief spending the psalmist's life — M03-C-VCG-01) shows co-occurrence with weakness. The anguish vocabulary of M03-D overlaps extensively with the distress/suffering vocabulary of M24.

(5) Prayer (M21): the dominant pattern of M03-D-VCG-01 (56 verses) is distress driving prayer — grief and prayer are constitutively related in this sub-group.

(6) Hope (M18): grief paired with hope as the distinguishing mark of Christian grief over the dead (1Th 4:13 — M03-C-VCG-01: "not like the hopeless grief of those without resurrection hope"); sighing and hope as paired eschatological conditions (Isa 35:10; 51:11 — M03-E-VCG-03; M03-C-VCG-01).

**[CHAR-1]** E — The most frequent co-occurring characteristics within M04 in this corpus: (1) **Gladness** (sim.chah, sa.me.ach) — Psa 14:7 ("let Jacob rejoice [gil], let Israel be glad [sa.me.ach]"); Psa 35:9 pairs rejoice (gil_verb) with a soul exulting; Psa 45:15 ("joy and gladness"); Psa 48:11 ("be glad... rejoice"); Isa 35:1 (glad and rejoice); Isa 65:18 (be glad and rejoice); Isa 66:10 — gladness is the most consistent co-occurring inner state with exultation. (2) **Praise and worship** — the exultation passages consistently move into praise (Psa 9:14; 63:5; 100:2; Isa 49:13). (3) **Trust** — Psa 13:5 explicitly pairs trust with rejoicing as precondition and state.

(4) *CHAR-6 (Habitual defection)*: VCG-04 — "walked in all the sins of Jeroboam... did not depart from them" — habitual defection is what accumulates the Jeroboam-sin legacy; CHAR-6 is the mechanism generating VCG-04's institutional record.

(1) *CHAR-13 (Sin as divine record)*: the record (CHAR-13) is what CHAR-14 addresses; Exo 32:30 — Moses seeking to atone for "your sin" — the sin-record is the object of the seeking; Lev 16:30 — clean from all sins — the record cleared is the goal; (2) *CHAR-3 (Confession)*: Exo 32:31 — Moses confessing the great sin before God; the verbal naming precedes and accompanies the seeking; (3) *CHAR-17 (Guilt as inner-being state)*: the forgiveness received addresses the subjective guilt that accompanies the objective record; Lev 23:27 — self-affliction is the guilt-posture of seeking; Luk 7:47 — the woman's love reveals guilt resolved; (4) *CHAR-11 (Sin as universal condition)*: Mar 3:28 — "all sins will be forgiven the children of man" — the universal human sin-condition (CHAR-11) is the scope within which CHAR-14 operates.

**[CHAR-15]** E — Four adjacent characteristics co-occur within or proximate to the 8-verse corpus. (1) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)*: Psa 78:17/32 — the persistent, escalating, willful rebellion ("sinned still more," "rebelling") within the generational pattern is CHAR-1's territory; the individual wilful sinning acts are how each generation perpetuates CHAR-15's inherited condition; (2) *CHAR-13 (Sin as divine record)*: Isa 43:27 — "your first father sinned, and your mediators transgressed against me" — the named ancestral sins constitute a divine record; the accumulated generational sinning of Isa 64:5 ("a long time in our sins") is the record's temporal depth; (3) *CHAR-3 (Confession)*: 1Ki 8:47 — "saying, 'We have sinned and have acted perversely and wickedly'" — the corporate confession is the seeking-acknowledgment characteristic; (4) *CHAR-5 (Refusal to repent)*: Psa 78:32 — "despite his wonders, they did not believe" — the persistent non-repentance that sustains the generational pattern.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Four adjacent characteristics co-occur within the 162-verse corpus. (1) *CHAR-13 (Sin as divine record)*: Hos 13:12 — "bound up; his sin is kept in store" — iniquity-as-crime is held in the same divine record that CHAR-13 describes; Psa 90:8 — "you have set our iniquities before you, our secret sins in the light of your presence" — both CHAR-18's iniquity and secret sins are before God simultaneously; (2) *CHAR-15 (Generational sin)*: VCG-02 (18 verses — Exo 20:5; Lam 5:7) — the generational iniquity register overlaps directly with CHAR-15's transmission concern; (3) *CHAR-14 (Forgiveness sought and received)*: VCG-06 (21 verses — Isa 40:2; Jer 31:34; Mic 7:18/19) — the pardon-and-removal register is the direct receiving-side of CHAR-14; (4) *CHAR-3 (Confession)*: Lev 16:21 — "confess over it all the iniquities"; Lev 26:40 — "confess their iniquity"; Psa 32:5 — "I did not cover my iniquity... I will confess" — confession is consistently paired with iniquity.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Four adjacent characteristics co-occur within the 147-verse corpus. Num 22:34 ("I have sinned") — Balaam's confession follows disclosure of inadvertent sinning. Confession is the prescribed adjacent characteristic activated by the realisation event. (2) *CHAR-14 (Forgiveness sought and received)*: Num 15:28 ("he shall be forgiven"), Lev 19:22 ("he shall be forgiven") — every prescribed remedy for unintentional sinning ends with forgiveness declared. Forgiveness-received is the terminal adjacent characteristic in the CHAR-2 arc. (3) *CHAR-17 (Guilt as inner-being state)*: Lev 5:5 ("when he realizes his guilt") — guilt-realisation is the post-disclosure inner-being state that characterises the transition into the remedy sequence.

(1) *CHAR-19 (Transgression as deliberate boundary-crossing)*: Lev 26:40 — "confess their iniquity and... treachery... and walking contrary to me" — iniquity and treachery paired; Hos 6:7 — "like Adam they transgressed the covenant; there they dealt faithlessly with me" — the transgression (covenant-crossing) and faithlessness are named together in the same event; (2) *CHAR-18 (Iniquity as accumulated moral crime)*: 2Ch 33:19 — "all his sin and his faithlessness" — faithlessness named alongside iniquity; Eze 18:24 — "the treachery of which he is guilty and the sin he has committed" — treachery and sin paired; (3) *CHAR-3 (Confession)*: Lev 26:40 — "if they confess their iniquity and... treachery"; Ezr 10:2 — "we have broken faith with our God"; (4) *CHAR-14 (Forgiveness sought and received)*: Lev 26:42 — "I will remember my covenant" as the divine response to confession of treachery.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Four adjacent characteristics co-occur within the 64-verse corpus. (1) *CHAR-18 (Iniquity as accumulated moral crime)*: Dan 9:5 — "we have sinned and done wrong (*a.vah*) and acted wickedly" — the perversity (a.vah) is named alongside iniquity and wickedness; 1Ki 8:47 — "acted perversely (*a.vah*) and wickedly" — the three-tier moral failure formula again; (2) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)*: 1Ki 8:47 — "we have sinned and have acted perversely" — sinning and perverting paired; Dan 9:5 — the comprehensive confession pairs all M10 categories; (3) *CHAR-19 (Transgression)*: Dan 9:5 — "done wrong and acted wickedly and rebelled (*pa.sha*)" — transgression alongside perversion; (4) *CHAR-16 (Sinner as moral character)*: 2Pe 2:12 — "irrational animals... born to be caught and destroyed" — the person constituted by corruption matches CHAR-16's constituted sinner-type.

(1) *CHAR-21 (Perversion as inner inversion)*: Eze 28:15 — "till unrighteousness was found in you" alongside the cherub's perversion; the inner structural distortion (CHAR-21) produces the unjust conduct (CHAR-22); (2) *CHAR-18 (Iniquity as accumulated moral crime)*: Eze 28:18 — "by the multitude of your iniquities, in the unrighteousness of your trade" — a.von (iniquity) and a.vel (injustice) paired; Rev 18:5 — "her sins are heaped high as heaven, and God has remembered her iniquities (*adikēmata*)" — adikēma and accumulation; (3) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)*: Psa 53:1 — "doing abominable iniquity (*a.vel*)" alongside sinning (*cha.ta*); (4) *CHAR-19 (Transgression)*: Eze 18:24 — "does injustice and does the same abominations" — injustice and rebellion paired.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Three adjacent characteristics appear alongside confession consistently.
