findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — The corpus evidences wilful sinning being produced by: (1) *Temptation/adversarial pressure*: Gen 39:9 (Potiphar's wife's persistent appeal), Neh 6:13 (enemies' constructed trap), Neh 13:26 (foreign women as corrupting influence) — these are external productions. (2) *Fear of persons*: 1Sa 15:24 ("I feared the people") — fear as the producing condition. (3) *Escalating compulsion*: Hos 13:2 — earlier sinning producing the next sinning — CHAR-1 is produced by prior CHAR-1 in the escalation pattern. (4) *Contempt*: Pro 14:21 ("whoever despises his neighbor is a sinner") — contempt as the inner condition producing interpersonal sinning.

**[CHAR-10]** E — Yes. (1) *Enticement is enabled by CHAR-4 (Conscience suppression)*: the conscience's suppression or absence is what allows desire-enticement to operate without internal resistance (T3.9.2 — enticement bypasses conscience). (2) *Enticement is produced by CHAR-6/16 (Habitual defection/Sinner as moral character)*: 2Pe 2:14 — "hearts trained in greed" — the enticers' own formed character (product of prior CHAR-6 habitual formation) is what enables them to practise enticement. (3) *Collective hypocrisy is produced by the social dynamics adjacent to CHAR-7*: the authority-conformity pressure that produces hypocrisy is structurally related to the contagious sin of CHAR-7.

**[CHAR-11]** E — CHAR-11 is produced by the Adamic representational act (Rom 5:12 — "sin came into the world through one man") — which is CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning) in its singular origin form. Adam's wilful sinning (CHAR-1 in the unique form of the representative head's deliberate transgression of a specific command) produced the universal condition (CHAR-11) that all subsequent humanity inherits. CHAR-11 is thus produced by CHAR-1 in a specific historical-representative context, though this is not the ordinary pattern (most CHAR-1 acts do not produce CHAR-11 for others).

**[CHAR-12]** E — Yes. (1) *Produced by CHAR-6 (Habitual defection)*: Joh 8:34 — "everyone who practices sin is a slave to sin" — CHAR-6 (the habitual practice of sinning) is the direct causal mechanism producing CHAR-12 (the enslaved state); CHAR-6 produces CHAR-12 through practice-accumulation. (2) *Enabled by CHAR-4 (Conscience suppression)*: Eph 4:26 — the suppression of conscience's resistance through unchecked affect enables sin's enslaving power to enter; CHAR-4 enables CHAR-12's installation.

**[CHAR-13]** E — Yes. (1) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)*: every sinning act (Lev 4:23 — "the sin which he has committed") creates a record entry; CHAR-1 is the primary producer of CHAR-13's entries; (2) *CHAR-6 (Habitual defection)*: VCG-04's sustained walking in Jeroboam's sins — the habitual pattern generates the institutional record that defines successive kings' reigns; (3) *CHAR-4 (Conscience suppression)*: while not explicitly named in this corpus, the failure to address the record (leading to its accumulation) is enabled by conscience suppression — Jer 16:10 — the people's failure to identify their sin under judgment implies CHAR-4-like suppression enabling record accumulation.

**[CHAR-14]** E — CHAR-14 is *enabled* by other characteristics rather than produced by them. (1) *CHAR-13 (Sin as divine record) creates the necessity*: the accumulated record is what makes forgiveness-seeking necessary; without the record, there is nothing to seek forgiveness for; (2) *CHAR-3 (Confession) often precedes*: the verbal naming of sin (CHAR-3) often accompanies or precedes the seeking (Exo 32:31 — Moses confessing before seeking); (3) *CHAR-4's reversal enables*: conscience engagement (the opposite of CHAR-4 — conscience suppression) is what triggers the seeking when sin "becomes known" (Lev 4:14).

**[CHAR-15]** E — Yes. (1) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning) at the originating moment*: Isa 43:27 — "your first father sinned" — the first instance of CHAR-15 was produced by a CHAR-1 wilful sinning act at the founding moment; the generational condition begins with an individual's wilful sinning; (2) *CHAR-5 (Refusal to repent) sustained the pattern*: Psa 78:32 — "they still sinned" — the persistent refusal to repent is what allows the generational pattern to continue across generations; CHAR-5's operation prevents the correction that would end CHAR-15's continuation.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Yes. (1) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)*: accumulated wilful sinning acts form the extreme-sinner-type identity (Gen 13:13; Amo 9:8); (2) *CHAR-6 (Habitual defection)*: the habitual departure from God is the formation mechanism of the extreme-sinner-type (VCG-03 — the sinner whose wrongdoing defines their total character); (3) *Federal imputation through Adam*: Rom 5:19 — "by the one man's disobedience the many were made sinners" — the sinner-identity is produced through Adam's representative sinning act, linking to CHAR-11 and CHAR-15 at the constitutional level.

**[CHAR-17]** E — Yes. (1) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)*: the sinning acts are the primary source of guilt-state entries — Jer 3:13 — "acknowledge your guilt, that you rebelled"; Lev 5:19 — "he has indeed incurred guilt before the Lord" — incurred by sinning; (2) *CHAR-6 (Habitual defection)*: 2Ch 33:23 — Amon's progressive guilt-accumulation results from habitual volitional defection rather than single acts; (3) *CHAR-11 (Sin as universal condition)*: Rom 5:19 (CHAR-16 corpus) — the sinner-condition produces the guilt that CHAR-17 registers subjectively; the universal sin-condition is the ontological source of the guilt-state's ongoing reality.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Yes. (1) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)*: the discrete sinning acts generate the iniquity-accumulation; Jer 3:13 — "acknowledge your guilt, that you rebelled" — the rebellion (CHAR-1) produces the iniquity (CHAR-18); (2) *CHAR-6 (Habitual defection)*: Psa 106:43 — "they were rebellious in their purposes and were brought low through their iniquity" — habitual rebellious purposes generate accumulated iniquity; (3) *CHAR-15 (Generational sin transmission)*: the generational transmission mechanism (CHAR-15) is how VCG-02's generational iniquity reaches the present generation; CHAR-15's mechanism produces CHAR-18's generational deposit in each new generation.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Yes. (1) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)*: the sinning acts of CHAR-1 are the specific contents of the transgressions; CHAR-19 is CHAR-1 seen at the knowing-boundary-crossing level; (2) *Absence of CHAR-5 (Fear of God)*: Psa 36:1 — "there is no fear of God before his eyes" — the absence of God-fear (which CHAR-19's adjacent cluster M10 would not cover but the inner-being landscape would) is the enabling condition that allows transgression's inner voice to speak; (3) *Adam's paradigm* (VCG-05 — Rom 5:15): the first transgression produced all subsequent transgression-possibility through the Adamic constitution.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 is produced by: (1) *Creaturely epistemic limitation* — not another moral characteristic but a constitutional feature: the creature's finite knowledge and perception make inadvertent sinning possible (Lev 4:2; Num 22:34). (2) *Instructional gap* — insufficient knowledge of God's commandments (Lev 4:2 — "the Lord's commandments about things not to be done" presupposes that not everyone knows all of them). (3) *Situational pressure/distraction* — the urgency of battle leading to ritual violation (1Sa 14:33/34). None of these are moral characteristics in the programme's sense — CHAR-2 is produced by epistemic and situational factors rather than by another inner-being characteristic.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Yes. (1) *Pride (within CHAR-16 adjacent)*: 2Ch 26:16 — "when he was strong, he grew proud, to his destruction. For he was unfaithful to the Lord his God" — pride is the generating inner condition; (2) *CHAR-6 (Habitual defection)*: the habitual departure from God's ways (2Ch 28:22 — progressively deepening) is the generative condition for consolidated faithlessness; (3) *Misplaced desire (within CHAR-16 adjacent)*: Pro 11:6 — "the treacherous are taken captive by their lust" — the lust that was present prior to the faithlessness is what drove the betrayal.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Yes. (1) *Deceitful desire (within CHAR-16/M31 adjacent)*: Eph 4:22 — "corrupt through deceitful desires" — the desire-faculty's deception drives the corruption; 2Pe 1:4 — "sinful desire" as world-corruption's source; (2) *CHAR-6 (Habitual defection)*: Jer 2:21 — the vine that "turned degenerate" — the habitual turning from God is the generating condition for the degeneracy perversion; (3) *Bribery* (external material corruption — within social dynamics): Exo 23:8 — bribery produces judgment-perversion — an externally induced inner-corruption.

**[CHAR-22]** E — Yes. (1) *CHAR-21 (Perversion)*: the perverted heart (Pro 6:14 — CHAR-21) generates the hand-enacted violence (Psa 58:2 — CHAR-22); the inner structural distortion produces the outer unjust conduct; (2) *God-denial (heart-atheism — Psa 53:1)*: the fool's heart-assertion "there is no God" produces the unjust conduct — the theological-cognitive failure drives the moral-conduct failure; (3) *Self-trust*: Hos 10:13 — "trusted in your own way" — the misplaced self-reliance produces the harvested injustice.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Confession is produced by: (1) *CHAR-17 (Guilt as inner-being state)*: the guilt-state experienced after sin is the inner condition that drives confession. 2Sa 24:10 — the heart-struck guilt produces the verbal confession. (2) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)*: the sin committed is the moral fact that confession names — the sin precedes and produces the need for confession. (3) *External judgment-pressure*: Num 21:7 (serpents), Judg 10:10 (enemy oppression), Exo 9:27 (plague) — suffering produces confession when it activates conscience. Whether the production is genuine (conscience engaged by judgment) or hollow (pressure-only, conscience not engaged) distinguishes the quality of what is produced.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Conscience suppression is produced by: (1) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)* through habituation: repeated wilful sinning without acknowledgment progressively suppresses the conscience (Ecc 8:12 — sinning "a hundred times" implies a formation process). (2) *CHAR-6 (Habitual defection)*: the habitual pattern of defection is both concurrent with and productive of conscience suppression — each act of defection that goes unacknowledged deepens the suppression. (3) *CHAR-5 (Refusal to repent)*: prolonged refusal to repent (which requires conscience-registration of the sin) can progressively suppress the conscience that originally registered it.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Refusal to repent is produced by: (1) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)*: a sin must have been committed before there is something to repent of — the wilful sinning is the precondition; (2) *CHAR-4 (Conscience suppression)* in its entry mode: the conscience that does not register the sin's gravity (Ecc 8:12 — dulled moral affect; 1Ki 16:31 — minimisation) provides less motivating force to turn; (3) *Inherited moral orientation*: 2Ki 15:9 — "as his fathers had done" — the inherited sinful pattern is the condition that makes refusal to repent the default, requiring no specific act of refusal to initiate.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Habitual defection is produced by: (1) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)* through accumulation: repeated wilful acts, when not addressed by confession or repentance, form the habitual pattern; (2) *CHAR-5 (Refusal to repent)* through sustained non-departure: the will's persistent refusal to turn from the sinning course progressively habituates the will to the sinning direction; (3) *CHAR-4 (Conscience suppression)* through numbing: the progressive numbing of the conscience removes the internal check that would prevent the formation of the habitual pattern.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Contagious sin is produced by: (1) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)* in the leader: the leader's personal wilful sinning is the source content of the contagious sin transmission — without the leader's own sinning, there is nothing to transmit causatively; (2) *CHAR-6 (Habitual defection)* as the received pattern: 1Ki 22:52 — Ahaziah received the habitual sinning pattern from father, mother, and Jeroboam — the received habitual pattern becomes the transmitted contagious sin in the next leader; (3) *CHAR-5 (Refusal to repent)* as the sustaining condition: the leader's refusal to turn from the sinning course is what keeps the CHAR-7 transmission active across a reign.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Political revolt is produced by: (1) *CHAR-20 (Faithlessness as covenant-breaking sin)* in the governing authority: 2Ch 21:10 — the ruler's forsaking of the Lord (faithlessness to the covenant) creates the spiritual-authority vacuum that enables the revolts; (2) *CHAR-1 (Wilful sinning)* as the opportunistic political act of the revolting community: the pa.sha revolt is a wilful transgressive act (the root's moral weight confirms this) — CHAR-1's wilful sinning operating in the political-authority domain; (3) *Political opportunity* (the governing authority's weakness — Ahab's death in 2Ki 1:1) — not a named characteristic but a political-circumstantial enabling condition.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Sinful speech is produced by: (1) *Heart corruption* (CHAR-16 — Sinner as moral character): Mat 15:19 — "out of the heart come... slander" — the constituted corrupt heart generates sinful speech; (2) *CHAR-4 (Conscience suppression)*: 1Ti 1:13 — "ignorant unbelief" as the ground of blasphemy — the suppressed or absent conscience allows sinful speech to flow unchecked; (3) *Affective states of hostility* (M06-adjacent — contempt, bitterness): Eph 4:31 / Col 3:8 — bitterness, wrath, and malice generate slander; (4) *Conceit and diseased volitional appetite*: 1Ti 6:4 — pride and craving produce the slander.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence suggests pride (Pro 21:4; Psa 10:2-4 — VCG-03) and practical-atheism/God-exclusion (VCG-02 — Psa 10:4; 9:17) as generative precursors, though the evidence does not establish a clean causal chain. Pride as an inner engine (VCG-03 — "arrogance drives the wicked," Psa 10:2) appears as a producing characteristic. The social alignment with wicked counsel (Psa 1:1 — VCG-04) also functions as a receptor-mechanism through which the characteristic is received. Eze 13:22 (VCG-07) shows that false prophetic enablement ("encouraging the wicked not to turn") functions as a maintaining-producing force for the characteristic's persistence. The evidence points to pride and God-exclusion as the primary upstream characteristics.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The evidence presents the characteristic as the constitutional baseline condition rather than as produced by another upstream characteristic within this corpus. Mat 7:11 (vc=14438 — VCG-02): "you who are evil" is addressed as a baseline fact. However, VCG-01 introduces a partial cosmic upstream: 1Jo 5:19 (vc=14433 — VCG-01) — "the whole world lies in the power of the evil one" — implies that the evil one's dominion over the world is a contributing environmental condition for the human constitutional evil. Mat 13:19 (vc=14435 — VCG-01): the evil one targets hearts that lack understanding, exploiting the constitutional vulnerability. The evidence suggests the cosmic adversarial dimension (M27 cross-register) as a partial upstream influence that exploits the constitutional condition rather than creating it from nothing.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. The characteristic is produced by the inner moral conditions that trigger the divine revulsion verdict. In the evidence: wickedness (CHAR-1 — the way of the wicked — Pro 15:9 — VCG-01), pride (the arrogant heart — Pro 16:5 — VCG-02), dishonesty (lying lips — Pro 12:22 — VCG-02; false balance — Pro 11:1 — VCG-01), and crooked heart (Pro 11:20 — VCG-01) all produce the abomination-verdict. These inner conditions are the upstream characteristics; CHAR-3 is their divine-verdict downstream. Conscience-silencing (VCG-04) is a secondary upstream: the silenced conscience enables sustained commission of abomination without arrest, which deepens the abominable condition.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The evidence presents multiple upstream characteristics. Pride: Eze 7:20 (vc=65909/65975 — VCG-05): "pride" drives the conversion of beautiful ornament into idol-material — pride as the generating upstream characteristic. Lust/desire: Eze 16:36 (vc=65986 — VCG-05): "your lust was poured out" in idolatrous whorings — inner desire as the upstream driver. Covetousness: Deu 7:25 (vc=1682 — VCG-02): "you shall not covet the silver or gold on them" — covetousness as the entry mechanism. The failure to separate from idolatrous peoples (Ezr 9:1 — VCG-03 — upstream environmental enabler). These characteristics (pride, lust, covetousness, failure of covenant separation) are the upstream conditions that produce CHAR-4.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The evidence presents multiple upstream producing characteristics. (1) Volitional preference for easy path over affliction — Job 36:21 (vc=38216 — VCG-04): iniquity chosen "rather than affliction" — the failure of will under pressure of cost produces the entry into iniquity. (2) Associational formation — Job 34:8 (vc=38214 — VCG-04): company of evildoers shapes the person toward iniquity. (3) Pride/self-assertion — 1Sa 15:23 (vc=38185 — VCG-02): "presumption is as iniquity" — self-assertive will elevating itself above divine word produces iniquity-as-presumption. (4) Uncircumcised heart — Jer 4:4 (vc=38447 — VCG-05): evil deeds from an uncircumcised heart — the uncleansed heart as the upstream condition.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The characteristic is produced by: (1) authority-rejection — Jude 8 (vc=14354 — VCG-01): "reject authority and blaspheme" — the blasphemy is produced by the prior authority-rejection; (2) sensory indulgence and dreamlike self-reliance — Jude 8 (VCG-01): "relying on their dreams, they defile the flesh" — the sensory-indulgent inner posture produces the blasphemous expression; (3) hardened will refusing repentance — Rev 16:9/11/21 (VCG-01): the will's refusal to repent produces each instance of cursing; (4) moral failure in conduct — Rom 2:24 (vc=14357 — VCG-02): the moral failure of those representing God produces the social blasphemy of his name; (5) hostile malicious evaluation — Joh 18:30 (vc=14378 — VCG-03): the accusers' inner hostile judgment produces the false verbal charge.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals two primary upstream producing characteristics. Pride is the most widely evidenced upstream condition: it produces Char 1 (Psa 10:2-4 — pride driving God-exclusion), Char 3 (Pro 16:5 — arrogant heart as abomination), and Char 6 (Jude 8 — self-relying on dreams, sensory self-indulgence enabling blasphemy). The fallen constitutional condition (Char 2) functions as the background enabling condition for all other M10b characteristics — the universal human constitutional evil provides the inner soil from which the other five characteristics grow. Char 4 partially generates Char 6 (idolatrous devotion leading to blasphemous speech against God as the covenant partner — Deu 32:16) and Char 3 (idolatrous abomination generating the moral-character abomination verdict). The cosmic adversarial dimension (Char 2 VCG-01 — the evil one's dominion) partially enables the conditions in which the other five characteristics flourish.

findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — Characteristic 1 is not produced by another inner-being characteristic — it is produced by bodily events (contact, emission, proximity) and authoritative verdicts (priestly examination). However, within Characteristic 1's sub-register VCG-04 (Lev 11:43-44, M10c-A-VCG-04), the willful non-avoidance of defiling contact would engage M10 (sin-act) cross-register — choosing to touch what one has been commanded not to touch is an act-of-sin that produces the defilement-state. In that sub-register, M10 (sin-act) produces Characteristic 1. More broadly, the cross-register flags from the Phase 3 verdicts identify M10 (sin→defilement) as a consistent companion: in those cases, the sin-act in M10 produces the defilement-state in Characteristic 1.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. Three upstream producers are evidenced: (1) M10 (sin-act): Rom 1:24 (VCG-02) — the sin-act of rejecting God is followed by God's giving over to impurity; the sin-act produces the defilement-state. (2) M29 (desire): Rom 1:24 (VCG-02) — "lusts of their hearts" as the generating desire; Col 3:5 (VCG-02) — "passion, evil desire" preceding impurity in the listed complex. (3) Job 14:4 constitutional origin (VCG-01) — the inherited human condition of uncleanness; the characteristic is also "produced" by the constituted human condition prior to individual acts.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. Two upstream producers are evidenced: (1) M10 (sin-act): the corporate sin-acts of idolatry, sexual violation, and desecration produce the defilement-state (Psa 106:39 — "they became unclean by their acts"). (2) The corporate habit-pattern operating across generations: Eze 20:18/30 — "defile yourselves after the manner of your fathers" — suggests the generational transmission of the defiling pattern is also a producing force; the generational defilement-habit is itself a prior condition that produces each generation's specific acts of defilement.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Characteristic 4 is produced by M27 (the unclean spirits as cosmic-evil agents) — the spirit's own agency is the producing cause of the defilement-state. M27 analyses the producing agents; Characteristic 4 analyses the defilement-state they produce. The INTEGRATION_NOTE confirms this relationship: defilement here is the result the external evil agent produces; in M27 the same verses analyse the agent's nature. No other characteristic in the M10c cluster produces Characteristic 4.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four producing-agents reveal the cluster's upstream ecology. Characteristic 1: primarily produced by bodily-contact events (mechanical, not a named inner-being characteristic); M10 (sin-act) produces Char 1 in the volitional-defilement sub-register (Lev 11:43-44). Characteristic 2: produced by M10 (sin-act — Rom 1:24), M29 (desire — Rom 1:24 lusts of the heart), and the inherited human constitutional condition (Job 14:4 — no clean thing from an unclean source). Characteristic 3: produced by M10 (sin-acts of idolatry, sexual violation, desecration — Psa 106:39: "became unclean by their acts") and generational defilement-habit transmission (Eze 20:18/30). Characteristic 4: produced by M27 (cosmic-evil agents — the unclean spirit as the exclusively external producer). The cluster's upstream map: the three self-generated characteristics (1-3) are produced by sin-acts (M10) and their constitutive elements (desire, habit, bodily mechanism); the externally-imposed characteristic (4) is produced exclusively by M27.

questions.section: T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics
questions.question_text: Is this characteristic a constituent element of another, or another a constituent of this one?

findings.session_b_note:
The data partially addresses this:

**Forgiveness as constituent of reconciliation:** Mat 5:24 (shared anchor with R130 reconciliation) — the forgiveness-act (leaving the gift) is the prerequisite act within the larger reconciliation process. Forgiveness may be a constituent element of reconciliation — a necessary but not sufficient component. Reconciliation requires forgiveness plus the bilateral restoration of the relationship. The data implies this but does not state it explicitly as a constituent relationship.

**Forgiveness as constituent of new covenant:** Jer 31:34 — "I will forgive their iniquity" is one of the constitutive elements of the new covenant promise (alongside "they shall all know me"). Forgiveness is a constituent of the new covenant, not a consequence of it — it is named as one of the defining features of the covenant itself.

**The aphiēmi act-structure as constituent of multiple characteristics:** OBS-064-026 names the shared act-structure between forgiveness and discipleship-leaving — the same aphiēmi that releases a debt-claim (forgiveness) releases family and property (discipleship). The releasing-act structure is a shared constitutional element across multiple characteristics in the programme. This raises the question whether forgiveness and discipleship share a common constitutive act at the deepest level.

*Gap noted:* Whether forgiveness is formally a constituent of grace or mercy (rather than a product of them) is not resolved in the data — the upstream relationship (grace → forgiveness) is established but the constituent relationship is not examined. This is likely a Session D synthesis question.

findings.session_b_note:
The data provides clear evidence on both sides:

**Compassion as a constituent element of love (R103):** The dominant co-occurrence signal (196 shared verses with love) and the shared RACHAM root (SD-001) indicate that compassion is at minimum a constituent element of the love vocabulary in the programme. The RACHAM root underlies both love (Reg 103) and compassion (Reg 23). The question raised by SD-001 and SD-005 is whether compassion is a constituent of love (one form that love takes when directed toward suffering) or whether they are genuinely distinct characteristics at the same constitutional level. This is the programme's most urgent constitutive boundary question for this registry.

**Compassion as a constituent of the chesed cluster:** The chesed vocabulary (H2617A — XREF in love and kindness registries; H2617B — OWNER in compassion registry carrying the shame/negative pole) demonstrates that compassion participates in the chesed semantic field that also constitutes love (R103) and kindness (R099). Compassion is constitutively embedded within the chesed cluster — it is not separable from it at the root level.

**Mercy as a constituent of compassion:** The three-stage SD-016 model (stirring → mercy disposition → act) positions mercy as a stage within compassion's operation rather than as a distinct parallel characteristic. If this model holds, mercy is a constituent element of compassion — its soul-level dispositional form — rather than a separate characteristic that compassion produces. This is a critical question for the programme that SD-009 defers to Session D.

**What does not constitute part of compassion:** The judicial-prohibition vocabulary (chus — "your eye shall not pity") reveals that hardness of judicial will is definitionally outside the constitutive structure of compassion. It is the active exclusion of compassion's constituent elements, not a form of them.

findings.session_b_note: Two constitutive relationships are evidenced: (1) Goodness is a constituent of the Gal 5:22 Spirit-fruit cluster — agathōsunē and chrēstotēs are both named as constituent elements of the Spirit-produced character cluster. The fruit of the Spirit is a unified character-expression of which goodness is a constituent. (2) Goodness as constituted: Mic 6:8 defines what is good as constituted by three things — doing justice, loving kindness, and walking humbly with God. On this reading, goodness in its human expression is not a simple quality but is constituted by these three orientations together. The constitutive relationship runs both ways: goodness is a constituent of the Spirit-fruit whole; and goodness itself is constituted by the tri-fold orientation of Mic 6:8. (OBS-067-OBS-027, OBS-067-OBS-045, SBF-067-Q005, SBF-067-Q003)

findings.finding_value: T6 as a whole reveals that goodness is structurally one of the most connected characteristics in the programme — both in co-occurrence breadth (top-25 co-occurrence list spanning the full dimensional spectrum), shared anchor density (7 shared anchors including the two highest-density synthesis nodes in the programme: Mic 6:8 and Gal 5:22), and root-level vocabulary sharing across three root families (TOV, AGATHO, CHRESTO) distributed across multiple registries. The structural picture confirms what T1 indicated definitionally: goodness is not a specialist characteristic but one that permeates and connects the whole inner-being landscape. The most significant T6 finding is the dual constitutive relationship (Q&A-152): goodness is simultaneously a constituent of the Spirit-fruit whole (Gal 5:22) and itself constituted by a tri-fold structure (Mic 6:8). This means goodness has both a containing relationship (it is part of something larger — Spirit-formed character) and an internal structure (it contains three orientations — justice, kindness, humility). The boundary distinctions (T6.5) remain the weakest component — all three nearest-neighbour boundaries (love, kindness, generosity) require Session D cross-registry synthesis. The R187 (strength) co-occurrence anomaly at 32 shared verses remains an open question for Session D (SP-067-027).

findings.finding_value: T1's boundary analysis (Q&A-019-021) identified three structural opposites and named the boundary problem with adjacent characteristics as partially unresolved. T6's structural relationships data confirms and deepens this: the boundary between goodness and love (R103), kindness (R99), and generosity (R65) is structurally unresolved at the root level — the vocabulary sharing (T6.4) and co-occurrence data (T6.1) reveal that these registries are adjacent precisely because they share root families and co-anchor at the same verses. T1's definition of goodness as constituted by the Mic 6:8 tri-fold (justice + kindness + humility — Q&A-152) directly names kindness as a component of goodness — which means the goodness-kindness boundary (T1.3 partially answered, T6.5 partially answered) is not between two separate characteristics but between a whole and one of its constituents. This reading resolves the boundary partially: kindness may be a constituent mode of goodness rather than a peer characteristic. Session D testing required.

findings.session_b_note: Both directions are evidenced: (1) Mercy as constituent of wisdom: Jam 3:17 (mercy is named as a component of wisdom from above — OBS-111-025; SP-111-017). (2) Atonement as constituent of mercy: the atonement vocabulary is not a separate characteristic but the structural mechanism through which mercy operates — atonement is mercy's embodied mechanism (DIM-111-001, OBS-111-075). (3) Holiness as mercy's companion: the holiness-mercy axis within R111 (OBS-111-050, OBS-111-051) suggests holiness and mercy are constitutively related rather than external to each other. *New finding: mercy has both constituent status within wisdom (Jam 3:17) and constituent elements within itself (atonement as its mechanism, compassion as its motivation, holiness as its relational character).* OBS-111-025, OBS-111-050, OBS-111-075.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-111-006: Reading T6 as a whole reveals mercy as structurally integrative — its cross-registry position is not peripheral but central. The T6 synthesis: (a) co-occurrence positions mercy as a hub between the gu…
findings.finding_value: Reading T6 as a whole reveals mercy as structurally integrative — its cross-registry position is not peripheral but central. The T6 synthesis: (a) co-occurrence positions mercy as a hub between the guilt-facing pole (R073 guilt at 75) and the grace-giving pole (R023 compassion at 76) and the power cluster (R187, R196, R197, R198); (b) mercy appears consistently in the middle of inner-being sequences as the bridge from negative condition to positive outcome (Q&A-149); (c) mercy is produced by love and compassion and produces forgiveness, joy, shame, identity, comfort; (d) mercy has constituent status within wisdom (Jam 3:17) and has constituent elements within itself (atonement as mechanism, compassion as motivation, holiness as relational frame); (e) the vocabulary root architecture is theologically coherent (Q&A-157), each root family tracing the full arc of the mercy-event; (f) 16 shared anchor verses confirm mercy's appearance at the intersection of multiple analytical domains (Q&A-165); (g) boundaries with compassion and lovingkindness are partially drawn but require Session D. The T6 synthesis: mercy functions as the structural integrator of the inner-being relational economy — it is the characteristic through which negative conditions are bridged to positive states across the widest range of cross-registry connections in C17.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-012: T1's four-element structure (disposition, mechanism, petition-response, spatial locus) maps to T6's finding that mercy is a structural hub. Each of mercy's four elements connects to a different cluste…
findings.finding_value: T1's four-element structure (disposition, mechanism, petition-response, spatial locus) maps to T6's finding that mercy is a structural hub. Each of mercy's four elements connects to a different cluster of adjacent characteristics: the disposition element connects to compassion/love/anger adjacencies; the mechanism element connects to forgiveness/guilt/atonement adjacencies; the petition-response element connects to prayer/calling/despair adjacencies; the spatial locus connects to holiness/mind/soul adjacencies. Mercy's definitional complexity (T1) is what enables its structural hub position (T6).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-111-021: T3 shows mercy as a faculty-comprehensive characteristic and T6 shows mercy as a structurally integrative hub characteristic. Reading together: the faculty-comprehensiveness (T3) is what enables the s…
findings.finding_value: T3 shows mercy as a faculty-comprehensive characteristic and T6 shows mercy as a structurally integrative hub characteristic. Reading together: the faculty-comprehensiveness (T3) is what enables the structural hub position (T6). A characteristic that activates all (or nearly all) inner faculties is positioned to connect to the widest range of adjacent characteristics — which is exactly what T6's co-occurrence and cross-registry data shows. Mercy's structural hub position in T6 is the cross-registry expression of its faculty-comprehensiveness in T3. The one missing faculty (creativity, T3.5.2 — S) corresponds to the one connection not evidenced in T6 — creative production is not a named output of mercy in the cross-registry data.

findings.session_b_note: Contrition is named as the inner precondition of genuine repentance (registry description — R135). This is a constitutive relationship: contrition constitutes part of what makes repentance genuine rather than a "change of strategy." Without contrition, repentance lacks its inner ground. Contrition is therefore constitutive of genuine repentance. OBS-030-001, OBS-030-002.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-030-006: T6 as a whole positions contrition within the inner-being landscape as a convergence characteristic with multiple structural connections. The co-occurrence pattern places contrition at the nexus of he…
findings.finding_value: T6 as a whole positions contrition within the inner-being landscape as a convergence characteristic with multiple structural connections. The co-occurrence pattern places contrition at the nexus of heart (R183), fear (R061), pride (R123), sorrow (R151), and fellowship (R062) — all meeting in contrition's primary anchor verses. The causal structure is rich: contrition is causally produced by divine-human encounter; it causally produces divine nearness; it is constitutive of genuine repentance (R135). The vocabulary is sufficiently distinctive (dkh/ktt/nkh root families) that contrition maintains lexical identity even amid these structural connections. The shared anchor analysis confirms Isa 57:15 as the convergence verse — simultaneously registering in divine identity, human moral failure, and creaturely posture registers. T6 synthesis: contrition is a structurally central characteristic that connects multiple inner-being registers (dependence, fear, pride, heart, sorrow, fellowship) while maintaining a distinctive vocabulary and position as the penitential sub-form of creaturely dependence before God.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-012: The definition tier (T1) establishes contrition's primary dimension (Dependence/Creatureliness) and its structural opposite (pride); the structural relationships tier (T6) confirms and enriches this t…
findings.finding_value: The definition tier (T1) establishes contrition's primary dimension (Dependence/Creatureliness) and its structural opposite (pride); the structural relationships tier (T6) confirms and enriches this through correlation data. T6's convergence position finding (Q&A-147 — contrition appears where heart, fear, and pride dynamics are simultaneously active) is a structural consequence of T1's definition: a characteristic defined by the collapse of self-sufficiency before God will necessarily appear in the same verses as the characteristics that are most involved in self-sufficiency (pride) and in creaturely orientation toward God (fear, heart). The causal sequence (contrition precedes divine nearness; contrition follows encounter with divine holiness) maps onto the sequential relationships in T6, confirming T1's directional analysis.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-026: The formative tier (T5) shows that contrition's formation produces the settled lowliness and word-permeability that Isa 66:2 designates; the structural relationships tier (T6) shows that contrition is…
findings.finding_value: The formative tier (T5) shows that contrition's formation produces the settled lowliness and word-permeability that Isa 66:2 designates; the structural relationships tier (T6) shows that contrition is constitutive of genuine repentance (T6.3). Together T5 and T6 reveal the inner logic of contrition's formative productivity: contrition forms the character that makes genuine repentance possible (T6.3 constitutive relationship) and sustains the inner posture (lowliness, word-permeability) that the structural connections (fear, heart) express in their own vocabularies. The formation account (T5) explains why contrition has such dense structural connections (T6) — it is the inner-being event that produces the character from which the connected characteristics flow.

findings.session_b_note: Fellowship is constituent of: unity (R167 — fellowship is the participatory inner reality of which unity is the corporate expression); sanctification (fellowship with God-fearers is the relational mechanism of character formation); divine nature participation (2Pe 1:4 — fellowship is the mode of ontological transformation). OBS-062-029, OBS-062-058.
findings.finding_value: Fellowship is constituent of: unity (R167 — fellowship is the participatory inner reality of which unity is the corporate expression); sanctification (fellowship with God-fearers is the relational mechanism of character formation); divine nature participation (2Pe 1:4 — fellowship is the mode of ontological transformation). OBS-062-029, OBS-062-058.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-062-006: T6 positions fellowship as a structurally central hub characteristic — it connects desire (R43 — strongest co-occurrence signal), unity (R167 — corporate outcome), spirit (R184 — mediating agent), com…
findings.finding_value: T6 positions fellowship as a structurally central hub characteristic — it connects desire (R43 — strongest co-occurrence signal), unity (R167 — corporate outcome), spirit (R184 — mediating agent), comfort (R192 — affective product of shared suffering), contrition and sorrow (R30, R151 — shared anchor Isa 53:5), yielding (R180 — shared anchor 2Pe 1:4), covenant (R34 — shared anchor Mal 2:14). Fellowship is structurally upstream of unity (fellowship is the participatory inner reality; unity is its corporate structural expression) and downstream of desire (desire directs fellowship). The vocabulary analysis (T6.4) reveals the root-level connection between wound and companionship (both from chavar) as the deepest structural finding: fellowship and suffering-wounding share the same etymological root, revealing that the deepest fellowship is structurally connected to the deepest wounding.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-012: T1's five-mode structure explains T6's co-occurrence pattern. The desire-R43 co-occurrence (6 shared verses — strongest signal) reflects T1's finding that desire is the internal motivating state direc…
findings.finding_value: T1's five-mode structure explains T6's co-occurrence pattern. The desire-R43 co-occurrence (6 shared verses — strongest signal) reflects T1's finding that desire is the internal motivating state directing fellowship — they co-occur because desire directs fellowship. The unity-R167 co-occurrence reflects T1's finding that fellowship is the participatory inner reality of which unity is the corporate outcome — they co-occur because fellowship produces unity. The structural connections in T6 are the cross-registry expression of T1's definitional relationships.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-021: T3's moral evaluation and conscience faculty engagements explain the co-occurrence pattern with desire (R43) in T6. Desire (R43) directs fellowship; conscience assesses the moral quality of the fellow…
findings.finding_value: T3's moral evaluation and conscience faculty engagements explain the co-occurrence pattern with desire (R43) in T6. Desire (R43) directs fellowship; conscience assesses the moral quality of the fellowship object; moral evaluation confirms or challenges the direction. The three characteristics (desire, fellowship, conscience) operate in sequence: desire directs → conscience evaluates → fellowship forms. The T6 co-occurrence signal between R43 and R062 is the shared-verse evidence of this sequential relationship that T3's faculty analysis illuminates.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-026: T5's formation mechanisms (participatory transfer and wound-as-cleansing) explain why fellowship is structurally connected in T6 to both desire (R43 — participatory-transfer mechanism begins with desi…
findings.finding_value: T5's formation mechanisms (participatory transfer and wound-as-cleansing) explain why fellowship is structurally connected in T6 to both desire (R43 — participatory-transfer mechanism begins with desire-directed alignment) and to contrition/sorrow (R30, R151 — wound-as-cleansing mechanism meets contrition and sorrow at Isa 53:5). T5's two formation mechanisms generate two distinct clusters of T6 structural connections: the habitual-alignment cluster (R43 desire, R167 unity, R34 covenant) and the suffering-cleansing cluster (R30 contrition, R151 sorrow, R192 comfort). Formation mechanism determines structural cluster.

findings.session_b_note: Forgiveness is constituent of: reconciliation (R130 — Mat 5:24 shared anchor; reconciliation presupposes forgiveness as its inner ground); the new covenant (Jer 31:34 — forgiveness is one of the defining elements of the new covenant); love-formation (Luk 7:47 — forgiveness is constitutive of the love-response). OBS-064-017, OBS-064-028, OBS-064-029.
findings.finding_value: Forgiveness is constituent of: reconciliation (R130 — Mat 5:24 shared anchor; reconciliation presupposes forgiveness as its inner ground); the new covenant (Jer 31:34 — forgiveness is one of the defining elements of the new covenant); love-formation (Luk 7:47 — forgiveness is constitutive of the love-response). OBS-064-017, OBS-064-028, OBS-064-029.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-064-006: T6 reveals forgiveness as a structural hub in the C17 and broader programme network. The guilt-073 connection (51 shared verses — dominant) positions forgiveness as the definitional counterpart and re…
findings.finding_value: T6 reveals forgiveness as a structural hub in the C17 and broader programme network. The guilt-073 connection (51 shared verses — dominant) positions forgiveness as the definitional counterpart and remedy to guilt. The mercy-111 connection (15 shared) positions mercy as the generating disposition for forgiving. The love-103 connection (8 shared) confirms the downstream love-production as a recurring structural signal. Jer 31:34 as the highest-convergence anchor (shared with guilt, love, thought) is analytically significant for Session D. The lexical analysis (T6.4) reveals salach's lexical isolation — no root-sharing — which structurally preserves the divine-exclusive domain of forgiveness at its deepest Hebrew root. The distinctions analysis positions: guilt as the condition forgiveness addresses (kind distinction), mercy as the disposition that generates forgiving (layer distinction), reconciliation as the restored state that forgiveness makes possible (sequence distinction). T6 synthesis: forgiveness is a structural hub whose connections are definitionally structured — every major co-occurrence corresponds to a logical role in the forgiveness transaction (guilt = prior condition; mercy = divine disposition; repentance = access-posture; love = downstream product; faith = receiving instrument; reconciliation = restored outcome).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-012: T1's definitional structure explains T6's co-occurrence pattern with precision. Guilt-073 (51 shared verses) is the definitional counterpart (T1 — forgiveness releases guilt; they are structurally ins…
findings.finding_value: T1's definitional structure explains T6's co-occurrence pattern with precision. Guilt-073 (51 shared verses) is the definitional counterpart (T1 — forgiveness releases guilt; they are structurally inseparable). Mercy-111 (15 shared) is the generating disposition (T1 — God's mercy is what produces the forgiving act). Repentance-135 (12 shared) is the access-posture (T1 — human side receiving condition). Love-103 (8 shared) is the named downstream state (T1 — Luk 7:47). Faith-059 (9 shared) is the receiving instrument (T1). Every major co-occurrence registry corresponds to a logical role in T1's definitional structure. T6's co-occurrence data is therefore a reading of the complete forgiveness transaction from the outside — each co-registry names one element of the transaction that T1 defines from the inside.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-021: T3's memory faculty finding (Jer 31:34 — divine "remember no more") explains the R160 thought/knowledge co-occurrence at that verse: the divine cognitive act of non-remembering and the human cognitive…
findings.finding_value: T3's memory faculty finding (Jer 31:34 — divine "remember no more") explains the R160 thought/knowledge co-occurrence at that verse: the divine cognitive act of non-remembering and the human cognitive outcome of knowing God meet in the same verse because they are structurally connected — the guilt-barrier's removal (forgiveness) enables the cognitive-relational access (knowing God). T3's affect-faculty finding (love produced — Luk 7:47) explains the R103 love co-occurrence (8 shared verses) — love is the affective downstream product of forgiveness. T3's conscience faculty finding confirms the R073 guilt structural partnership — guilt is what conscience identifies as the prior condition that forgiveness addresses. Faculty engagements (T3) and structural co-occurrences (T6) are mutually explanatory.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-024: T4's relational directions correspond to T6's structural connections. The God-to-human direction (T4.1) corresponds to the mercy-111 connection (mercy as the divine disposition generating the act, ope…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational directions correspond to T6's structural connections. The God-to-human direction (T4.1) corresponds to the mercy-111 connection (mercy as the divine disposition generating the act, operating in the same direction). The human-to-God direction (T4.2) corresponds to the repentance-135 and faith-059 connections (the access-postures that operate in the seeking direction). The horizontal giving-direction (T4.3) corresponds to the love-103 connection (love as the upstream motivator of horizontal forgiveness — Eph 4:32) and the reconciliation-130 connection (Mat 5:24 — reconciliation as the restored state that horizontal forgiveness produces). T4's relational architecture and T6's co-occurrence network are different analytical lenses on the same structural reality.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-026: T5's formation sequence (forgiveness received → love → capacity to extend) explains why T6 finds love-103 as a co-occurrence signal (8 shared verses) — love is the formation product most visibly evide…
findings.finding_value: T5's formation sequence (forgiveness received → love → capacity to extend) explains why T6 finds love-103 as a co-occurrence signal (8 shared verses) — love is the formation product most visibly evidenced in the co-occurrence data. T5's two mechanisms (declaratory and atoning) explain the guilt-073 co-occurrence dominance (51 shared verses) — guilt is the condition both mechanisms address, and so it co-occurs across the entire forgiveness corpus. T5's sanctification-formation dimension (T5.5 — Eph 4:32) explains the reconciliation-130 shared anchor (Mat 5:24): the commanded forgiveness in the formation context is structurally connected to the restored relational state (reconciliation) as the goal of the horizontal act. T5's formation mechanisms generate T6's structural connections.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-006: T6 reveals compassion as the structural centre of the C17 cluster rather than a peripheral member. The love co-occurrence (196/351 = 55.8% of all OWNER verses) is uniquely dominant — compassion and lo…
findings.finding_value: T6 reveals compassion as the structural centre of the C17 cluster rather than a peripheral member. The love co-occurrence (196/351 = 55.8% of all OWNER verses) is uniquely dominant — compassion and love co-occur in more than half of all active verses, raising the programme-level question whether they are truly separable at the data level. Three structural observations from the co-occurrence landscape: (1) compassion sits at C17's centre of gravity (love, mercy, kindness as top three co-occurrences — all within-cluster); (2) compassion generates a human-response cluster (peace, faith, will, surrender, seeking co-occurring at significant levels — the pattern of divine compassion generating human inner-being responses); (3) compassion is constitutively responsive to human distress (despair, guilt, distress, evil all present in the co-occurrence table — compassion operates most characteristically in the presence of need). The CHASAD root crossing compassion (C17) and shame (C06) is the programme's most structurally unexpected finding — a root family that bridges two clusters. Exod 34:6 as the programme's most multiply-anchored verse (6 registries) must be treated as a cluster-level synthesis anchor. The compassion/mercy boundary (SD-009) is the most critical unresolved distinction. T6.7 (dimensional sharing) is programme-stage limited — formally deferred.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-017: T2's somatic-constitutional location explains several T6 structural connections. The shared anchor at Isa 53:5 (with R030 contrition) confirms that the somatic wound vocabulary intersects both compass…
findings.finding_value: T2's somatic-constitutional location explains several T6 structural connections. The shared anchor at Isa 53:5 (with R030 contrition) confirms that the somatic wound vocabulary intersects both compassion and contrition at the constitutional-somatic level — both characteristics have somatic-body language as part of their evidential ground. The CHASAD root's crossing of compassion and shame clusters (T6.4 — most unexpected structural finding) is partly explainable from T2: if CHASAD names a covenantal-soul disposition, it can operate in both the positive register (chesed — steadfast love/compassion) and the negative register (bōsheth — shame as the opposite soul-condition of exposed vulnerability). T2's constitutional portrait (soul-body interface) is the constitutional ground for the root-level cluster-crossing that T6 identifies.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-026: T5's three mechanisms of change explain the structural pattern visible in T6's co-occurrence landscape. The encounter/sudden mechanism (splanchnizō producing immediate transformation) corresponds to t…
findings.finding_value: T5's three mechanisms of change explain the structural pattern visible in T6's co-occurrence landscape. The encounter/sudden mechanism (splanchnizō producing immediate transformation) corresponds to the high co-occurrence with despair (28 verses) and distress (16 verses) — these are the conditions that trigger the sudden compassion-event. The covenantal-sustaining mechanism corresponds to the high co-occurrence with love (196 verses), mercy (76 verses), and covenant (17 verses) — these are the characteristics that share the sustaining, gradual register with chesed. The participatory-ontological mechanism corresponds to the sequential relationship (compassion → mercy confirmed as constitutionally causal in T6.2) — the deepest formation mechanism produces the person who naturally extends mercy as the externalised form of the compassion-character formed within. Formation mechanisms (T5) explain co-occurrence patterns (T6).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-006: T6 produces the most structurally significant finding in the review set for any single tier: grace is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic. It is the originating point of a causal chai…
findings.finding_value: T6 produces the most structurally significant finding in the review set for any single tier: grace is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic. It is the originating point of a causal chain, not its product. This categorically distinguishes grace from every other characteristic reviewed — all others can be produced by at least one other characteristic; grace cannot. This structural uniqueness is confirmed by T2.9's origin analysis (grace originates with God — it does not originate in the human constitutional system) and is analytically consistent across T6.2 (seeking is the posture before grace arrives, not its producer), T6.3 (S-rating on "is grace produced by another characteristic"), and T6.4 (the vocabulary's structural completeness without a generative human-side term). The co-occurrence pattern reveals grace at the intersection of divine initiative and creaturely need: seeking (R140 — 40 verses, dominant) as the creature's pre-grace posture; moral failure cluster (evil, guilt, sin, transgression) as the creaturely context; power cluster (strength, might) confirming the 2Cor 12:9 connection. The love co-occurrence (R103 — 14 verses) is the primary within-cluster signal raising the grace-love boundary question (SD013). All major boundary distinctions (grace-love, grace-mercy, grace-justice, grace-chesed) remain open at T6.5 — the most unresolved boundary cluster in the review set. T6.7 (dimensional sharing) is programme-stage limited.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-012: T1's dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) and T6's co-occurrence pattern are mutually confirming. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is the co-occurrence ex…
findings.finding_value: T1's dimension classification (Relational Disposition as primary) and T6's co-occurrence pattern are mutually confirming. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is the co-occurrence expression of T1's finding that grace requires the receptor's inner posture of appeal: seeking is the relational posture before grace arrives, and the vocabulary encodes this (tachanum — built into the same root as chen). T6's structural uniqueness finding (grace is not produced by any other characteristic) is T1's definitional consequence: because grace is constitutively the uncaused inclination of the greater toward the lesser, it cannot be produced by anything in the lesser's constitutional system. T1's definition predicts T6's structural uniqueness.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-017: T2's constitutional origin finding (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system) and T6's structural uniqueness finding (grace is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic) …
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin finding (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system) and T6's structural uniqueness finding (grace is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic) are the same finding from constitutional and structural perspectives. They confirm each other from different analytical directions: T2 establishes that there is no constitutional source for grace within the human person; T6 establishes that there is no characteristic-level source for grace within the programme's inner-being landscape. The vocabulary's structural completeness (T7 — but relevant here as T6.4) reflects this constitutional uniqueness: because grace originates entirely from outside the human system, its vocabulary must encode the full two-sided circuit (giving and receiving) from within a single root, with no gap left for a generative human-side term.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-021: T3's faculty findings explain several patterns in T6's co-occurrence landscape. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is partly explained by T3.6's agency-constituting finding: seekin…
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty findings explain several patterns in T6's co-occurrence landscape. The seeking co-occurrence dominance (R140 — 40 verses) is partly explained by T3.6's agency-constituting finding: seeking requires the constituted agency that grace provides for its own reception (SD026 — grace giving the capacity for supplication). The power cluster co-occurrences (strength R187 — 15 verses, might R198 — 10 verses) confirm T3.7's agency-constituting finding at the cross-registry level: grace producing agency is registered as co-occurring with power/strength across the corpus. T3.8's moral clarity finding explains the guilt co-occurrence (R073 — 10 verses): the moral clarity grace produces is most visible at the point of moral failure, and the co-occurrence reflects this — grace and guilt appear together because grace produces the moral clarity that accurately names the guilt it addresses.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-026: T5's five formation mechanisms explain the structural pattern visible in T6's co-occurrence and sequential landscape. The encounter mechanism (sudden grace-event) corresponds to the sequences confirme…
findings.finding_value: T5's five formation mechanisms explain the structural pattern visible in T6's co-occurrence and sequential landscape. The encounter mechanism (sudden grace-event) corresponds to the sequences confirmed in T6.2 (grace precedes and causes the immediate responses of mourning, fear, supplication — SD038, SD026). The word mechanism (Act 20:32) corresponds to the faith co-occurrence (R059 — 10 verses): the proclaimed word that carries grace produces faith as its response. The inference mechanism (Rom 8:32 — assurance derived by reasoning) corresponds to the hope and peace co-occurrences (R117 — 10 verses): reasoned assurance from grace produces the inner peace and hope co-occurring registries name. The mediated-transformation mechanism (tenderheartedness → forgiving) produces the love co-occurrence (R103 — 14 verses) as tenderheartedness is the inner precondition of the forgiving that love and grace share. T5's mechanisms generate T6's structural connections.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-028: T6's structural uniqueness (grace is not produced by any inner-being characteristic — categorically the originating point of the causal chain) and T7's vocabulary structural completeness (every dimens…
findings.finding_value: T6's structural uniqueness (grace is not produced by any inner-being characteristic — categorically the originating point of the causal chain) and T7's vocabulary structural completeness (every dimension of grace's operation has a corresponding term, including the structural negative acharistos) confirm and explain each other. T6 establishes that grace stands outside the characteristic-production network; T7 establishes that the vocabulary encodes this structural position with unique completeness — including the negative (acharistos) and the NT coinage (charitoō) as markers of grace's conceptual uniqueness. The shared anchor verses (T6.6) are also T7's most evidentially rich texts: Eph 2:8 (which anchors multiple co-occurring registries) carries the most complete single-verse expression of grace's structural position (sovereign gift, not of works, producing faith). T6 and T7 mutually confirm that grace's structural uniqueness in the programme landscape corresponds to a lexical uniqueness in the vocabulary — both point to the same underlying analytical claim: grace is categorically distinct from every other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Two directions are evidenced. (1) Covenant as constituent of other characteristics: hesed (steadfast love, R103) is constituted in part by its covenantal context — Deu 7:9 pairs hesed and berit as a unit, suggesting that the committed, enduring quality of hesed is in part constituted by the covenantal relationship within which it operates. Similarly, hope (R078) in the biblical sense is constituted in part by covenantal promise — the covenants of promise (Eph 2:12) are the structural constituent of eschatological hope. (2) Other characteristics as constituents of covenant: faithfulness (emunah-root — OBS-034-008) is a constituent element of the firm covenant (amanah) — faithfulness is the character quality from which genuine covenant-keeping is constituted. Oath (H0423, H7650 — OBS-034-007, OBS-034-017) is the verbal-performative constituent of the covenant-making act — covenant cannot be constituted without the performative commitment mechanism of the oath. **[CLUSTER]** E. The cluster's internal constitution is the most important finding here. F (moral reckoning) is a constitutive mechanism within C (justification's reception) — the person who is justified must reckon from that declared reality (F) to appropriate it. B (moral uprightness) is a constitutive inner expression of A2 (human righteousness) — uprightness is the dispositional quality that characterises the inner texture of the righteous state. D (avenging justice) is a constitutive response-mode of A1 (God's righteousness expressed in its judicial-retributive mode). E (condemnation) and C (justification) are constitutively paired as the negative and positive poles of the same judicial verdict faculty. G (structural opposites) is constitutively defined by its opposition to A1 and A2.

The cluster is not a set of independent characteristics but an internally constituted system: each sub-group is either the source (A1), the derived state (A2), a mechanism within it (C, F), a dispositional expression of it (B), a response-mode of it (D), a negative counterpart (E), or its defining boundary (G).

findings.finding_value: M01-A is a constituent element of: (1) **wisdom** — Pro 1:7 establishes fear as wisdom's beginning/foundation — it is constitutively included in wisdom as its root, though not identical to it; (2) **covenant faithfulness** — Mal 2:5 (Levi's covenant defined by reverential fear — the fear is constitutive of the covenant relationship, not merely its accompaniment). Additionally, M01-A has constituent elements within it: cognitive alignment (knowing God's greatness), volitional governance (choosing to maintain the posture), and affective reverence (the felt awe) are all constituents of the reverential fear itself.

M01-B's awe-register (B-VCG-02: fear at Jesus's miracles) is a constituent element of **worship** in those contexts: Mat 9:8 (fear moving immediately into glorifying God — the fear is the entry-point and a constituent element of the worship response).

M01-G timidity is constituted in part by the absence of the spirit of power and love (2Ti 1:7) — the characteristic is constituted by the privation of what God gives. Courage (the spirit of power and self-control) is the constitutive positive of which timidity is the absence.

M01-A is constitutively linked to wisdom (as its root), to covenant faithfulness (as its relational ground), and to worship (as its affective expression). These relationships are constitutive, not merely correlational.

Rage appears as a constituent of divine judgment-wrath across the Jer-Eze corpus: Jer 21:5 (M02-B-VCG-06) lists "anger, fury, and great wrath" as constituent elements of a single complex divine state. The rage is a constituent of the larger judgment-wrath complex.

**Transition: E-VCG-01 → D-VCG-01:** Divine jealousy is a constituent of divine anger: Deu 6:15 (M02-B-VCG-01): "because he is jealous, his anger can be kindled and bring destruction" — jealousy is the ground from which anger springs; it is constitutive of the anger's character.

Grief appears to be a constituent element of repentance (M11) in its affective dimension — genuine repentance as the New Testament narrates it includes godly grief as its affective core (2Cor 7:9-11; Jam 4:9 — M03-C-VCG-02, M03-B-VCG-04). Grief is also a constituent element of lament — the genre-form that makes grief articulable and Godward. Whether other characteristics constitute parts of grief: love (M05) is constitutive of the relational core of grief — the capacity for grief requires the capacity for love; without love there is no grief.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence suggests exultation is a constituent element of **worship** in the OT framework — the Psalmic and prophetic commanded exultations (Psa 2:11; 32:11; 100:2; Isa 65:18) show exultation as integral to what worship is. Worship is not complete without exultation. Conversely, **gladness** (M04 Characteristic 3) appears to be partially constituted by exultation in the highest registers — the gladness that co-occurs with exultation (Psa 14:7; 48:11; Isa 65:18) may include the exultation as its most elevated expression.

**[CHAR-2]** E — (1) **Joy is a constituent element of worship** — the feast-commandments make Joy intrinsic to worship; the "serve the Lord with gladness" command (Psa 100:2) makes Joy constitutive of the service-relationship; (2) **Joy is a constituent of the kingdom of God** — Rom 14:17 ("righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit") names Joy as one of three kingdom-constituents; (3) **Thanksgiving (eucharistia, M04-C-VCG-06) is partly constituted by Joy** — the gratitude register within this characteristic shares Joy's affective character; (4) **Suffering-Joy (Characteristic 7) is partly constituted by Joy** — the paradoxical suffering-Joy register (agalliao in M04-E-VCG-02) is Joy operating in the specific context of suffering, not a fully distinct phenomenon.

**[CHAR-7]** E — (1) **Suffering-Joy partly constitutes Hope** — the characteristic's eschatological orientation is the affective-experiential face of the theological virtue of hope; (2) **Joy (Characteristic 2) partly constitutes Suffering-Joy** — the agalliao term is shared; Suffering-Joy is Joy in its most paradox-sustaining form; Joy provides the genus of which Suffering-Joy is a specific species; (3) **The Spirit's joy (Gal 5:22) constitutes Suffering-Joy** — the Spirit-fruit of joy is the constitutive Spirit-level element that makes agalliao in suffering possible.

**[CHAR-3]** E — (1) **Gladness is a constituent of worship** — the ki-tov tradition makes accurate evaluation of divine goodness intrinsic to worship; recognising God as good is the cognitive foundation of doxological worship; (2) **The evaluative-gladness faculty is partly constitutive of wisdom** — M04-L-VCG-03 (wisdom's surpassing worth is recognised through the comparative-evaluative faculty of Gladness); (3) **Gladness-as-wellbeing (M04-O-VCG-03) is partly constituted by Delight** (Characteristic 4) — "it is well with him" (Psa 112:5; 128:2) and Delight's satisfaction in what is genuinely good overlap; the boundary is that Gladness is more cognitively-settled and less object-focused than Delight.

**[CHAR-4]** E — (1) **Delight constitutes Love's pleasurable dimension** — Jer 31:20 (sha.a.shu.im alongside "my heart yearns for him"); 1Th 2:8 (affectionate Delight as the pleasurable face of Paul's love for the Thessalonians); Delight is the affective-pleasurable constituent within the broader experience of Love; (2) **Delight constitutes worship's motivational core** — M04-G's Delight in God's word is constitutive of genuine worship; Delight is what makes worship pleasurable and sustained rather than dutiful and intermittent; (3) **Obedience constitutes Delight's obedience-face** — M04-M shows obedience-orientation as a constitutive element of Delight (the soul directed toward what pleases God is the obedience-form of Delight); (4) **Delight is partly constituted by will** — the cha.phets vocabulary makes volitional direction a constitutive element of Delight; Delight without the volitional direction (the will engaged) is merely passive pleasure.

**[CHAR-5]** E — (1) **Pleasure is the experiential face of Gladness** — Psa 133:1 (tov + na.im = Gladness's evaluative-cognitive quality + Pleasure's felt-experiential quality); Pleasure is the felt dimension of what Gladness evaluates; (2) **Pleasure is the sensory-experiential face of Delight** — the a.nog/ta.a.nug/ed.nah vocabulary serves both Delight (specific object-focused treasuring) and Pleasure (ambient sensory ease); M04-K-VCG-02 constitutes a Pleasure dimension partly shared with Delight's luxury register; (3) **Ni.cho.ach-Pleasure constitutes the receptive face of the worship-relationship** — the ni.cho.ach is the experiential-Pleasure dimension of the covenantal worship relationship, which includes also obedience, faith, and covenant faithfulness as its constituent elements.

**[CHAR-6]** E — (1) **Wonder is a constituent of worship** — the VCG-01 proclamatory corpus shows Wonder as constitutive of genuine biblical worship; worship without Wonder is not the characteristic whole-hearted response Scripture describes; (2) **Wonder partially constitutes epistemological humility** — Job 42:3's "things too wonderful for me" contributes to the humility that is constituted by recognising one's cognitive limits before God; (3) **Fear/awe partially constitutes Wonder's VCG-03 register** — dark Wonder is partly constituted by awe-as-dread, though Wonder is the broader term that includes positive astonishment as well.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The constitutive relationships across the cluster reveal a nested architecture: (1) **All seven are constituents of worship** — the cluster as a whole is constitutive of genuine biblical worship; worship without Joy, Gladness, Delight, Wonder, Pleasure, Exultation, and Suffering-Joy is structurally deficient; (2) **Suffering-Joy (Char 7) is partly constituted by Joy (Char 2)** — confirmed at the lexical level by the shared agalliao vocabulary; (3) **Gladness (Char 3) and Pleasure (Char 5) stand in a cognitive/experiential pairing** — Gladness evaluates what is good (cognitive); Pleasure feels what is agreeable (experiential); Pleasure is partly the experiential dimension of what Gladness evaluates; (4) **Delight (Char 4) partly constitutes Love** — it is the pleasurable-attachment dimension of the relational act of love; Love without Delight lacks pleasure; Delight without Love lacks relational commitment; (5) **The Kingdom of God is partly constituted by Joy** — Rom 14:17's "righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit" makes Joy a kingdom-constituent.

findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — CHAR-1 appears to be constitutive of the *conscience* experience in its shame-dimension: conscience's registration of failure *is* the experience of guilt-shame (M07-C). Shame and conscience are not separate — they are the same inner event described from two angles (moral registration vs. felt experience). This constitutive relationship is why the loss of shame = the loss of conscience (Jer 6:15; 8:12).

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 is produced by pride (moral cause, VCG-03), military defeat (political cause, VCG-02), and social community's enacted judgment (social cause, VCG-01). CHAR-2 produces CHAR-1 (the inner shame experience) as its primary downstream consequence, and in extreme cases produces the VCG-04 enduring-burden condition. CHAR-2 is constituted by the mechanism of enforcement — it is definitionally enforced, not chosen.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 is produced by the failure or refusal of the worth-recognition faculty (internal cause) or by sovereign assignment (external cause, VCG-02). CHAR-3 produces CHAR-1 (felt shame) in the dishonoured and can produce CHAR-2 (enforced downward movement of standing) when the worth-denial is enacted through public demotion. CHAR-3 is distinct from but frequently causally connected to CHAR-5.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 is produced by the conscience's engagement with the moral standard. CHAR-4 produces moral conduct (through renunciation) or immoral conduct (through the inverted embrace of the shameful). CHAR-4 constitutes the moral-evaluative component of conscience — it is conscience in its shame-recognitive mode.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 is produced by the contempt-act (M06's characteristic is the producing mechanism; CHAR-5 is its product in the recipient). CHAR-5 produces CHAR-1 (the felt shame-experience) in the recipient. CHAR-5 is a constitutive element of the contempt-shame dynamic: without a recipient who experiences the shame, the contempt remains only in the contempt-er. The dynamic requires both M06 (contempt-er's act) and CHAR-5 (recipient's received shame) to be complete.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 is produced by the sustained moral choices of covenant faithfulness — it is the output of the volitional-moral process of avoiding deliberate wrongdoing. CHAR-6 produces the enabling condition for approach to God (Psa 26:6) — the relational access that guilt-shame would block. CHAR-6 is constitutively the positive pole of the guilt-shame polarity: it is what CHAR-1's M07-C guilt-shame register is the absence of. The two characteristics are structurally opposite: CHAR-6 present = CHAR-1's guilt-shame absent; CHAR-6 absent = CHAR-1's guilt-shame potentially present.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — Primary causal relationships at the cluster level: CHAR-3 and CHAR-5 produce CHAR-1 (dishonour and contempt are upstream causes of the felt shame-experience). CHAR-2 produces CHAR-1 as its inner-experience downstream product. CHAR-4 when absent or inverted enables CHAR-1's seared-conscience form. CHAR-6 when present prevents CHAR-1's guilt-shame form by removing the moral failure that would produce it. Primary constitutive relationships: CHAR-4 and CHAR-6 are the constituting poles of the conscience — CHAR-4 is the conscience's evaluative mode; CHAR-6 is the conscience's integrity mode. Together they constitute the full inner-being conscience-operation: evaluation of the shameful (Char 4), maintenance of innocence that removes guilt from the conscience (Char 6), registration of guilt-shame when moral failure has occurred (Char 1 M07-C). The causal network: Chars 2, 3, 5 are upstream producers of CHAR-1; Chars 4, 6 are the constitutional framework within which all other characteristics operate.
