findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — Two constitutive relationships are evidenced. First, CHAR-1 constitutes the dispositional ground from which CHAR-3 (boasting) emerges as its expressive form: Isa 16:6 (vc=33969, vc=33989, M08-A3-VCG-01) — the pride is the inner root (CHAR-1) from which the boasting is the outer expression (CHAR-3); the two stand in a constitutive relationship as ground and expression. Second, filautos (self-love) constitutes part of CHAR-1's generative base as its root: 2Ti 3:2 (vc=1899) — self-love is the inner orientation that CHAR-1 requires; CHAR-1 is self-love turned outward into competitive self-elevation above others. Additionally, CHAR-1 appears to constitute the dispositional precondition for CHAR-2 (presumptuous defiance — M08-B): the will's settled elevation of self (CHAR-1) is the inner state from which the specific volitional act of defying a divine boundary (CHAR-2) can emerge — CHAR-1 as dispositional ground, CHAR-2 as its activated form in the face of a specific limit.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-1 constitutes part of CHAR-2's substrate: CHAR-2's self-authorising will arises from the elevated self-regard (CHAR-1) that has not been submitted to divine authority. In the opposite direction, CHAR-2 may be a constituent expression of CHAR-1's dispositional energy when it encounters a specific divine limit — CHAR-2 is what CHAR-1's unconstrained volition does when it hits an authority boundary. The relationship is constitutive: CHAR-1 generates the dispositional ground; CHAR-2 is one of its characteristic activations.

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-1 constitutes CHAR-3's dispositional ground (the arrogance from which the boasting emerges). CHAR-3 constitutes the expressive form of CHAR-1 — it is CHAR-1 made public and verbal. The relationship is constitutive in both directions: CHAR-1 provides CHAR-3's inner substrate; CHAR-3 is CHAR-1's outer expression. The VCG-03 form of CHAR-3 may constitute part of M22 (praise/glorying of God) — the God-directed boasting of VCG-03 is adjacent to the praise-register of M22, sharing vocabulary and direction. (See carry-forward observation below.)

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-1 constitutes the dispositional ground of CHAR-4: the same self-elevation that CHAR-1 holds as a general posture, CHAR-4 embodies as a cognitive self-assessment. CHAR-4 is CHAR-1's cognitive sub-form — it is the specific expression of dispositional self-elevation through the mind's self-assessment faculty. CHAR-4 in turn constitutes the inner cognitive stage from which CHAR-3 (verbal boasting) emerges as expression: CHAR-4 is the inner cognitive reality; CHAR-3 is what it produces when verbalized.

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-1 constitutes CHAR-5's dispositional ground: CHAR-5 is the specific form of CHAR-1's dispositional self-elevation when that elevation is mediated through and sustained by structural power. CHAR-5 in turn constitutes a misuse-form of M23 (strength/power/dominion): the cross-register flag (M23) identifies that CHAR-5's primary terms (ga.on proud-might, ma.rom, shal.le.tet, archō) carry their primary register in M23's legitimate strength faculty; CHAR-5 is the corruption of the M23 faculty when that strength becomes the ground for self-aggrandisement. CHAR-5 constitutes the M08 manifestation of the M23 faculty's potential misuse.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The constitutive relationships within M08 form a coherent hierarchy. CHAR-1 constitutes the dispositional ground of the entire cluster. CHAR-2's dispositional substrate is constituted by CHAR-1 (the boiling-will presupposes the elevated self-regard). CHAR-3's alazoneia is constituted by CHAR-1 as its inner source. CHAR-4 is constituted as CHAR-1's cognitive sub-form (the same self-elevation applied to the cognitive faculty). CHAR-5 is constituted as CHAR-1 expressed through the structural-power medium (CHAR-5 = CHAR-1 + structural goods). The cluster-synthesis: M08's constitutive hierarchy is: filautos → CHAR-1 (dispositional core) → CHAR-2 (volitional expression) / CHAR-3 (communicative expression) / CHAR-4 (cognitive sub-form) / CHAR-5 (structural-medium expression).

findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-2]** E — Submission appears to be a *constituent element* of the "obedience of faith" (Rom1:5; 16:26) — a compound that also includes trust (faith) and the cognitive reception of the gospel. Within M09, submission is also partly constituted by humility: Phili2:8 — Christ "humbled himself by becoming obedient" — the self-humbling and the obedience are jointly constitutive of the single kenotic act. The two characteristics (CHAR-1 Humility and CHAR-2 Submission) operate together in Phili2:8 as co-constituents of the single paradigmatic act; neither alone describes the full reality of what Christ did.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Isa57:15 confirms that *lowliness (CHAR-1 Humility) is a constituent element co-present with contrition* — "contrite and lowly in spirit." The two are not identical but are co-constitutive of the inner state of the person before God in their most broken-and-receptive form. Contrition appears as the acute form of humility (Phase 9 CHAR-1 T6.5.1 established this boundary) — the intensity-form that humility takes in the moment of genuine moral crisis. In this sense, contrition is both a distinct characteristic and a constituent of the most intense form of the humility posture.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Metriopatheō (Heb5:2) appears as a *constituent of the mediating-priestly character* in Hebrews — one of the qualities that makes the high priest capable of genuine priestly function. Within M09, the characteristic is the *relational-engagement expression* of the humility register: meekness/gentleness is what humility looks like when it is in the act of dealing with others. In this sense, CHAR-4 is a constituent expression of CHAR-1's self-lowering posture in the specific register of engagement-with-the-erring, rather than a wholly independent characteristic.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Tit2:7 — "show integrity, dignity" — pairs semnotēs with integrity as co-constituents of authentic teaching character. The two together constitute the full character-authenticity of the teacher — integrity is the moral-content dimension; semnotēs is the gravity-manner dimension. The characteristic is thus a *co-constituent* (alongside integrity) of authentic teaching and leadership character, not an isolated quality. It is part of the cluster of character virtues that together constitute genuine godly leadership.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Psa51:12's pairing of joy and willing spirit evidences that joy (M04) and willing-heartedness (CHAR-6) are *co-constituent elements* of the renewed-spirit state that Psa51:12 seeks — neither alone constitutes the full restored inner life; both together constitute the freely-devoted person. Additionally, within M09, willing-heartedness is adjacent to Submission (CHAR-2) as its positive-motivational complement: where submission is the will's yielding to authority, willing-heartedness is the will's free movement toward God. Together they describe two different postures of the yielded will — one responsive-to-command (submission), one spontaneously-generating (willing-heartedness).

**[CHAR-1]** E — Humility appears as a *constituent element* of several wider complexes. Col3:12's character-wardrobe (compassion, kindness, humility, meekness, patience) and Eph4:2 (humility, gentleness, patience, love-bearing) position humility as one constituent in a larger character-complex. The wisdom tradition (Pro11:2) positions humility as a constituent of the wise person's inner-life profile. Conversely, the submission characteristic (CHAR-2) appears to have humility as a constitutive element — submission of will is most genuinely expressed when the inner posture is also humble (Phili2:8 — Christ humbled himself *by becoming obedient*: humility and obedience are jointly constitutive of the single act). The causal-constitutive relationships are bidirectional.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Several constitutive relationships are evidenced within and across characteristics. Humility (CHAR-1) and Submission (CHAR-2) are jointly constitutive of the single Christological act of Phili2:8 — "humbled himself by becoming obedient" — where the inner disposition and the directional yielding cannot be separated; each is a constitutive element of the other in this paradigmatic act. Contrition (CHAR-3) is a constituent expression of Humility (CHAR-1) in its most acute form — Isa57:15 ("contrite and lowly in spirit") names contrition as co-present with lowliness, making contrition the acute-crisis constituent of the humility register. Meekness and Gentleness (CHAR-4) is a constituent expression of CHAR-1's self-lowering posture in the specific register of relational engagement with the erring. Dignity (CHAR-5) is a co-constituent (alongside integrity) of authentic teaching and leadership character (Tit2:7 — "show integrity, dignity"). Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6) is a co-constituent (alongside joy — M04) of the renewed freely-devoted inner life (Psa51:12 — the two are co-restored as parallel gifts). Cluster-level: Phili2:8 is the cluster's most important constitutive verse — it holds CHAR-1 and CHAR-2 as jointly constitutive of a single act, confirming that the cluster's two foundational characteristics are not merely adjacent but mutually constituting in the Christological paradigm.

findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — Wilful sinning is a constituent element of: (1) *CHAR-6 (Habitual defection)*: habitual defection is constituted by repeated wilful sinning that has become a settled pattern — CHAR-1 is the repeated act that constitutes CHAR-6. (2) *CHAR-5 (Refusal to repent)*: refusal to repent presupposes sinning that has occurred — CHAR-1 is the prerequisite event whose un-repented state becomes CHAR-5. Conversely, what constitutes wilful sinning itself is the will (T1.8) operating through the decision-point (T5.2.1) — no single adjacent characteristic constitutes wilful sinning; it is constituted by the will's own choosing.

**[CHAR-10]** E — CHAR-10's three mechanisms are constituent elements of their respective cross-cluster characteristics: deleazō constitutes part of M14 (desire/temptation); sunupokrinomai constitutes part of M08 (pride/hypocrisy); apostasia constitutes part of M31 (faith/unbelief). Within M10, each mechanism is a *route* into the sinning characteristics rather than a constitutive element of them. The cross-cluster flags formalise the constitutive relationships: each mechanism belongs partly to M10 (as a sinful outcome) and partly to its respective cross-cluster (as the mechanism-type).

**[CHAR-11]** E — CHAR-11 is the *foundational constituent* of the entire M10 cluster: every other sinning characteristic presupposes the universal condition as the moral-anthropological ground within which they operate. CHAR-1 (wilful sinning) occurs within CHAR-11; CHAR-5 (refusal to repent) presupposes CHAR-11 as the condition of sin from which departure would be needed; CHAR-8 (political revolt) carries the moral weight of transgression because all transgression ultimately occurs within the universal condition. Within CHAR-11, VCG-01 (wickedness-as-character), VCG-02 (redemption register), and VCG-03 (enslaving power) are its three constituent analytical registers.

**[CHAR-12]** E — CHAR-12 is the *power-register constituent* of CHAR-11 (Sin as universal condition): CHAR-11 encompasses the universal condition in all its registers; CHAR-12 is one specific register of that condition — the active enslaving power dimension. Within CHAR-12, CHAR-6 (habitual practice) constitutes the mechanism through which CHAR-12 is installed; CHAR-6's practice is not merely adjacent but is the formative constituent of CHAR-12's enslavement.

**[CHAR-13]** E — CHAR-13 is a constituent element of the broader concept of moral accountability before God. Within M10, CHAR-13 is the *ledger dimension* that gives CHAR-11 (universal condition), CHAR-1 (wilful sinning), and CHAR-6 (habitual defection) their moral permanence: without the divine record, sins would be transient acts; the record is what makes them moral facts retained before God. Conversely, CHAR-17 (guilt as inner-being state) constitutes the subjective experiential face of CHAR-13's objective reality.

**[CHAR-14]** E — CHAR-14 is a constituent element of M11 (Repentance, Forgiveness, Restoration) — all three VCGs carry the M11 cross-register flag. Within M10, CHAR-14 is the resolution-characteristic that constitutes the reversal of CHAR-13's record and CHAR-11's condition. CHAR-3 (confession) is a partial constituent of CHAR-14's seeking dimension (Exo 32:31 — Moses's verbal naming before God is part of his seeking act).

**[CHAR-15]** E — CHAR-15 is the *temporal-historical constituent* of CHAR-13 (Sin as divine record): the generational accumulation is what gives CHAR-13's record its cross-generational depth (Isa 64:5 — "a long time in our sins"; Isa 43:27 — "your first father sinned"). Within CHAR-15, CHAR-1 (wilful sinning acts) constitutes the mechanism of generational perpetuation: each generation's CHAR-1 acts are the content that fills CHAR-15's inherited framework.

**[CHAR-16]** E — CHAR-16 is the *characterological dimension* of CHAR-11 (sin as universal condition): CHAR-11 is the ontological condition; CHAR-16 is the identity-expression of that condition at the level of recognisable moral character. CHAR-16's VCG-03 (extreme type) is constituted partly by CHAR-6 (habitual defection): the habit of defection forms the extreme-sinner character. CHAR-16's VCG-02 (constituted identity) is constituted partly by CHAR-13's record: the accumulated sin-record (CHAR-13) is what makes the person recognisable as "the sinner."

**[CHAR-17]** E — CHAR-17 is the *subjective-experiential constituent* of CHAR-13's objective-record reality: CHAR-13 (the divine record) is the objective basis; CHAR-17 (guilt-as-inner-state) is the subjective experience of that basis from the inside. Together they are the two dimensions of what being-guilty means: the objective standing before God (CHAR-13) and the inner felt weight of that standing (CHAR-17). CHAR-17 also constitutes an element of CHAR-14 (forgiveness sought and received): the guilt-state is what is addressed when forgiveness is sought; it is the inner experiential content that CHAR-14's seeking and receiving resolve.

**[CHAR-18]** E — CHAR-18 is the *content dimension* of CHAR-13 (sin as divine record): CHAR-13's divine record contains what CHAR-18 names — the accumulated moral crimes that God holds in memory. CHAR-18 is what fills CHAR-13's record. CHAR-18's VCG-02 (generational iniquity — 18 verses) partially overlaps with CHAR-15's concern, but CHAR-15 focuses on the transmission mechanism while CHAR-18 focuses on what is transmitted (the iniquity-content). CHAR-18's VCG-06 (pardon and removal — 21 verses) is the resolution-register that CHAR-14 addresses from the seeking/receiving side.

**[CHAR-19]** E — CHAR-19's VCG-05 (Adam-paradigm paraptōma — 5 verses) is constitutively the origin-event of CHAR-11 (Sin as universal condition): the "one man's trespass" (Rom 5:15/16/17/18) is the foundational boundary-crossing that established the universal sin-condition (CHAR-11). CHAR-19 is thus a constituent element of CHAR-11 at the historical-origin level — CHAR-11's universal condition was created by CHAR-19's paradigmatic first act. CHAR-19's VCG-06 (pardon and erasure — 13 verses) overlaps with CHAR-14's receiving dimension: the transgression-pardon is what CHAR-14 receives.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 is a potential *precursor constituent* of CHAR-4 (Conscience suppression) if the realisation event occurs and the conscience is suppressed rather than responded to. The person who realises inadvertent sin and refuses to acknowledge it moves from CHAR-2 into CHAR-4. CHAR-2 is also a constituent element of the broader sin-cluster's remedial arc (CHAR-3/14/17) — it is the opening event that the arc addresses. Within CHAR-2 itself, the cultic-purification register (VCG-02) and the personal-moral register (VCG-01) are constituent sub-elements sharing vocabulary but differing in inner-being content.

**[CHAR-20]** E — CHAR-20 is the *relational-betrayal dimension* of CHAR-19 in verses where both occur: Hos 6:7 — "they transgressed the covenant; there they dealt faithlessly with me" — CHAR-19 (transgressed) and CHAR-20 (dealt faithlessly) are two analytic faces of the same covenant-breach. CHAR-20's VCG-01 (unfaithfulness toward God) is the sin-dimension that M13 (Truth/Faithfulness) addresses from the positive side and M31 (Faith/Unbelief) addresses from the faith-perspective; CHAR-20 IS the M10 expression of M13's positive characteristic's absence.

**[CHAR-21]** E — CHAR-21 is the *inner-structural foundation* of M10's sin-acts: it is the constitutional distortion from which the sinning acts (CHAR-1), accumulated crimes (CHAR-18), and transgressions (CHAR-19) proceed. The "perverted heart" (Pro 6:14) that devises evil is what underlies and drives all the other M10 characteristics' overt expressions. CHAR-21 is uniquely positioned as M10's constitutional-distortion characteristic: the twisting of the inner moral faculty that generates the other characteristics' expressions.

**[CHAR-22]** E — CHAR-22 is the *conduct-expression dimension* of CHAR-21: the inner structural distortion (CHAR-21 — perverted heart) expresses outward as unjust conduct toward others (CHAR-22 — hands dealing violence). CHAR-22's VCG-03 (character of the unjust person — adikos) is the person-type dimension that M26 (Righteousness/Justice) addresses from its positive side: the adikos is the person whose M26 character is absent. CHAR-22 IS M10's structural opposite of M26's righteousness-characteristic.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Confession is a constituent element of the larger *repentance arc* in Scripture — repentance (the turning of the will) typically includes confession as its verbal component: the turn is named as the person turns (Num 21:7; Judg 10:10/15; Luk 15:21). Confession without the turning produces VCG-03's hollow form; the turn without the verbal naming remains an interior movement not yet completed as confession. The two together constitute repentance. Confession itself has CHAR-17 (guilt) and CHAR-1 (sinning) as constituent prerequisites — without prior sin and guilt there is nothing to confess.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Conscience suppression is a *component dimension* of CHAR-6 (Habitual defection) and CHAR-5 (Refusal to repent) in their advanced forms: the person who habitually defects or persistently refuses to repent necessarily develops some degree of conscience suppression (otherwise the sustained defection/refusal would be intolerable to a fully active conscience). Within CHAR-4 itself, the active-denial mode (Jer 2:35) contains an element of CHAR-1's volitional agency — the denial requires a will-act. The characteristic is thus a site of intersection between conscience failure and volitional rebellion.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Refusal to repent is a constituent element of *CHAR-6 (Habitual defection)*: habitual defection requires not just the single act of sinning but the sustained volitional non-departure that CHAR-5 describes — CHAR-5 is the volitional engine that drives CHAR-6. Refusal to repent also constitutes a dimension of the generational pattern that characterises Israel's history in Kings: the generational perpetuation of Jeroboam's sin is constituted by each generation's refusal to repent. Within CHAR-5 itself, the Heb 10:26 mode constitutes an intensified sub-type: deliberate sinning after full knowledge, which represents the most volitionally accountable form of the characteristic.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Habitual defection is the *formational endpoint* that constitutes the fully developed sinner-type (CHAR-16 — Sinner as moral character): the person-type of Ecclesiastes (Ecc 7:26; 9:2/18; Pro 11:31/13:22) represents the sinner as a constituted moral identity, which is what habitual defection has formed. CHAR-6 thus constitutes CHAR-16 through its formation process. Within CHAR-6 itself, CHAR-1 (each discrete sinning act), CHAR-5 (each refusal to turn), and CHAR-4 (each conscience-numbing) are constituent elements that combine to produce the habitual pattern.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Contagious sin is constituted by three elements from adjacent characteristics: CHAR-1 (the leader's personal sinning — the content of transmission), CHAR-5 (the leader's sustained non-departure — the duration of transmission), and the authority structure (the medium of transmission). CHAR-7 is constitutively distinct from these: it is the specific combination of personal sinning + authority position + Hiphil causative extension to the community. No other characteristic covers this specific combination. CHAR-7 also constitutes the *communal dimension* of CHAR-6: the community's habitual defection in the Kings corpus is largely the product of CHAR-7 transmission from leaders.

**[CHAR-8]** E — Political revolt (CHAR-8) is the *political-register expression* of CHAR-19 (Transgression as deliberate boundary-crossing): both use the pa.sha root in its breaking-away mode, but CHAR-19 applies it in the personal-moral-covenantal domain while CHAR-8 applies it in the political-social domain. CHAR-8 is constitutively a sub-register of the H6586 root's semantic range that CHAR-19 covers in another register. The two are related as registers of the same root rather than as constituent elements of each other.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Sinful speech is a constituent element of CHAR-16 (Sinner as moral character): the practitioner of sustained sinful speech is constituted by it as a sinner-type (2Ti 3:2 — blasphemous character as settled type). Within CHAR-9, the three VCG registers are constituent elements: VCG-01 (slander/abusive speech — person-directed) + VCG-02 (divine-authority usurpation — God-directed judicial) + VCG-03 (constitutive identity-level defiance) together constitute the full characteristic. The M06 cross-register (contempt/hate) constitutes part of VCG-01's affective ground.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Pride functions as a constituent element within wickedness-as-settled-person-identity (Pro 21:4 — VCG-03: "haughty eyes and a proud heart, the lamp of the wicked, are sin"). The practical-atheism dimension (VCG-02) is a structural constituent — the God-exclusion is not merely a consequence but a constitutive feature of the settled wicked person. The iniquity dimension (the wicked person's inner scheming — some verses overlap with M10b-E) is also a partial constituent. Whether wickedness-as-settled-identity is itself a constituent of another broader characteristic is less clear from this evidence — it appears to be a primary category rather than a constituent of a yet-larger characteristic.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The VCG-01 cosmic-evil sub-corpus (13V — INTEGRATION_NOTE) represents the M27 (cosmic/concrete evil) characteristic constituting a partial context for CHAR-2's expression. The evil one's power (1Jo 5:19) and the evil age (Gal 1:4; Eph 5:16) constitute the cosmic environment within which the personal constitutional evil operates. Conversely, the vice-saturation VCG-05 (kakia, ponēria, adikia) shows specific characteristics (malice, wickedness, unrighteousness) as constituent expressions of the constitutional evil — they are the specific forms in which the general constitutional condition manifests. CHAR-2 is constituted by these specific vice-forms while simultaneously being the constitutional ground from which they flow.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The characteristic is constituted in part by multiple upstream inner-being conditions: wickedness (CHAR-1), pride, dishonesty, and the crooked heart are all constituent elements of the situations that trigger the abomination verdict — without these inner conditions, the abomination verdict would not be applied. In this sense, CHAR-3 is a compound verdict that draws its content from multiple other characteristics. CHAR-3 also constitutes the divine-relational dimension of those other characteristics: when CHAR-1 (wickedness) is assessed at the divine-holiness interface, it becomes CHAR-3 — abomination is CHAR-1 seen from God's perspective of active revulsion. The relationship is perspectival: CHAR-1 and CHAR-2 name the human inner condition; CHAR-3 names the divine-relational verdict on those conditions.

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-3 (moral-character abomination) shares the abomination-verdict category with CHAR-4 but constitutes a distinct register. CHAR-4 shares its vocabulary (to.e.vah, shiq.quts) with CHAR-3 — both are instances of the broader abomination category — but CHAR-4's distinguishing constituent is the idolatrous devotion dimension (the heart going after idols, the soul delighting in abominations). The idol-objects named as shiq.quts (foreign deities — 1Ki 11:5; 2Ki 23:13 — VCG-03) are constituent elements of the characteristic's content — they are the specific objects to which false devotion is attached. CHAR-4 is itself constituted by the conjunction of the devotion-capacity (from the image-bearing design) and the false-object (the idol) toward which it is misdirected.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The characteristic shares vocabulary and category with CHAR-1 (wickedness as settled person-identity using ra.sha vocabulary): both address the evildoer-person type but from different angles (CHAR-1 — settled identity; CHAR-5 — active scheming process). CHAR-5's VCG-03 evildoer class (24V) provides the person-type evidence that bridges to CHAR-1; the a.ven vocabulary is distinct from CHAR-1's ra.sha vocabulary, but the evildoer as a character-type overlaps. CHAR-5's VCG-05 (evil deeds register — ro.a) constitutes the expressed-deeds dimension of what CHAR-1 names as the settled wicked character — the deeds are the outward expression of the inner character both characteristics address. CHAR-5 and CHAR-1 are thus constitutively related as process (CHAR-5 — active scheming) and identity (CHAR-1 — settled character), with CHAR-5's VCG-03 and CHAR-1 sharing the evildoer-type.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The blasfēmeō vocabulary is flagged as sharing a cross-register with M06 (contempt / hostile speech / defiant rejection of authority — noted in §2). CHAR-6 and M06 share the speech-defiance domain: CHAR-6 analyses the inner wickedness expressed through speech; M06 analyses the contemptuous hostile speech act as a relational phenomenon. Part of what constitutes CHAR-6 (the contemptuous hostile speech content) is also constitutive of M06 — the characteristics share overlapping content from different analytical angles. The authority-rejection of Jude 8 (VCG-01) is itself a separate characteristic adjacent to CHAR-6 and constitutive of the condition that produces it.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Within the cluster: Char 3 (moral-character abomination) is constitutively applied to Chars 1, 2, and 5 — it functions as a meta-verdict layer that names the divine response to the conditions those three characteristics describe. Char 5's evildoer-class (VCG-03) is conceptually constitutive of Char 1's wicked-person type — the evildoer and the wicked person share the same category, approached from different analytical angles (active process vs. settled identity). Char 6 is constitutively dependent on Chars 1-5 as its inner source — Char 6 can only exist when one of the other five forms of inner evil is present to be expressed through speech. The cluster reveals a nested constitutive structure: Char 2 (constitutional baseline) → Chars 1, 4, 5 (specific inner-evil forms) → Char 3 (divine verdict applied) and Char 6 (speech expression of all five) → downstream consequences.

findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — The 133-verse corpus does not show Characteristic 1 as a constituent of another characteristic. Within the M10c cluster, the four characteristics are separate analytical registers (ritual, moral-inner, corporate-covenantal, external-spiritual) of the broader defilement domain. Characteristic 1 is constituted in part by the clean/unclean categorical system (M12's positive domain defines the negative space that Characteristic 1 inhabits), but M12 is not a constituent element of Characteristic 1 — it is its structural opposite.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The characteristic is constituted in part by desire (M29): the defilement-state is the condition that unchecked desire produces and inhabits. Desire is a constituent vehicle of the characteristic. The characteristic is also constituted by conscience-defilement (1Cor 8:7, VCG-03): the conscience's defiled state is both a part of the characteristic and the characteristic's primary inner faculty engagement. However, neither desire nor conscience-defilement is fully identical with Characteristic 2 — they are contributing constituent elements that together with the will's bondage and the heart's allegiance disorder constitute the full characteristic.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The M10b (abomination) register constitutes a partial overlap with Characteristic 3's Ezekiel idolatry corpus (VCG-02 — the INTEGRATION_NOTE carry-forward). The same acts are simultaneously abominations (M10b) and defilements (Characteristic 3). The two characteristics are not one; they characterise the same acts from different analytical lenses: M10b owns the moral-character assessment (abominable); Characteristic 3 owns the defilement-condition produced by those acts. Neither is a constituent of the other — they co-characterise the same evidence from different angles.

**[CHAR-4]** E — M27 (cosmic-evil agents) constitutes the agency-dimension of Characteristic 4: without the M27 agents there is no Characteristic 4 defilement-state. However, the two are not identical: M27 is broader (cosmic-evil agency in all its forms) while Characteristic 4 is narrower (the specific defilement-condition produced in human persons by those agents). Characteristic 4 is a sub-domain of the consequences of M27's operation.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals constitutive relationships at two boundaries. At the Char 3 / M10b boundary: the Ezekiel idolatry corpus (VCG-02/03 — confirmed by INTEGRATION_NOTE #249) shows the same acts simultaneously owned by M10b (abomination — the moral-character assessment) and Characteristic 3 (defilement — the condition produced by those acts). The two characteristics co-characterise the same evidence from different analytical lenses; neither constitutes the other. At the Char 4 / M27 boundary: M27 (cosmic-evil agents) constitutes the agency-dimension of Characteristic 4 — without M27's agents there is no Characteristic 4 defilement-state. Characteristic 4 is thus analytically a sub-domain of M27's consequences (confirmed by INTEGRATION_NOTE #248). Within the M10c cluster: Characteristic 3 presupposes Characteristic 2 as its generating inner condition — the corporate moral defection (Char 3's outward extension) flows from the community's inner moral corruption (Char 2's domain). This internal constitutive relationship is the cluster's most important structural finding at T6.3.3: Characteristic 3 is generated by and depends on the inner-moral condition that Characteristic 2 owns.

findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — Not applicable.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 is produced by pride (moral cause, VCG-03), military defeat (political cause, VCG-02), and social community's enacted judgment (social cause, VCG-01). CHAR-2 produces CHAR-1 (the inner shame experience) as its primary downstream consequence, and in extreme cases produces the VCG-04 enduring-burden condition. CHAR-2 is constituted by the mechanism of enforcement — it is definitionally enforced, not chosen.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 is produced by the failure or refusal of the worth-recognition faculty (internal cause) or by sovereign assignment (external cause, VCG-02). CHAR-3 produces CHAR-1 (felt shame) in the dishonoured and can produce CHAR-2 (enforced downward movement of standing) when the worth-denial is enacted through public demotion. CHAR-3 is distinct from but frequently causally connected to CHAR-5.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 is produced by the conscience's engagement with the moral standard. CHAR-4 produces moral conduct (through renunciation) or immoral conduct (through the inverted embrace of the shameful). CHAR-4 constitutes the moral-evaluative component of conscience — it is conscience in its shame-recognitive mode.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 is produced by the contempt-act (M06's characteristic is the producing mechanism; CHAR-5 is its product in the recipient). CHAR-5 produces CHAR-1 (the felt shame-experience) in the recipient. CHAR-5 is a constitutive element of the contempt-shame dynamic: without a recipient who experiences the shame, the contempt remains only in the contempt-er. The dynamic requires both M06 (contempt-er's act) and CHAR-5 (recipient's received shame) to be complete.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 is produced by the sustained moral choices of covenant faithfulness — it is the output of the volitional-moral process of avoiding deliberate wrongdoing. CHAR-6 produces the enabling condition for approach to God (Psa 26:6) — the relational access that guilt-shame would block. CHAR-6 is constitutively the positive pole of the guilt-shame polarity: it is what CHAR-1's M07-C guilt-shame register is the absence of. The two characteristics are structurally opposite: CHAR-6 present = CHAR-1's guilt-shame absent; CHAR-6 absent = CHAR-1's guilt-shame potentially present.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — Primary causal relationships at the cluster level: CHAR-3 and CHAR-5 produce CHAR-1 (dishonour and contempt are upstream causes of the felt shame-experience). CHAR-2 produces CHAR-1 as its inner-experience downstream product. CHAR-4 when absent or inverted enables CHAR-1's seared-conscience form. CHAR-6 when present prevents CHAR-1's guilt-shame form by removing the moral failure that would produce it. Primary constitutive relationships: CHAR-4 and CHAR-6 are the constituting poles of the conscience — CHAR-4 is the conscience's evaluative mode; CHAR-6 is the conscience's integrity mode. Together they constitute the full inner-being conscience-operation: evaluation of the shameful (Char 4), maintenance of innocence that removes guilt from the conscience (Char 6), registration of guilt-shame when moral failure has occurred (Char 1 M07-C). The causal network: Chars 2, 3, 5 are upstream producers of CHAR-1; Chars 4, 6 are the constitutional framework within which all other characteristics operate.

---

questions.section: T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics
questions.question_text: Which vocabulary terms, if any, does this characteristic share with other characteristics in the programme? Record none if none is shown.
questions.review_note: Stage 1 supplies the raw strong_related pull; cross-referencing which characteristic each related code belongs to needs Stage 2's own input-assembly linkage — a genuine two-stage dependency, not purely Stage 1.

findings.session_b_note:
The registry records zero shared terms (shared_term_count: 0; term_sharing_ratio: 0.0). However, this requires careful interpretation:

The formal shared_term_count measures terms that are XREF-linked across registries in the database. The zero count means **no term is formally classified as shared (XREF) with another registry**. This does not mean the vocabulary has no overlap at the root or semantic level — it means the formal cross-reference mechanism has not been applied.

**The significant vocabulary overlap at the structural level:**
- G0863H (afiēmi — forgive): the same root as G0863G (leave/forsake) and G0863I (permit/allow) — all three are variations of aphiēmi and all three appear in this registry. The root generates three distinct semantic directions within a single registry.
- H5545 (sa.lach) appears exclusively in this registry within the programme — no other registry uses this root.
- G0859 (afesis) — the noun form of the releasing-act — is the primary NT forgiveness noun and appears to be registry-exclusive in the programme.

OBS-064-011 and OBS-064-012 address vocabulary sharing through co-occurrence rather than formal XREF sharing. The 25 co-occurrence pairs reviewed in the Session B analysis identified structural connections through shared verses rather than shared terms.

findings.finding_value: T6 as a whole reveals that goodness is structurally one of the most connected characteristics in the programme — both in co-occurrence breadth (top-25 co-occurrence list spanning the full dimensional spectrum), shared anchor density (7 shared anchors including the two highest-density synthesis nodes in the programme: Mic 6:8 and Gal 5:22), and root-level vocabulary sharing across three root families (TOV, AGATHO, CHRESTO) distributed across multiple registries. The structural picture confirms what T1 indicated definitionally: goodness is not a specialist characteristic but one that permeates and connects the whole inner-being landscape. The most significant T6 finding is the dual constitutive relationship (Q&A-152): goodness is simultaneously a constituent of the Spirit-fruit whole (Gal 5:22) and itself constituted by a tri-fold structure (Mic 6:8). This means goodness has both a containing relationship (it is part of something larger — Spirit-formed character) and an internal structure (it contains three orientations — justice, kindness, humility). The boundary distinctions (T6.5) remain the weakest component — all three nearest-neighbour boundaries (love, kindness, generosity) require Session D cross-registry synthesis. The R187 (strength) co-occurrence anomaly at 32 shared verses remains an open question for Session D (SP-067-027).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-017: T2 confirmed that goodness's origin is singular (God) but its delivery is multiple (encounter, word, Spirit). T6 confirmed that goodness's vocabulary is distributed across multiple registries through …
findings.finding_value: T2 confirmed that goodness's origin is singular (God) but its delivery is multiple (encounter, word, Spirit). T6 confirmed that goodness's vocabulary is distributed across multiple registries through shared root families. These two findings are structurally related: the vocabulary distribution (T6.4 — TOV root to R103, AGATHO root to R65, CHRESTO root to R99) reflects the multiple delivery mechanisms of T2. The TOV root's distribution to love (R103) corresponds to the encounter-relational delivery mechanism; the AGATHO root's distribution to generosity (R65) corresponds to the action-expression level of the constitutional movement; the CHRESTO root's shared presence across R67 and R99 corresponds to the dispositional-kindness register of chrēstotēs. The vocabulary distribution is not arbitrary — it tracks the constitutional and relational architecture of how goodness operates and reaches the person. The single-origin of goodness (T2.9.2) is expressed through a vocabulary distributed across the programme's relational-characteristic cluster, reflecting the multiple pathways of the one goodness.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-028: T6 confirmed that goodness has the most extensive vocabulary-sharing and cross-registry connection pattern of any characteristic analysed so far in the programme. T7 confirms through the vocabulary ar…
findings.finding_value: T6 confirmed that goodness has the most extensive vocabulary-sharing and cross-registry connection pattern of any characteristic analysed so far in the programme. T7 confirms through the vocabulary arc (Q&A-177) that this extensiveness is a lexical reality, not a programme classification artefact: the three root families (TOV, AGATHO, CHRESTO) each generate multiple terms distributed across multiple registries because the semantic ranges genuinely overlap. The vocabulary sharing (T6.4) is not the result of how the programme has drawn its boundaries — it reflects the actual lexical distribution of the Hebrew and Greek goodness vocabulary, which crosses conceptual boundaries that English vocabulary maintains more distinctly. The three-stage vocabulary arc (H2896A breadth → agathōsunē precision → chrēstotēs precision) tracks the same movement as the cross-registry distribution pattern: H2896A generates the widest distribution (TOV root to R103, to R42, to multiple other registries); the NT precision terms (G0019, G5544) generate narrower distributions (R65 and R99 respectively). As the vocabulary narrows to precision, the cross-registry connections narrow correspondingly. T6's structural pattern and T7's lexical arc describe the same underlying phenomenon: goodness vocabulary begins broad and specialises, and its cross-registry connections follow the same trajectory.

findings.finding_value: Love's structural position in the programme is that of the central node in the inner-being vocabulary's relational architecture. Co-occurrence data: 196 with compassion, 105 with strength, 68 with peace, 62 with faith — confirming love's connections to the full range of C17 characteristics and extending to C20 (strength/authority). Shared anchor data: 48 verses shared across multiple registries, with Exo 34:6 (5 registries) and Gal 5:22 (5 registries) as the highest-density shared anchors — confirming love as the vocabulary cluster around which the programme's most significant cross-registry verses gather. Sequential position: love stands downstream of divine action (received) and upstream of the ethical-moral life (generative of commandment-keeping, Spirit-fruits, community identity). Causal productivity: love generates joy, rest, grief, obedience, praise — the programme's most causally productive characteristic. Vocabulary sharing: term sharing ratio 0.701, the highest in C17 — love shares vocabulary with compassion, mercy, kindness, goodness, desire, and peace. The primary gap: distinctions from adjacent characteristics (compassion, mercy, kindness) remain partially drawn; Session D is the resolution context.

findings.finding_value: Love's definition as the programme's most semantically comprehensive inner-being characteristic is confirmed and deepened by the structural relationship analysis. The term sharing ratio (0.701 — highest in C17) and the co-occurrence breadth (196 with compassion through to 29 with mercy) reflect the definition's conclusion: love is not a bounded standalone characteristic but the semantic centre of a cluster. The sequential finding (love as mediating-and-generative node — Q&A-105) maps onto the definition's tripartite structure: love is downstream (condition-received from God), central (disposition that organises), and upstream (act that generates all subsequent ethical life). The definition's vocabulary arc (from divine being to love of darkness — Q&A-131) is confirmed by the structural relationship data: the vocabulary extends into every adjacent registry (through XREF sharing, co-occurrence, and shared anchors), touching every corner of the programme. The structural analysis thus confirms the definitional claim: love is not merely a characteristic among others but the organising principle of the inner-being vocabulary.

findings.finding_value: Love's comprehensive constitutional location (all five levels) is structurally consistent with its position as the programme's central co-occurrence node. A characteristic that operates at every constitutional level will co-occur with the broadest range of other characteristics — because any verse that names soul, heart, mind, spirit, or body is potentially within love's evidential terrain. The co-occurrence breadth (top 25 covering registries from C17 through C20 and beyond) reflects the constitutional breadth: strength and authority (C20) co-occur with love because the same verses that address God's inner character include both love and power vocabulary — the divine portrait (Exo 34:6) is constitutionally comprehensive. The vocabulary sharing ratio (0.701 — highest in C17) similarly reflects the constitutional comprehensiveness: love shares vocabulary with compassion (at the somatic/racham level), with goodness (at the heart/tov level), with desire (at the ahav/phileō root level), with peace (at the soul-rest level). Constitutional breadth and vocabulary breadth are the same phenomenon viewed from different angles.

findings.finding_value: The structural relationship data and the evidential foundation are the most mutually confirming pair in the synthesis matrix. The co-occurrence breadth (T6.1) is directly explained by the vocabulary breadth (T7.1.10 — the widest semantic arc in the programme): a vocabulary that spans from divine being to love of darkness will co-occur with every other inner-being characteristic because it occupies every register of the inner-being vocabulary. The shared anchor density (48 verses — T6.6) is explained by the primary anchor's function (Lam 3:22 — T7.2.5/T7.2.6): the programme anchors the most significant cross-registry verses at love because love is the definitional centre from which adjacent characteristics derive their meaning. The vocabulary sharing ratio (0.701 — T6.4) is explained by the root-level connections (T7.1.2): the racham root connects love, compassion, and mercy; the ahav root connects love and desire; the tov root connects love and goodness. The structural relationship data is, at its core, the observable programme-level effect of the lexical architecture that the evidential foundation analysis reveals. Structural breadth and lexical breadth are the same reality at different levels of analysis.

The T6 synthesis: mercy functions as the structural integrator of the inner-being relational economy — it is the characteristic through which negative conditions are bridged to positive states across the widest range of cross-registry connections in C17.

The co-occurrence pattern places contrition at the nexus of heart (R183), fear (R061), pride (R123), sorrow (R151), and fellowship (R062) — all meeting in contrition's primary anchor verses. The causal structure is rich: contrition is causally produced by divine-human encounter; it causally produces divine nearness; it is constitutive of genuine repentance (R135). The vocabulary is sufficiently distinctive (dkh/ktt/nkh root families) that contrition maintains lexical identity even amid these structural connections. The shared anchor analysis confirms Isa 57:15 as the convergence verse — simultaneously registering in divine identity, human moral failure, and creaturely posture registers. T6 synthesis: contrition is a structurally central characteristic that connects multiple inner-being registers (dependence, fear, pride, heart, sorrow, fellowship) while maintaining a distinctive vocabulary and position as the penitential sub-form of creaturely dependence before God.

findings.finding_value: T6 reveals compassion as the structural centre of the C17 cluster rather than a peripheral member. The love co-occurrence (196/351 = 55.8% of all OWNER verses) is uniquely dominant — compassion and love co-occur in more than half of all active verses, raising the programme-level question whether they are truly separable at the data level. Three structural observations from the co-occurrence landscape: (1) compassion sits at C17's centre of gravity (love, mercy, kindness as top three co-occurrences — all within-cluster); (2) compassion generates a human-response cluster (peace, faith, will, surrender, seeking co-occurring at significant levels — the pattern of divine compassion generating human inner-being responses); (3) compassion is constitutively responsive to human distress (despair, guilt, distress, evil all present in the co-occurrence table — compassion operates most characteristically in the presence of need). The CHASAD root crossing compassion (C17) and shame (C06) is the programme's most structurally unexpected finding — a root family that bridges two clusters. Exod 34:6 as the programme's most multiply-anchored verse (6 registries) must be treated as a cluster-level synthesis anchor. The compassion/mercy boundary (SD-009) is the most critical unresolved distinction. T6.7 (dimensional sharing) is programme-stage limited — formally deferred.

T2's constitutional portrait (soul-body interface) is the constitutional ground for the root-level cluster-crossing that T6 identifies.

findings.finding_value: T6 produces the most structurally significant finding in the review set for any single tier: grace is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic. It is the originating point of a causal chain, not its product. This categorically distinguishes grace from every other characteristic reviewed — all others can be produced by at least one other characteristic; grace cannot. This structural uniqueness is confirmed by T2.9's origin analysis (grace originates with God — it does not originate in the human constitutional system) and is analytically consistent across T6.2 (seeking is the posture before grace arrives, not its producer), T6.3 (S-rating on "is grace produced by another characteristic"), and T6.4 (the vocabulary's structural completeness without a generative human-side term). The co-occurrence pattern reveals grace at the intersection of divine initiative and creaturely need: seeking (R140 — 40 verses, dominant) as the creature's pre-grace posture; moral failure cluster (evil, guilt, sin, transgression) as the creaturely context; power cluster (strength, might) confirming the 2Cor 12:9 connection. The love co-occurrence (R103 — 14 verses) is the primary within-cluster signal raising the grace-love boundary question (SD013). All major boundary distinctions (grace-love, grace-mercy, grace-justice, grace-chesed) remain open at T6.5 — the most unresolved boundary cluster in the review set. T6.7 (dimensional sharing) is programme-stage limited.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-017: T2's constitutional origin finding (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system) and T6's structural uniqueness finding (grace is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic) …
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional origin finding (grace does not originate in the human constitutional system) and T6's structural uniqueness finding (grace is not produced by any other inner-being characteristic) are the same finding from constitutional and structural perspectives. They confirm each other from different analytical directions: T2 establishes that there is no constitutional source for grace within the human person; T6 establishes that there is no characteristic-level source for grace within the programme's inner-being landscape. The vocabulary's structural completeness (T7 — but relevant here as T6.4) reflects this constitutional uniqueness: because grace originates entirely from outside the human system, its vocabulary must encode the full two-sided circuit (giving and receiving) from within a single root, with no gap left for a generative human-side term.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-028: T6's structural uniqueness (grace is not produced by any inner-being characteristic — categorically the originating point of the causal chain) and T7's vocabulary structural completeness (every dimens…
findings.finding_value: T6's structural uniqueness (grace is not produced by any inner-being characteristic — categorically the originating point of the causal chain) and T7's vocabulary structural completeness (every dimension of grace's operation has a corresponding term, including the structural negative acharistos) confirm and explain each other. T6 establishes that grace stands outside the characteristic-production network; T7 establishes that the vocabulary encodes this structural position with unique completeness — including the negative (acharistos) and the NT coinage (charitoō) as markers of grace's conceptual uniqueness. The shared anchor verses (T6.6) are also T7's most evidentially rich texts: Eph 2:8 (which anchors multiple co-occurring registries) carries the most complete single-verse expression of grace's structural position (sovereign gift, not of works, producing faith). T6 and T7 mutually confirm that grace's structural uniqueness in the programme landscape corresponds to a lexical uniqueness in the vocabulary — both point to the same underlying analytical claim: grace is categorically distinct from every other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-099-006: T6 reveals that kindness sits at the structural centre of a dense network of related characteristics rather than on the edge. Its most consistent co-occurrences (faithfulness, justice, compassion, for…
findings.finding_value: T6 reveals that kindness sits at the structural centre of a dense network of related characteristics rather than on the edge. Its most consistent co-occurrences (faithfulness, justice, compassion, forgiveness, humility, patience) are not merely adjacent virtues but appear to be partially constituent of kindness itself — the Mic 6:8 triad (justice/kindness/humility) and the Eph 4:32 cluster (kindness/tenderheartedness/forgiveness) function as composite wholes where each element reinforces and partly defines the others. The causal network is explicit and directional: divine kindness → praise + repentance in the recipient → reproduced human kindness toward others → sustained covenant relationships. This causal chain means kindness is not only a characteristic that one possesses but one that is structurally self-propagating through its own operation. The semantic-root finding is analytically significant: the CHESED root family spans the noun (chesed — kindness), the verb (chasad — be kind), the person (chasid — the kind one), the negative (shame/reproach for its failure), and a proper name (Chesed) — a root family that covers definition, action, identity, consequence, and proper-noun instantiation within a single family. T6's most significant intra-tier finding: Mic 6:8 anchors eight registries simultaneously, which confirms that kindness is not a standalone quality but a node in a structural web of C17 cluster characteristics — its full meaning requires these other registries to be seen.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-021: T3's finding that kindness engages volition, agency, and conscientiousness as an integrated whole maps onto T6's causal network in a specific way: it is precisely these three faculties operating toget…
findings.finding_value: T3's finding that kindness engages volition, agency, and conscientiousness as an integrated whole maps onto T6's causal network in a specific way: it is precisely these three faculties operating together that make the T6 causal chain function. The T6 finding that received human kindness causes its reproduction (2Sa 10:2 — "as his father dealt loyally with me, so I will deal loyally") requires all three: the cognition (knowing what was done), the moral evaluation (recognising the obligation), and the agency (acting on it). The T6 co-occurrence finding that kindness clusters with faithfulness, patience, and humility maps onto T3's multi-faculty profile: faithfulness requires conscientiousness; patience requires impulse-control at the volitional level; humility requires conscience and moral evaluation. The T3 finding that imagination and creativity are absent connects with T6's finding that kindness is a central node in a relational-moral web — it is constitutively oriented toward the actual other, not toward the imagined or created.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-024: T4's relational circuit and T6's structural network overlap most clearly at the causal level. The T6 causal network (divine kindness → praise + repentance → reproduced human kindness → sustained coven…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational circuit and T6's structural network overlap most clearly at the causal level. The T6 causal network (divine kindness → praise + repentance → reproduced human kindness → sustained covenant relationships) is a structural description of the T4 circuit in causal terms: T4 identifies the directions; T6 names the causal mechanism connecting them. The T6 finding that Mic 6:8 anchors eight registries is a cluster-level reflection of T4's circuit: Mic 6:8's triadic requirement (do justice / love kindness / walk humbly) is addressed to the covenant community's relational practice — it describes the T4 relational interface requirements in condensed form. The T6 finding that kindness is self-propagating through the causal chain (received kindness → reproduced kindness) is the structural guarantee that the T4 circuit is not a closed loop requiring constant external input but a self-sustaining relational ecosystem once kindness is received and given. The T4 finding that the spiritual beings interface is absent (Q&A-070) is consistent with T6's causal analysis: the causal chain operates within the human-divine-communal relational web, not across spiritual-ontological boundaries.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-028: T6's structural relationship findings and T7's lexical and literary findings are mutually confirming at the level of the semantic root. The T6 finding that the CHESED root family covers noun (chesed),…
findings.finding_value: T6's structural relationship findings and T7's lexical and literary findings are mutually confirming at the level of the semantic root. The T6 finding that the CHESED root family covers noun (chesed), verb (chasad), person (chasid), shame-negative (H2617B), and proper noun (Chesed) is a T7 lexical observation that has structural significance: a root family that spans all these categories is not merely a lexical curiosity but evidence that kindness (as the CHESED root names it) is a comprehensive inner-being reality — it has a noun form (what it is), a verb form (what it does), a person form (who embodies it), a consequence form (what happens when it fails), and a proper-noun instantiation (when it names a person). The T6 co-occurrence finding that kindness clusters with faithfulness, justice, and compassion maps directly onto the T7 semantic range finding that chesed itself encompasses goodness/kindness/faithfulness — the co-occurrence cluster is partly a reflection of the internal semantic complexity of chesed: different registries are studying different dimensions of what is, in the original Hebrew, a single concept. T7's primary anchor verse (Lam 3:22) is T6's most significant causal statement: the inexhaustibility of chesed (T7) is the precondition for the causal chain's stability (T6) — if chesed could run out, the chain would break.

T6's trust → peace causal sequence (Q&A-148/149) maps onto T1's "covenant → gift → inner condition" — trust is the human act that enables reception of the divine gift. T6's reconciliation-constitutes-peace finding (Q&A-153) maps onto T1's eschatological dimension — the cross-accomplished peace (T1 dimension 4) is what reconciliation produces. The shared anchor network (59 relationships across 43 registries) confirms that T1's four dimensions are each structurally connected to multiple other registries — peace is not self-contained but embedded in the programme's full inner-being ecosystem.

findings.finding_value: T2's body evidence (Psa 38:3 — no sha.lom in bones because of sin) connects directly to T6's finding that reconciliation constitutes relational peace (Col 1:20, Eph 2:14) — the same sha.lom that is absent from bones when sin is present is the sha.lom that reconciliation restores. The SHA.L root (T6.4.2) names completeness — and Psa 38:3's use of sha.lom for somatic soundness is directly rooted in this: sha.lom IS somatic completeness, sha.lom IS relational completeness, sha.lom IS covenantal completeness — one root, all dimensions. The constitutional and structural analyses confirm the same root-level truth from different angles.

findings.finding_value: T3's volitional finding (peace is chosen and refused, T3.6) connects to T6's causal sequences (trust → peace, T6.2) — trust is the volitional act that enables the causal chain; the refusal of peace (Isa 30:15) is the volitional act that interrupts it. T3's conscience-gateway finding (T3.9) connects to T6's peace-is-produced-by findings (T6.3.2 — confession produces peace) — conscience exercise is the specific faculty engagement that makes the Psa 32 causal sequence possible. T3's moral evaluation finding (T3.8 — authentic peace enables right judgment) connects to T6's shared anchor Isa 59:8 (the way of peace they do not know) — the morally disordered person cannot find the peace-way because moral disorder corrupts the evaluative faculty.

findings.finding_value: T4's God-to-human direction and T6's causal sequences describe the same reality at different levels of abstraction. T4.1 (God gives peace through covenant/Christ/Spirit) is the relational description of what T6.3.2 catalogues as causal inputs (trust, righteousness, discipline, Spirit, confession, love of law all produce peace). The covenant-of-peace (T4.1 — Isa 54:10) is the relational framework for what T6.4.2 names as the SHA.L root shared between peace and covenant at the structural level. The two analyses are not parallel but nested: T4 names the relational direction; T6 names the structural mechanism through which that direction operates.

findings.finding_value: T5's developmental findings and T6's structural relationships describe the same causal network at different scales of analysis. T5's sequences (trust → peace → strength, T5.2) and T6's causal chains (trust → peace → strength, T6.2) are identical — T5 describes the temporal unfolding; T6 describes the structural relationship. T5's finding that peace is both condition and fruit of sanctification (T5.5) maps onto T6's finding that peace has multiple causal inputs (trust, righteousness, discipline, Spirit) and multiple causal outputs (strength, joy, stability, righteousness-harvest) — the sanctification arc is the time-extended version of the causal network. T5's irreversibility finding (Isa 54:10) maps onto T6's constitutive relationship: reconciliation constitutes peace (T6.3.3) — the accomplished peace is irreversible because reconciliation is accomplished.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-117-021: T6's structural relationships and T7's lexical foundation are the most directly complementary tiers in the analysis. T6's root-level finding (SHA.L shared with R34 covenant, T6.4.2) is validated and g…
findings.finding_value:
T6's structural relationships and T7's lexical foundation are the most directly complementary tiers in the analysis. T6's root-level finding (SHA.L shared with R34 covenant, T6.4.2) is validated and grounded by T7's etymology (T7.1.1 — SHA.L root meaning completeness-wholeness-settlement; sha.lam = to pay in full). The root-level semantic bond between peace and covenant (T6) is not lexical coincidence but semantic identity: they share the same root because they name the same underlying reality from different angles — the covenant is the relational structure of completeness; shalom is the experiential condition of completeness. T6's shared anchor network (59 relationships, T6.6) is confirmed as structurally grounded by T7's lexical richness (10 vocabulary dimensions, person-type terms, supplication terms, antonym vocabulary) — the wide vocabulary arc (T7) generates the wide structural network (T6).

findings.finding_value: Chesed is shared across M05-A and M05-D (kindness) — the same root family generates terms in both love and kindness registries. The ra.cham/rachamim family overlaps with M05-B. The philo- compounds are the widest vocabulary family in the cluster.
Ra.cham/rachamim vocabulary overlaps with M05-A (love family via womb-root). Splanchnon (bowel/affection) overlaps with M05-G (Phili 2:1 — Group 1055 — "any affection and sympathy").
Eleos vocabulary is primarily bounded within M05-C. The overlap with the broader mercy/compassion semantic field is at the conceptual rather than primary-vocabulary level.
Agathos root family is broadly distributed across M05-D and appears in M05-G (Phile 6 — Group 1056: "knowledge of every good thing"). Chrēstotēs is concentrated within M05-D.
Praotēs/praus vocabulary is concentrated within M05-E. The epieikeia/epieikēs vocabulary is also concentrated.

Na.cham vocabulary shares the OT compassion/pity register with M05-B (na.cham used for divine compassion alongside ra.cham). Parakaleō/paraklēsis vocabulary overlaps with M05-G (Phili 2:1 — Group 1055) and M05-B (2Cor 1:7 — Group 1057).
Koinōn- vocabulary is concentrated within M05-G. The epoikodomeō term overlaps with M05-F's community-building context.

The most significant cross-sub-group vocabulary sharing is at the OT level: the chesed and ra.cham root families both span multiple sub-groups (A, B, D for chesed; B, F for na.cham). The NT vocabulary is more sub-group-bounded. G-codes T6.4.3 (cross-registry chesed distribution), T6.6.3 (anchor verse cross-registry overlaps), and T6.7.3 (dimensional overlap counts) are raised for CC to provide the quantitative cross-programme picture.

**[CLUSTER]** E. Key shared vocabulary:
- **ne.phesh (H5315)** — appears in Eze 18:20 (M26-A2-002) in the "the soul who sins shall die" clause. Ne.phesh is the primary term in the Soul cluster (C15/R109) and in numerous other clusters. Its appearance here is not as a characterisation of righteousness's location but as the holistic-person reference ("the person who sins"). Cross-cluster vocabulary sharing at the ne.phesh level.
- **lev (H3820)** / **le.vav (H3824)** — heart terms appear repeatedly in connection with righteousness (the hard heart of Rom 2:5; the law written on the heart, VSG M26-A2-005). The heart vocabulary is shared with every cluster that engages heart-level characteristics.
- **mish.pat (H4941)** — justice/judgment term appears across M26 as the most frequent co-occurrence partner. This term likely appears in a distinct cluster of its own (judicial/justice family). Vocabulary sharing is extensive.
- **logizomai (G3049)** — the reckoning term in F. This term may appear in other clusters where counting, crediting, or reasoning is involved (e.g., conscience material, moral evaluation material in other clusters).
- **suneidesis** — sunoida (G6083, conscience-adjacent, appears in the unrouted verse 1Cor 4:4 in this cluster) shares vocabulary with the conscience cluster.

findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. (1) *Ka.lam* (H3637) appears in M07-D (humiliation as enforced abasement) as well as CHAR-1 — it spans the inner experience (CHAR-1) and the enforced outer movement (CHAR-2). (2) *Qa.lon* (H7036) appears in M07-E (dishonour) as well as CHAR-1 — it spans the relational-worth-denial dimension and the inner moral-consequence dimension. (3) *Atimazō* (G0818) appears in M07-E and CHAR-1 — dishonour as relational act and as experienced inner wound. (4) *Kataischunō* (G2617) spans CHAR-1 (the experience) and M07-G (contempt producing shame). Vocabulary sharing is extensive because shame's inner experience, outer abasement, relational worth-denial, and contempt-mechanism are all connected phenomena sharing root words.

**[CHAR-2]** E — CHAR-2 shares vocabulary significantly with CHAR-1: ka.lam, bosh, bo.shet, ke.lim.mah all appear in both. The distinction is the verse-emphasis: when the term names the enforced outer mechanism, it is CHAR-2; when it names the felt inner collapse, it is CHAR-1. Vocabulary sharing reflects the fact that inner and outer are aspects of the same shame-event differently observed.

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 shares atimazō and atimia with CHAR-1 (where these terms name the felt experience of dishonour) and with CHAR-2 (where they name the enforced downward movement). The head-covering kataischunō (1Cor 11:4-5) appears in CHAR-1 for the shame-experience register and in CHAR-3 for the relational-disrespect register. Vocabulary sharing is significant and reflects the close analytical relationship between the cluster's characteristics.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 shares aischunē (G0152) with CHAR-1 (where it names the felt experience vs. CHAR-4 where it names the moral quality of conduct — 2Cor 4:2; Phili 3:19). CHAR-4 shares atimia (G0819) with CHAR-1 and CHAR-3 (where it names the relational worth-denial vs. CHAR-4 where it names the quality of disordered passions). The vocabulary sharing reflects the semantic overlap between the shameful quality and the shame-experience in the biblical vocabulary.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 shares exoutheneō with M06's contempt vocabulary. Atimazō (G0818) is shared with CHAR-3 (dishonour). The vocabulary sharing confirms that CHAR-5 is analytically positioned at the intersection of contempt (M06) and dishonour (CHAR-3): it is the received form of the contempt-act, experienced as worth-denial.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 shares its vocabulary (niq.qa.von, qe.ha.von) with M12 (purity/holiness) as the terms' primary register. This is the principal vocabulary-sharing relationship for CHAR-6: the same terms that name CHAR-6's inner-moral-innocence function are also the primary vocabulary of M12's purity register. The sharing reflects the fact that CHAR-6 is retained in M07 because of its shame-polarity function, while M12 holds the terms in their primary purity-holiness register.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's vocabulary sharing confirms the analytical distinctness of the six despite their shared semantic field. Most significant shared vocabulary: atimazō/atimia appears in Chars 1, 2, and 3 — naming the inner experience, the outer mechanism, and the relational act respectively. Aischunē appears in Chars 1 and 4 — the felt experience vs the evaluative quality. Exoutheneō appears in Chars 3 and 5 — worth-denial and contempt-dismissal overlap. The bosh-family (primarily Char 1, with secondary presence in Chars 2 and 4) is the cluster's most widely distributed primary family. Vocabulary sharing is extensive but analytical distinctness is maintained by verse-emphasis: the same term names the inner experience (Char 1), the outer mechanism (Char 2), the relational act (Char 3), the evaluative quality (Char 4), or the contempt-source (Char 5). The programme's characteristic structure imposes the analytical distinctions that the vocabulary does not make on its own.

findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The primary vocabulary terms of CHAR-1 are shared with at least two other clusters. First, M22 (Divine Majesty and Exaltation): rum (H7311A) spans both CHAR-1's human self-elevation register and M22's divine exaltation register — confirmed by the Phase 5.5 set-aside of 122 M22-register verses from rum, ga.on, ga.vah, ga.a.vah, ge.ut, go.vah, ga.ah. The same Hebrew terms that name God's legitimate exaltation (M22) also name the creature's illegitimate self-elevation (M08/CHAR-1). Second, M09 (Humility): huperēfanos (G5244) appears in M08-A4-VCG-01 (CHAR-1's arrogance) and in Jam 4:6 and 1Pe 5:5 where it is placed directly against M09's tapeinophrosynē (humility) — the vocabulary of CHAR-1 is definitionally entangled with the vocabulary of M09. Third, ga.on (H1347) spans M08's national-pride register and M22's divine-glory register (the 122 M22 set-asides included ga.on as a term with dual-register function).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The primary zid/za.don/zed vocabulary of CHAR-2 is largely distinctive to M08-B within the M08 cluster — it does not span multiple clusters in the way CHAR-1's rum/ga.on vocabulary does. However, za.don/zed/zid carry both the M08-B (presumptuous defiance) register and an adjacent arrogance register that overlaps with CHAR-1 at the edges: Isa 13:11 (vc=34104, M08-B-VCG-02): "the arrogant [zed] person" appears in a verse whose broader context also carries CHAR-1 material. The Greek authadēs (G0829) and tolmētēs (G5113) are not evidenced in other M08 characteristics' vocabulary sets in the current corpus.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes, extensively. The kauchaomai family (kauchaomai/kauchēma/kauchēsis) spans all three of CHAR-3's VCGs and crosses the M08–M22 boundary: the same verb that names self-directed condemned boasting (VCG-01) also names God-directed glorying (VCG-03) and Pauline examined self-commendation (VCG-02). The ha.lal root similarly spans M08's self-boasting sense (VCG-01) and M22's praise-of-God register (the 22 ha.lal praise verses in M22). This is the most extensive vocabulary sharing in M08: CHAR-3 shares its primary vocabulary with M22 (Divine Praise and Thanksgiving) at the root level.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The primary fusioō/tufoō/huperfroneō vocabulary of CHAR-4 is largely distinctive within M08. Fusioō does not appear in CHAR-1's rum/ga.on vocabulary set or in CHAR-2's zid/za.don vocabulary — it is specific to the cognitive-inflation register. Huperfroneō (to think above) belongs to the same huper- prefix family as huperēfanos (above + appear — CHAR-1's Greek vocabulary), suggesting root-level proximity without term-sharing. The conceptual overlap between CHAR-1's self-elevation and CHAR-4's cognitive self-inflation is confirmed by the shared huper- prefix etymology.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes, extensively. Ga.on (H1347) spans M08-CHAR-5 (proud-might subset) and M22 (divine majesty — confirmed by the 122 M22-register ga.on/rum set-aside at Phase 5.5). Ma.rom (H4791) spans M08-CHAR-5 (fortified-elevation register) and M23 (strength/height in its legitimate exercise). Hupsēlofroneō (G5309) contains the huper- prefix shared with CHAR-1's huperēfanos (G5244) and CHAR-4's huperfroneō (G5252) — the huper- prefix family spans CHAR-1 (dispositional above-others appearance), CHAR-4 (cognitive above-measure thinking), and CHAR-5 (wealth-grounded above-others haughtiness). This is the most cross-characteristic vocabulary overlap in M08's Greek evidence.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The vocabulary comparison across the five reveals the cluster's two primary cross-cluster vocabulary relationships (confirmed in Observations #11 and #12). First, CHAR-3 ↔ M22: kauchaomai and ha.lal span both M08's self-directed boasting (CHAR-3 VCG-01) and M22's God-directed glorying/praise (CHAR-3 VCG-03). Second, CHAR-5 ↔ M23: ga.on, ma.rom, shal.le.tet, and archō carry their primary register in M23 (strength/power/dominion) and appear in M08 only in verses where those strength-terms evidence self-exaltation. Additionally, within M08: the g-'-h root family spans CHAR-1 (ga.on, ga.vah, ga.a.vah) and CHAR-5 (ga.on proud-might subset, ga.vah wealth-pride). The huper- prefix family spans CHAR-1 (huperēfanos), CHAR-4 (huperfroneō), and CHAR-5 (hupsēlofroneō). The cluster-synthesis: M08's vocabulary overlaps primarily with M22 (through CHAR-3) and M23 (through CHAR-5), both as confirmed observations.

CHAR-6 (na.div — freely-springing) shares semantic-domain adjacency with M04 (Joy/Delight) and M29 (Desire/Will) without root-level sharing. *Most isolated vocabulary*: CHAR-5 (semnotēs — from sebomai, reverence/worship root) is terminologically distinct from all other M09 characteristics and connects more to the godliness vocabulary (eusebeia) than to the other M09 terms. CHAR-4 (metriopatheō; okneō) is also terminologically distinct. Cluster-level: the vocabulary network of M09 has a Hebrew OT core (ka.na, dak.ka, na.div, yiq.qe.hah) connected by downward-and-freely-giving semantic domains, and a NT Greek layer (tapein-, hupo-, semnotēs, metriopatheō) that develops the OT registers into dispositional and social-ordering vocabulary. CHAR-5's vocabulary is the most distinctive — its root-connexion to reverential worship (sebomai) makes it the cluster's most theologically-embedded vocabulary.

findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The ta.me vocabulary (H2930A verb, H2931 adjective) is shared across all four M10c characteristics at the lexical level — the same Hebrew root for "defile/unclean" operates in the ritual register (Characteristic 1), the moral-inner register (Characteristic 2), the corporate-covenantal register (Characteristic 3), and can appear in the spiritual-agency context (Characteristic 4, though G0169 akathartos is the primary NT term there). The nid.dah (H5079) term appears in both Characteristic 1 (M10c-A-VCG-05 and -07) and Characteristic 3 (M10c-D sub-group — Eze 36:17, Lev 18:19) — the same term spans the bodily-ritual and the moral-corporate registers.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. The ta.me root (H2931) is shared with Characteristic 1 (Ritual defilement-state), Characteristic 3 (Corporate-covenantal defilement), and Characteristic 4 (External spiritual agency defilement) — all four M10c characteristics share the same Hebrew root. G0169 akathartos is shared between Characteristic 2 (moral-inner uses: 2Cor 6:17, Eph 5:5, Rev 16:13/17:4/18:2, VCG-03/04) and Characteristic 1 (ritual/categorical uses: Act 10:14/28, M10c-B-VCG-05) and Characteristic 4 (unclean spirits, M10c-E). The vocabulary sharing across all four characteristics using the same Greek and Hebrew root confirms a shared lexical domain.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. The ta.me root (H2930A verb, H2931 adj) is shared across all four M10c characteristics. H5079 nid.dah is shared with Characteristic 1 (ritual-bodily register of nid.dah) and appears in Characteristic 3's corporate-prophetic uses (Eze 36:17 — "like the uncleanness of a woman in her menstrual impurity"; Lam 1:17 — "a filthy thing"). The vocabulary of "abomination" (tô‛ēbāh — referenced at Jer 7:30, 2Ch 36:14, Eze 22:11 as paired with defilement in VCG-02 and -03) is shared with M10b.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. G0169 akathartos ("unclean") is shared across all four M10c characteristics. In Characteristic 1, akathartos names the person's ritual status (Act 10:14/28). In Characteristic 2, akathartos names the morally defiled inner condition (2Cor 6:17). In Characteristic 4, akathartos names the character of the external spiritual agent ("unclean spirit" — pneuma akatharton). The same Greek adjective operates across three different registers within the M10c cluster.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's vocabulary sharing is the most analytically significant lexical finding in the M10c domain: all four characteristics share G0169 akathartos (the Greek akathartos root) and three share the ta.me root (H2930A/H2931 — Hebrew; all four M10c characteristics). The akathartos/katharos root is the cluster's universal lexical anchor. H5079 nid.dah ("menstrual impurity") appears in both Characteristic 1's bodily-ritual register (Lev 12/15) and Characteristic 3's corporate-prophetic metaphorical register (Eze 36:17 — the community's conduct "like the uncleanness of a woman in her menstrual impurity"; Lam 1:17 — Jerusalem "a filthy thing"), showing the bodily-impurity paradigm functioning as the metaphorical vehicle for corporate moral repugnance. The shared vocabulary confirms the four characteristics as four registers of one unified defilement domain — the same lexical root names the same fundamental condition (defilement/uncleanness) across its bodily-ritual, moral-inner, corporate-covenantal, and external-spiritual-agent dimensions.
