findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — The distinction is one of *kind* at the volitional level: CHAR-1 and CHAR-2 are not the same act at different degrees of intensity but differ in the quality of inner engagement. CHAR-1 is the will knowingly choosing the wrong; CHAR-2 is the will acting without that knowledge. This is a difference in kind (knowing vs not knowing) rather than degree (more or less serious). Both produce moral liability (both require atonement in the cultic system), confirming that the distinction is not about moral seriousness but about the inner faculty of knowledge engaged at the moment of the act.

**[CHAR-10]** E — The distinction is one of *kind and temporal phase*: CHAR-10 names the mechanism (the process of enticement/training); CHAR-6 names the dispositional state (the formed settled sinning orientation). They are different kinds of inner-being phenomena (process vs condition) occupying different temporal positions (the mechanism produces the condition). Neither is reducible to the other: knowing the mechanism (CHAR-10) does not tell you everything about the formed condition (CHAR-6), and knowing the condition (CHAR-6) does not tell you how the mechanism operated.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The distinction is one of *scope and register*: CHAR-11 is the broadest characteristic in M10 (all persons, all registers — wickedness/debt/power); CHAR-12 focuses on the power/enslavement register specifically. The distinction is not of degree (more or less conditioned) or constitutional level (both address the deepest inner-being state) but of the *analytical scope and register*: CHAR-11 asks "what is the universal condition all persons stand in?"; CHAR-12 asks "what is the nature of sin's enslaving power specifically?"

**[CHAR-12]** E — The distinction is one of *scope and analytical register*. CHAR-11 addresses the universal bedrock condition (all persons, all registers — wickedness, debt, power); CHAR-12 focuses specifically on the enslaving-power dimension of sin as an active governing force over the will. The distinction is not of degree (more or less enslaved), constitutional level (both operate at the deepest inner-being level), or direction (both are inward-operation characteristics). It is register-scope: CHAR-12 narrows to the power-governing-force register; CHAR-11 encompasses all registers of the universal condition.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The distinction is one of *kind and subjectivity*: CHAR-13 is the objective moral fact; CHAR-17 is the subjective inner-being experience. They are different kinds of phenomena (objective account vs subjective experience) rather than different degrees of the same thing. The direction differs: CHAR-13 faces toward God (the record is before God); CHAR-17 faces toward the person's own inner awareness (guilt is the person's inner experience of what is before God).

**[CHAR-14]** E — The distinction is one of *scope*: CHAR-3 is the verbal-acknowledgment component; CHAR-14 is the full seeking-and-receiving transaction. CHAR-3 names one element of the seeking; CHAR-14 names the complete event including recognition, seeking, mediation, divine response, and consequent transformation. The direction is the same (human toward God); the constitutional level is the same (will and conscience); but the scope differs: CHAR-3 ⊂ CHAR-14 (CHAR-3 is contained within CHAR-14 as one of its components).

**[CHAR-15]** E — The distinction is one of *kind and mechanism*: CHAR-11 is the ontological condition (structural, universal, without requiring a specific lineage); CHAR-15 is the transmission mechanism (genealogical-communal, historically specific, requiring ancestral belonging). They are different kinds of sin-condition: CHAR-11 is constitutional-structural; CHAR-15 is historical-relational. They operate at the same constitutional level (the whole person's standing before God) but through different mechanisms.

**[CHAR-16]** E — The distinction is one of *level and mode of description*: CHAR-11 describes the ontological structural level (condition all persons stand in); CHAR-16 describes the characterological identity level (what the person has become or is recognised as through that condition). Both operate at the same constitutional level (the whole person's moral standing) but CHAR-11 is condition-language and CHAR-16 is identity/character-language. The distinction is between condition (CHAR-11) and constituted character-type (CHAR-16).

**[CHAR-17]** E — The distinction is one of *direction and subjectivity*: CHAR-13 faces toward God (the record is held in divine memory before God); CHAR-17 faces toward the person (the guilt-state is experienced in human conscience). They are the same moral reality seen from different directions — divine-record-side (CHAR-13) and human-experience-side (CHAR-17). The distinction is directional rather than one of degree (both engage the same moral weight) or constitutional level (both operate at the whole-person level of moral standing).

**[CHAR-18]** E — The distinction is one of *content vs. container*: CHAR-13 is the divine-record system (the "kept in store" mechanism, the divine memory that holds all moral failures); CHAR-18 is the specific crime-content (the a.von H5771G accumulation) that is the primary content of that record. The distinction is not one of degree (both address the full weight of moral accumulation) but of level: CHAR-13 is at the system level (how God holds moral accounts); CHAR-18 is at the content level (what the primary moral-crime content is that the system holds).

**[CHAR-19]** E — The distinction is one of *kind with directional specification*: CHAR-1 is the genus (wilful sinning act — missing the mark); CHAR-19 is a species (the specific kind of wilful sinning that constitutes a known boundary-crossing/rebellion). CHAR-19 adds the relational-boundary-violation dimension to what CHAR-1 names as the act. The knowing-defiance of CHAR-19 is a kind-distinction from CHAR-1's act-of-missing (which can be less relationally oriented) — not merely a more severe instance of the same thing.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The distinction is one of *kind* at the inner-being level: not more sinning vs less sinning (degree), not sinning in a different direction, not sinning at a different constitutional depth — but sinning with a fundamentally different inner-quality of the will and conscience at the moment of the act. The knowing will (CHAR-1) and the unknowing will (CHAR-2) are qualitatively different inner states. Both produce real moral liability (both require atonement); the system differentiates them in the prescribed remedy's scale (CHAR-1 may require more costly offering in the cultic corpus) but not in whether a remedy is required.

**[CHAR-20]** E — The distinction is one of *relational depth and prior-bond requirement*: CHAR-19 is the boundary-crossing category (can operate without prior intimate bond — the Amos nations); CHAR-20 is the covenant-betrayal category (constitutively requires a prior covenant relationship). The distinction is thus not of degree (one more serious than another) or constitutional level (both operate at will and spirit-levels) but of the *type of relational context* that gives the sin its specific character: boundary (CHAR-19) versus bond (CHAR-20).

**[CHAR-21]** E — The distinction is one of *focus and level*: CHAR-18 focuses on the accumulated moral-crime account (objective, juridical, before God); CHAR-21 focuses on the inner moral-faculty distortion (subjective, constitutional, the bent inner instrument). They operate at different analytic levels of the same moral failure: CHAR-18 at the juridical-record level; CHAR-21 at the constitutional-faculty level. The perverted heart (CHAR-21) is what generates the iniquity-record (CHAR-18).

**[CHAR-22]** E — The distinction is one of *direction*: CHAR-21 is primarily *inward* (the twisted inner constitution); CHAR-22 is primarily *other-directed* (the unjust conduct toward persons). Both operate at the heart/will level, but CHAR-21's defining orientation is the inner distortion of the moral faculty itself, while CHAR-22's defining orientation is the harm done to others through that distorted faculty's expression. The same perverted heart (CHAR-21 — Pro 6:14) produces the hands that deal violence (CHAR-22 — Psa 58:2) — the distinction is directional.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The distinction between CHAR-3 (Confession) and CHAR-17 (Guilt) is one of *kind* — not more or less of the same thing, but two different events: an inner state (guilt) and an outer speech-act (confession). They are related causally (guilt produces confession) but are qualitatively different events. The distinction between genuine confession (VCG-01/02) and hollow confession (VCG-03) is one of *degree and constitutional depth*: both produce the verbal form; genuine confession additionally produces the volitional reorientation.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The distinction between CHAR-4 and CHAR-5 is one of *kind* at the conscience level: in CHAR-4 the conscience does not register (or the registration is denied); in CHAR-5 the conscience has registered and the will refuses to respond. Both involve unaddressed sin, but the inner-being mechanism is different in kind — one is a conscience failure, the other is a will-refusal. The distinction between CHAR-4's modes (active denial vs perceptual blindness vs habituated absence) is a distinction of *degree and mechanism* within the characteristic.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The distinction between CHAR-5 (Refusal to repent) and CHAR-6 (Habitual defection) is one of *kind* — they are not the same phenomenon at different intensities but different aspects of a related inner-being reality: one is a volitional commitment (CHAR-5), the other is a formed dispositional pattern (CHAR-6). The distinction between CHAR-5 and CHAR-4 (Conscience suppression) is one of *kind* at the conscience-registration node: CHAR-4 = conscience not registering; CHAR-5 = conscience registers (or knowledge is present) but will overrides.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The distinction between CHAR-6 (Habitual defection) and CHAR-5 (Refusal to repent) is one of *kind* at the will-level: CHAR-5 is the will in its decision-mode (choosing not to turn); CHAR-6 is the will in its formation-mode (shaped by accumulated choices into a default direction). They share the sinning-direction but are qualitatively different modes of the will. The distinction between CHAR-6 and CHAR-16 (Sinner as moral character) is one of *degree and formation stage*: CHAR-6 is the process; CHAR-16 is the constituted endpoint identity.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The distinction between CHAR-7 (Contagious sin) and CHAR-5 (Refusal to repent) is one of *direction and relational scope*: CHAR-5 is self-directed (the leader's own volitional non-departure); CHAR-7 is other-directed (the leader's causative transmission to the community). The distinction is also grammatically marked: CHAR-5 uses the Qal personal sinning form; CHAR-7 uses the Hiphil causative. The distinction is not of degree (more or less refusal) but of the fundamental directional orientation of the characteristic: inward vs outward through authority.

**[CHAR-8]** E — The distinction is one of *direction and domain*: both characteristics involve the same wilful breaking-away dynamic (same root) but applied in different relational directions and domains (political-authority vs personal-moral-covenantal). The direction of the breaking differs: CHAR-8 breaks upward (subordinate breaking from governing authority); CHAR-19 breaks outward (person breaking from moral-covenantal constraint). Neither is a matter of degree (one being more or less than the other) but of distinct relational domains.

**[CHAR-9]** E — The distinction is one of *kind and form*: CHAR-1 is the wilful moral act as a category; CHAR-9 is that category specifically and exclusively in its speech-form. The distinction is not of degree (more or less sinful) but of the constitutive form: CHAR-9 requires the spoken word as its essential medium, which CHAR-1 does not require. The speech-form is constitutive, not merely coincidental.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The distinction is primarily one of kind: CHAR-1 is a person-type characteristic (who the person is), while M10b-E is an activity-type characteristic (what the inner person generates). They address different analytical questions about the same inner reality. The distinction is not of degree (one is not more or less wicked than the other) or constitutional level (both operate at the same heart/soul/mind level) or direction (both are outwardly oriented in their consequences). It is a categorical distinction between identity and activity as analytical frames for the same inner-being domain.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The distinction is primarily one of kind and constitutional level. Kind: CHAR-1 is a person-identity category (the wicked person as a type), while CHAR-2 is a structural-condition category (the evil constitutional nature as the condition from which the person-identity flows). Constitutional level: CHAR-1 operates at the level of the settled will and its directional orientation; CHAR-2 operates at the deeper constitutional level of the generative inner architecture that precedes and shapes the will's options. The distinction is not of degree (more or less wicked) or direction (different moral directions) but of analytical depth: CHAR-2 describes the constitutional condition; CHAR-1 describes the settled orientation that the condition makes probable.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The distinction from CHAR-4 is one of kind: different contents of what is found abominable (moral character corruption vs. idolatrous allegiance), not different degrees or constitutional levels of the same content. Both CHAR-3 and CHAR-4 operate at the same constitutional level (the inner person's character and allegiance before God) and both involve the same divine-revulsion response mechanism — what differs is the object of the divine revulsion. The distinction from CHAR-1 is one of direction and perspective: CHAR-1 describes wickedness from the human-inner side (the settled orientation of the will away from God); CHAR-3 describes the same reality from the divine-relational side (the verdict of revulsion on that orientation).

**[CHAR-4]** E — The distinction from CHAR-3 is one of kind: different contents of what is abominable (idolatrous devotion vs. moral-character corruption), not different degrees of abomination. Both operate at the same constitutional level (inner person before God) and both involve the same divine-revulsion mechanism. What differs is the object that triggers the divine revulsion: misdirected devotion to idols (CHAR-4) vs. morally corrupt inner character (CHAR-3). The distinction is categorical/kind, not gradational/degree, directional, or level-based.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The distinction is one of kind: different aspects of the same moral domain (wickedness/evil) are named. CHAR-1 names the settled dispositional identity; CHAR-5 names the active generative process. Both operate at the same constitutional level (inner person before God) and in the same moral domain. The distinction is not gradational (CHAR-5 is not more evil than CHAR-1 or vice versa) nor directional (both involve inner-to-outer movement) nor level-based (both are at the inner constitutional level). It is a categorical distinction between what the person is (CHAR-1) and what the person's inner life does (CHAR-5).

**[CHAR-6]** E — The distinction from M06 is one of analytical angle (not degree, kind, or level): same speech-contempt phenomenon analysed from the inner-expression angle (CHAR-6) versus the relational-act angle (M06). The distinction from CHAR-1 is one of mode: CHAR-1 names the inner identity; CHAR-6 names one specific expressive mode of that identity (through speech). This is a mode-distinction rather than degree, kind, or level — the same inner wickedness can be named as settled identity (CHAR-1) or as speech-expression (CHAR-6); both are correct from their respective analytical angles.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's internal distinctions are uniformly categorical/kind distinctions rather than degree, direction, or level distinctions. Char 1 vs. Char 5: identity vs. activity (kind). Char 3 vs. Char 4: moral-character content vs. idolatrous-devotion content (kind). Char 1 vs. Char 2: directional-orientation vs. constitutional-structure (analytical level). Char 6 vs. M06: inner-expression angle vs. relational-act angle (analytical angle/kind). The cluster reveals that its six characteristics are not more-or-less versions of the same thing but genuinely distinct analytical entries into the same domain of inner evil — each addressing a different dimension of the same moral-theological reality.

findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — The distinction is primarily of kind and constitutional level. The kind distinction: ritual defilement (Characteristic 1) is a legal/sacral condition arising from bodily mechanism; moral-inner defilement (Characteristic 2) is a condition of the inner person arising from within. The constitutional level distinction: Characteristic 1 is primarily a condition of the embodied person at the level of bodily function and sacral status; Characteristic 2 penetrates to the spirit level (2Cor 7:1: "defilement of body and spirit"). The distinction is not merely of degree (more or less severe defilement) but of a different kind of condition at a deeper constitutional level.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The distinction is primarily of kind and constitutional level. Kind: Characteristic 1 is a legally-defined bodily-mechanism condition; Characteristic 2 is a morally-defined inner-volitional condition. Constitutional level: Characteristic 1 operates at the bodily-mechanism and social-sacral level; Characteristic 2 penetrates to the spirit level (2Cor 7:1 — "defilement of body and spirit") and operates primarily at the soul level of conscience, will, heart, and desire. Characteristic 2 is constitutionally deeper than Characteristic 1.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The distinction is primarily of direction and scope. Kind: both are defilement-state conditions. Constitutional level: Characteristic 2 penetrates to the spirit level (2Cor 7:1); Characteristic 3 operates at the soul level (will, desire, heart allegiance) and extends outward to the corporate-covenantal domain (land, sanctuary, name) — not inward toward the spirit level. Direction: Characteristic 2 moves inward (from desire to the deepest constitutional level); Characteristic 3 moves outward (from the community's inner will to the sacred spatial and relational environment). Scope: Characteristic 2 is individual; Characteristic 3 is corporate.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The distinction is primarily of kind and constitutional level. Kind: the defiling agent is categorically different — material/impersonal (Characteristic 1) vs spiritual/personal/adversarial (Characteristic 4). Constitutional level: Characteristic 1 operates at the bodily-mechanism and social-sacral level; Characteristic 4 operates at the spirit level (the deepest constitutional level), which is why the domination is more comprehensive and the resolution requires divine command rather than ritual remedy.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's distinctions across nearest-neighbour pairs are consistently of kind and constitutional level — not of degree. Chars 1-2: kind (bodily-ritual vs moral-inner) and constitutional level (Char 1 operates at the bodily/social-sacral level; Char 2 penetrates to the spirit level — 2Cor 7:1). Chars 2-3: direction and scope (Char 2 individual-internal; Char 3 corporate-extending outward) — not of kind (both are moral-volitional conditions). Chars 1-4: kind (impersonal-material vs personal-spiritual-adversarial) and constitutional level (Char 1 operates bodily-sacral; Char 4 operates at the spirit level directly). The cluster's unanimous finding: the four characteristics are not more-or-less of the same thing — each is a different kind of defilement-condition at a different constitutional level or with a different directionality. The M10c cluster contains four categorically distinct defilement conditions, not four points on a single defilement scale.

findings.finding_value: **[CHAR-1]** E — Not applicable; distinction work is required and evidenced above.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The nearest neighbour distinction with CHAR-1: CHAR-2 is the outer-mechanism; CHAR-1 is the inner-experience. The distinction is of kind (mechanism vs. experience). CHAR-2 is also distinct from CHAR-5 (contempt producing shame): CHAR-5's mechanism is specifically contempt/dismissal; CHAR-2's mechanism is enforced downward movement (which can be produced by contempt but also by military defeat, divine judgment, natural loss).

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — CHAR-3 is most closely related to CHAR-5 (shame produced by contempt): both involve the treatment of persons as of diminished worth. The distinction: CHAR-3 names the relational verdict (worth-denial as the act and its structural effect); CHAR-5 names the specific mechanism (contempt/dismissal as the producing agent and its received shame as the specific outcome in the recipient). CHAR-3 is broader — worth-denial can be produced by contempt (CHAR-5), by structural assignment (VCG-02), or by hypocrisy and favoritism (VCG-01) without being contempt in the strict sense.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 is most closely related to CHAR-1 in its moral-consequence register (M07-B — shame as the consequence of moral failure). The distinction: CHAR-1-M07-B is about shame as the experience that follows moral failure; CHAR-4 is about the conscience's recognition of what is shameful as a quality of conduct or desire. CHAR-4 is the evaluative faculty; CHAR-1-M07-B is the experiential consequence. They frequently occur together: the same act that CHAR-4 identifies as shameful produces CHAR-1's shame-experience in the person who commits it.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 is most closely related to CHAR-3 (dishonour as relational worth-denial) and to M06 (contempt as the producing mechanism). The distinction between CHAR-5 and CHAR-3: CHAR-5 names the specific mechanism (contempt as the producing force) and the received shame as the specific outcome; CHAR-3 names the relational verdict of worth-denial more broadly (which can arise from causes other than contempt). The distinction between CHAR-5 and M06: M06 holds the contempt-projection (the contempt-er's inner act); CHAR-5 holds the contempt-received shame (the recipient's inner experience). CHAR-5 and M06 are relational complements — they are the two faces of the same contempt-shame dynamic.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 is most closely related to M12 (purity/holiness) through shared vocabulary, but the analytical distinction is clear: M12 holds the purity/holiness register of niq.qa.von and qe.ha.von as the primary meaning of these terms; CHAR-6 holds the innocence-as-counter-to-shame function of the same terms in every verse of the 8-verse corpus. The distinction is one of purpose and register: M12 = moral and ritual purity as the characteristic; CHAR-6 = innocence as specifically the protection against and structural counter to shame.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The most important cluster-level distinctions: (1) Experience vs mechanism (Chars 1 vs 2) — the felt shame vs the enforced abasement are analytically distinct even when co-occurring. (2) Specific contempt vs broad dishonour (Chars 5 vs 3) — contempt as zero-worth-assignment is a subset of relational worth-denial. (3) Evaluative quality vs experienced state (Chars 4 vs 1) — what the conscience names as shameful vs what the person experiences as shame. (4) Protective positive condition vs the shame-states it counters (Char 6 vs Chars 1-5) — the one positive characteristic in the cluster vs the five naming shame's forms. These distinctions are the programme's analytical achievement in M07: a field experienced by the ordinary reader as a single phenomenon (shame) has been analytically differentiated into six genuinely distinct characteristics. The distinctness is not imposed but demonstrated by verse-evidence: different verses name different dimensions with different vocabulary in different relational contexts.

---
